goals.origin: The 3/6/9 selections were incorrectly treated as a fixed number of exposures.
goals.required_behavior: The shutter may remain held and 3/6/9 mean target frames per second, never total frames per press.
required_evidence: UI labels and values encode fps
capture state retains stock continuous-until-release exposure logic
no fixed-exposure-count hook or guard exists
goals.title: Continuous-rate semantics

goals.origin: Earlier builds put controls in the wrong menu or left the official UI unchanged.
goals.required_behavior: Selecting Continuous in the official Drive Mode popover exposes one native-style selector with exactly 16-bit 3fps, 14-bit 3fps, 14-bit 6fps, and 14-bit 9fps.
required_evidence: compiled QML round-trip
runtime right-panel model inspection
touch selection reaches the intended backend property
goals.title: Correct native UI path

goals.origin: Separate asynchronous bit-depth and rate settings could race or describe a mode that was not active.
goals.required_behavior: Each of the four UI values atomically selects its matching bit depth and rate and survives restart without cross-mode contamination.
required_evidence: exhaustive setter/getter state matrix
restart persistence harness
live read-back equals selected preset
goals.title: Atomic preset selection and persistence

goals.origin: v8 forced electronic shutter for 14-bit 6/9fps instead of extending the native lens-shutter chain.
goals.required_behavior: All four presets use the lens shutter command, acknowledgement, exposure, close/reset, sensor readout, and re-arm path; no preset forces or silently selects electronic shutter.
required_evidence: no electronic-shutter override in binary diff
lens command/ack trace for every exposure
electronic-shutter property remains unchanged in live tests
goals.title: Native lens/leaf-shutter capture chain

goals.origin: The sensor does not provide full-frame ultra-high-rate 16-bit readout.
goals.required_behavior: 16-bit is offered only as the approximately 2.7fps product path labelled 3fps; 6/9fps are 14-bit only.
required_evidence: sensor mode table audit
preset-to-mode routing matrix
captured 3FR bit-depth metadata
goals.title: 16-bit sensor limit respected

goals.origin: The installed original v8 produced heavy live-view noise and logged DEWARP timeout plus ION memory import failure.
goals.required_behavior: Preview uses a format-compatible buffer topology with no new corruption, timeout, memory-import failure, or persistent noise.
required_evidence: official-versus-candidate preview topology audit
buffer format/stride/capacity verification
live preview log and image comparison
goals.title: Preview integrity and noise regression

goals.origin: Installed v8 showed an async DSP output with zero enqueues and one dequeue during teardown.
goals.required_behavior: DMA, DSP, preview, JLS, and writer buffers have per-frame ownership and balanced enqueue/dequeue/return counts.
required_evidence: state-machine or emulation ownership matrix
no overwrite of in-flight frame context
live queue counters balance after burst and teardown
goals.title: Buffer ownership and queue balance

goals.origin: v8 could actuate capture but produced no stored image and remained busy.
goals.required_behavior: For every accepted exposure, DMA, DSP, JLS, 3FR open/write/close, pending-save decrement, and buffer return all complete exactly once.
required_evidence: counter equality across every pipeline stage
valid 3FR files for single and sustained continuous tests
camera returns to ready state without error 20 or permanent writing indicator
goals.title: Complete RAW-to-3FR storage transaction

goals.origin: A prior relocated QML unit caused the entire overlay UI and controls to disappear.
goals.required_behavior: All stock UI remains visible and responsive and only the intended Continuous right-panel content changes.
required_evidence: QML loader/runtime path audit
full control-screen interaction harness
live button/touch regression sweep
goals.title: No compiled-QML relocation UI loss

goals.origin: Earlier diagnosis reasoned about v2/v3/v6/v8 without first proving which build was active.
goals.required_behavior: Every live result is tied to active slot and exact hashes of camera-service, camera-gui, sensor configuration, and package manifest.
required_evidence: active-slot read-back
live component SHA-256 values
exact match to the candidate manifest before and after testing
goals.title: Exact running-version attribution

goals.origin: Multiple incomplete generations were sent to the camera and shifted avoidable debugging cost to live testing.
goals.required_behavior: No CIM or installer is emitted until UI, backend, persistence, shutter, sensor, processing, storage, rollback, and live read-only gates all pass for the same hashes.
required_evidence: all-gates aggregate report
local-only marker while any gate is incomplete
package generation hard-fails on any non-PASS status
goals.title: No half-build release

goals.origin: The first v8 export contained identity and hashes but its unfiltered logcat stream ended before the latest failed capture; the rollback gate would have accepted that incomplete bundle.
goals.required_behavior: Before leaving a failed camera build, preserve identity, exact hashes, active-slot state, recent and capture-filtered logcat, kernel log, runtime/configuration state, storage file index, log index, and tombstone index on the PC.
required_evidence: all required artifacts are non-empty and SHA-256 recorded
recent capture-filtered logs include the failure window or explicitly record that the camera produced no matching events
rollback controller hard-fails when any required artifact is absent
goals.title: Complete pre-rollback failure evidence

goals.origin: Unbounded logcat and kernel-log exports saturated the factory TCP diagnostic tunnel and the camera disappeared from USB before the evidence bundle completed.
goals.required_behavior: Live diagnostic commands filter on-camera, cap output size, emit an explicit end marker, and capture identity/slot/hash evidence before larger streams so a transport reset cannot corrupt attribution.
required_evidence: every large preset has a finite line cap and explicit end marker
transport-size and command-length audit passes
all local files are non-empty and contain their expected completion marker where applicable
goals.title: Bounded live diagnostic export

goals.origin: The blackbox UNRD dump prints key plus value, while a live single-key UNRD query returns only the bare numeric value; the first rollback preflight assumed the dump format.
goals.required_behavior: Slot-state parsing accepts both verified formats, rejects all other output, and never reaches a slot write when parsing is ambiguous.
required_evidence: unit tests cover bare-value and key-value formats
malformed output test fails closed
live preflight reads all six slot flags before any write
goals.title: Live UNRD output parsing

goals.origin: DEWARP timeout, ION import failure, and buffer-return warnings at 11:18 were initially attributed to v8 capture, but their full context shows they occurred while USB connection forced live-view teardown under E_ErrorCode_UsbConnected.
goals.required_behavior: A runtime error may be attributed to capture only when its time window contains a real shutter/capture request and is not a USB, mode-switch, shutdown, or topology-destruction transition.
required_evidence: event timeline includes trigger, camera state, stream state, and error category
USB and topology teardown windows are excluded from capture-causality counts
root-cause report labels correlation separately from proven causation
goals.title: Separate USB transition artifacts from capture failures

goals.origin: Switching back to the official system slot left v8-era /data settings debug_mode=1 and E_DebugOption_EnableFastCaptureWithSlowBurst, while the recorded official baseline is debug_mode=false and E_DebugOption_None(0).
goals.required_behavior: An official rollback restores or explicitly verifies all modified persistent /data settings in addition to system-slot binaries.
required_evidence: pre-change persistent settings backup
official baseline comparison
post-rollback live read-back shows debug mode false and debug option none
goals.title: Rollback restores persistent runtime settings

goals.origin: The withdrawn v8r3 electronic-shutter design continued to be described as a current candidate with a 34/34 PASS suite after the requirement had been corrected to continuous 3/6/9 fps through the native leaf-shutter path.
goals.required_behavior: A test result may count toward release only when its asserted UI semantics, frame-rate semantics, bit-depth rules, and shutter path exactly match the current user requirement; obsolete suites remain historical evidence and can never be carried forward as release evidence.
required_evidence: machine-readable requirement contract hash recorded beside every test report
test assertions explicitly cover continuous fps semantics and reject fixed-count or electronic-shutter substitutions
aggregate release gate excludes every report whose requirement contract hash differs from the candidate
goals.title: Test evidence is bound to the current requirement

goals.origin: The R1 slot-overlay attempt locked the camera and then failed on a stale or unavailable host endpoint with WinError 10049; no camera write occurred, while its offline simulation had been mistaken for live readiness.
goals.required_behavior: Before any camera lock, mount, upload, slot write, or reboot, the installer must discover and bind the currently present camera transport, complete a bounded read-only handshake, and prove that cleanup can restore a known state. Cleanup is idempotent, and any ambiguous endpoint or cleanup result fails closed before a write.
required_evidence: live transport interface and endpoint are discovered rather than assumed
bounded read-only handshake succeeds before camera lock or mount
fault-injection tests cover endpoint loss before and after lock
cleanup can be repeated safely and leaves no stale lock, mount, or slot state
offline simulation is explicitly marked device_tested false and cannot satisfy a live release gate
goals.title: Bounded transport preflight and idempotent cleanup

goals.origin: Earlier candidates treated the IMX861 6fps and 9fps readout modes as proof that the complete XCD leaf-shutter capture chain could sustain the same rates, even though a live candidate remained near 2.8fps.
goals.required_behavior: A 3fps, 6fps, or 9fps label is enabled only when the native lens-shutter command, acknowledgement, exposure, close/reset, sensor readout, re-arm, RAW processing, and file-close chain sustains that measured cadence while the shutter is held. Sensor mode rate alone is never accepted as whole-camera burst performance.
required_evidence: per-frame lens command, acknowledgement, exposure, close/reset, and re-arm timestamps
electronic shutter remains disabled and unchanged for every preset
accepted exposure, RAW completion, JLS completion, 3FR close, and buffer-return counts remain equal
sustained measured cadence and jitter are reported for each lens and preset rather than copied from the sensor mode table
continuous-charge capability and minimum safe leaf-shutter cycle are characterized before exposing 6fps or 9fps in the UI
goals.title: Leaf-shutter cadence is measured, not inferred from sensor fps

goals.origin: The saved XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 log reports Charge during readout: Yes but Has shutter continuous charge: No. Those are distinct capabilities, and ignoring the latter could overrun the physical leaf-shutter recharge cycle.
goals.required_behavior: The effective burst rate is negotiated against the exact attached lens and firmware. A lens that reports no continuous shutter charge is never driven as though it reports yes, and an unsupported 6fps or 9fps leaf-shutter request is rejected or disabled rather than silently falling back, switching shutter type, or overstressing the mechanism.
required_evidence: exact lens product, firmware, and relevant capability bits are captured before the burst session
Charge during readout and shutter continuous charge are parsed and tested as separate flags
supported and unsupported lens-capability matrices are covered by behavioral tests
live command traces prove no command is issued before the lens is ready to re-arm
UI and metadata report the effective rate honestly when the requested rate is unavailable
goals.title: Attached-lens shutter capability is enforced fail-closed

goals.origin: The SlowBurst debug option and FastCaptureAllowed predicate were previously treated as if enabling them created 6fps or 9fps. Static state-machine analysis shows they only select a fast full-press or session-entry transition and do not add a per-frame repeat scheduler.
goals.required_behavior: FastCaptureAllowed may affect first-shot readiness only. No burst rate is enabled or claimed unless an explicit repeated-exposure state path and measured whole-chain cadence exist independently of this readiness bit.
required_evidence: binary and state-machine audit separates first-shot entry from inter-frame repeat transitions
tests prove that toggling the debug option cannot satisfy a 3fps, 6fps, or 9fps cadence gate by itself
live traces report first-shot latency separately from steady-state frame intervals
no release gate accepts FastCaptureAllowed as evidence of repeated leaf-shutter operation
goals.title: Fast-capture readiness is not sustained burst cadence

goals.origin: The official 14-bit HS log records EXMCU leaf-shutter sequences of 274ms, 274ms, and 275ms while physical FSync intervals are 334ms and 338ms. Removing the roughly 64ms session and live-view gap alone can approach only about 3.65fps, not 6fps or 9fps.
goals.required_behavior: Any 6fps or 9fps implementation must demonstrate a safe redesigned overlap and re-arm schedule that shortens measured FSync-to-FSync cadence. Bypassing only session teardown or live-view restart is never accepted as sufficient.
required_evidence: EXMCU phase timestamps cover prep, lens acknowledgement, FSync, close or reset, transfer, restore, idle, and sequence completion
an overlap diagram identifies every shortened dependency and proves that the attached lens reports support for it
fault tests reject a new exposure before sensor, buffer, or lens readiness
sustained whole-chain cadence passes with equal accepted, RAW, JLS, 3FR-close, and buffer-return counts
goals.title: Native exposure-sequence duration bounds burst claims

goals.origin: The official preStartExposure path copies the captured lens charge-during-readout flag into its exposure state, and the restore handler skips the separate post-transfer charge request when that flag is true. XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 reports this capability as enabled, so it is already represented in the measured 274ms to 275ms baseline.
goals.required_behavior: Performance estimates must distinguish charge during readout from continuous shutter charge and must use the actually active stock capability set as their baseline. An already-active overlap cannot be subtracted again or presented as new headroom.
required_evidence: exact EXMCU function and binary hash bind the charge-during-readout state assignment
restore-handler control flow proves when the separate charge request is skipped
live lens identity and both charge capability flags are captured together
every claimed improvement is based on a newly measured FSync interval rather than duplicated phase subtraction
goals.title: Already-active charge-during-readout is not counted twice

goals.origin: The shared DecompileAt helper silently retried a missing address at address plus 0x100000, which misattributed several XCD 35-100E targets to unrelated functions in another region.
goals.required_behavior: Every reverse-analysis address is resolved only at the requested address. Any relocation or rebase adjustment must be explicit, recorded, and independently verified; a missing function remains NOT_FOUND.
required_evidence: analysis helper contains no implicit address offset fallback
known missing lens addresses remain NOT_FOUND instead of aliasing another function
all function-level conclusions record exact image base, requested address, and resolved entry
candidate evidence is regenerated after any address-resolution correction
goals.title: Reverse-analysis addresses resolve exactly

goals.origin: The first seeded XCD 35-100E Ghidra import stopped at an alternate Thumb entry inside an already-created function, so all later task and diagnostic handlers were left unseeded even though the overall import reported success.
goals.required_behavior: Function-pointer discovery records an overlapping or alternate entry and continues through the complete candidate list. A single overlap may not abort discovery or silently reduce analysis coverage.
required_evidence: seed report contains one outcome for every requested Thumb target
contained alternate entries are identified by their exact containing function
the script completes without an overlapping-function exception
post-seed analysis coverage and target string references are regenerated
goals.title: Function-pointer discovery survives overlapping entries

goals.origin: An aligned odd-word sweep treated 0x60023a00 as a Thumb function target, but that address is a literal-data region and the real nearby function begins at the 0x60023a20 push prologue. Seeding the false target polluted later control-flow analysis.
goals.required_behavior: A word whose low bit resembles a Thumb pointer is only a candidate. It becomes function evidence only after instruction-boundary, executable-region, prologue or incoming-control-flow, and surrounding table-context checks pass. Any project seeded from a rejected candidate is discarded and regenerated cleanly.
required_evidence: every manually seeded function records the source reference and exact decoded entry bytes
literal pools and compact ROPI string offsets are excluded from function-pointer results
known false target 0x60023a00 is rejected while 0x60023a20 is decoded as the nearby function start
function-level conclusions come from a clean project with no rejected seeds
goals.title: Thumb-like data words are not assumed to be functions

goals.origin: The first 1181-entry Thumb-prologue sweep exceeded the Windows batch command-line limit before Ghidra started, so no candidate was processed despite the target list being valid.
goals.required_behavior: Large reverse-analysis target sets are passed through a UTF-8 response file with an explicit requested-entry count. Command-line truncation or launch failure cannot silently reduce coverage.
required_evidence: candidate generator has unit-tested address and instruction-pattern bounds
Ghidra seed report records the complete requested-entry count
one terminal outcome is present for every response-file entry
a failed process launch produces no coverage claim
goals.title: Large analysis target sets use bounded response files

goals.origin: XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 contains an Exposure_Burst_shooting shell command, but function-level analysis shows that it loops two shutter diagnostic commands and delays; it does not enter the production LensExpRequest 0x31, LensExpReply 0x32, sensor-capture, RAW-processing, or file-close path.
goals.required_behavior: A lens diagnostic actuator loop may be used only to characterize shutter mechanics. It cannot satisfy or support a 3fps, 6fps, or 9fps camera-performance claim unless the same cadence is independently measured through the complete production lens, sensor, RAW, JLS, 3FR, and buffer-return transaction.
required_evidence: the diagnostic command descriptor, handler, arguments, loops, and delay calls are resolved from the exact lens binary
the production 0x31 request registration and 0x32 reply path are resolved separately
tests reject diagnostic shutter-cycle counts as captured-frame or stored-file counts
release evidence uses whole-camera FSync and file-close cadence rather than diagnostic shell timing
goals.title: Lens diagnostic burst is not production-capture proof

goals.origin: The exploratory prologue sweep began the Exposure_Burst_shooting handler at 0x600436da and lost its leading argc comparison, producing an in_ZR artifact. The command descriptor identifies the Thumb pointer 0x600436d9, whose exact function entry is 0x600436d8 and whose first instruction enforces param_1 == 6.
goals.required_behavior: When a verified descriptor or function-pointer table provides a Thumb entry, analysis starts at the pointer with bit zero cleared. A later prologue-like address may not replace it, truncate its leading guard, or supply semantic evidence.
required_evidence: the descriptor offset, ROPI base, odd Thumb pointer, and even function entry are recorded together
clean-project disassembly begins at 0x600436d8 and retains the six-argument guard
the truncated 0x600436da exploratory interpretation is rejected as semantic evidence
function-level reports bind requested and resolved entries exactly
goals.title: Descriptor-derived Thumb entries retain their first instruction

goals.origin: The EXMCU network log prints packet bytes in hexadecimal. Treating LensExpRequest tokens 11, 13, 17, and 12 as decimal obscured their real values 0x11, 0x13, 0x17, and 0x12 and therefore their low-nibble dispatch cases 1, 3, 7, and 2.
goals.required_behavior: All lens request and reply fields taken from packet hex dumps are parsed as base-16 bytes. The complete byte, its flag bits, and its low-nibble dispatch case are retained; display formatting may not silently convert the token to decimal semantics.
required_evidence: the bounded stock trace reproduces three exact 0x11 to 0x13 to 0x17 to 0x12 sequences
each command maps to the verified low-nibble switch case and callback-table entry
unit tests fail if packet tokens are parsed with base 10
request-to-reply timing is grouped by the full hexadecimal command byte
goals.title: Lens protocol trace bytes are parsed as hexadecimal

goals.origin: The official EXMCU request builder translates internal operation enums into low-nibble lens commands before applying the sync-mode high nibble. Without binding both layers, a call-site enum can be confused with the transmitted byte or mapped to the wrong production callback.
goals.required_behavior: Every leaf-shutter schedule change preserves an exact, hash-bound mapping from EXMCU operation enum through sync-mode packet encoding to the lens 0x31 request, low-nibble dispatch case, verified lens callback, and observed production role.
required_evidence: the official EXMCU request builder proves operation 3, 5, 7, 0, and 8 encode low-nibble commands 1, 3, 7, 2, and 8
sync mode 1 is shown to produce packets 0x11, 0x13, 0x17, 0x12, and 0x18
prestart, exposure, charge-during-readout, restore, and completion call sites are bound to exact functions and binary hash
the bounded stock trace reproduces the mapped 0x11 to 0x13 to 0x17 to 0x12 production sequence
goals.title: EXMCU operation enums map exactly to production lens packets

goals.origin: In the successful stock trace, the 0x17 lens reply arrives 104ms to 106ms before sensor transfer completes, and the final 0x12 reply arrives 36ms before ExposureSequence Done and 99ms to 102ms before the next prep request. Treating a lens acknowledgement as permission to reuse the frame context would race the sensor, restore, RAW, or storage path.
goals.required_behavior: A repeated-exposure scheduler may advance or reuse a frame resource only after its separately tracked lens, sensor-transfer, restore, RAW, JLS, 3FR-close, and buffer-return dependencies are complete. No individual lens reply may stand in for whole-frame or next-frame readiness.
required_evidence: bounded stock timing records request, reply, transfer, idle, sequence-done, and next-prep timestamps independently
tests reject scheduling from either the 0x17 or 0x12 reply alone
each in-flight frame has an immutable frame id and separate readiness flags for every downstream owner
fault injection delays or drops each completion independently without overwriting, leaking, or closing the wrong frame
accepted exposure, RAW, JLS, 3FR-close, and buffer-return counts remain equal throughout sustained capture
goals.title: Lens reply is not whole-frame or next-frame readiness

goals.origin: The stock camera-service already maintains a QMap keyed by ExposureId with independent CaptureRequestInfo objects and completion flags. The earlier model that v8 failed because stock lacked all multi-frame identity infrastructure was wrong; replacing this graph with a global current-capture context would create the frame and metadata mismatches seen in failed builds.
goals.required_behavior: Every burst implementation preserves an immutable ExposureId and item-specific CaptureRequestInfo ownership chain from result arrival through storage acknowledgement, request cleanup, capture reporting, and buffer return. No global current frame, shared mutable metadata record, or inferred callback order may replace it.
required_evidence: exact camera-service hash and symbol-level analysis bind processExposureItems, CaptureRequestInfo::setDone, the storage completion callback, and checkExposureRequestDone
every in-flight frame retains independent RAW, preview, metadata, storage result, and completion state
out-of-order and delayed callbacks close only the matching ExposureId and item
fault injection cannot overwrite another frame, double-return a buffer, or decrement the wrong pending count
sustained accepted, RAW, JLS, 3FR-close, per-item release, and final buffer-return counts remain equal
goals.title: Preserve official per-ExposureId item ownership

goals.origin: In the successful stock three-frame trace, the second and third physical exposure sessions start while hasPendingBuffers is true and before the first FullRaw item is even sent to storage. Three distinct 3FR files are later persisted and their FullRaw buffers are released per ExposureId; forcing every next exposure to wait for file close would destroy the stock pipeline, while reusing a pending buffer would corrupt it.
goals.required_behavior: The physical leaf-shutter scheduler may overlap later exposures with earlier RAW processing and storage only through bounded, separately owned frame contexts. File persistence is not a global next-shot gate, but a frame buffer remains unavailable until the matching successful storage callback and request cleanup return it. When the bounded pool is exhausted, capture applies backpressure instead of overwriting or deadlocking.
required_evidence: a stock reference trace proves later sessions begin before earlier FullRaw notification and release
each 3FR write end is followed by file persistence and then the matching FullRaw release
a bounded in-flight-frame model states pool capacity, allocation, ownership transitions, and backpressure behavior
tests cover slow storage, out-of-order item completion, failed persistence, pool exhaustion, shutter release, and recovery
target-rate traces show equal exposure, RAW, JLS, 3FR persistence, FullRaw release, and buffer-return counts with no permanent pending state
goals.title: Capture cadence and storage completion remain safely asynchronous

goals.origin: The earlier IMX861 audit directly correlated DUSS or HAL still-mode token 2 with libsensor register-table index 2. A successful official capture instead records sensor_mode id 2 for IMX861_11K9K_14b_M0_H_9P while the physical driver executes readout mode 53 (0x35), which selects group 5 index 3 and differs from direct group-0 index 2 at 99 register values.
goals.required_behavior: Every sensor-mode modification must bind each UI or HAL selection token to the actual production physical readout ID, registry group, local table index, descriptor, and live sensor name. A numerically equal or similarly named direct-driver index is never accepted as the production mapping without independent runtime evidence.
required_evidence: exact hashes bind the official libsensor ELF, loader-applied readout registry, and successful stock camera log
one live transaction maps the upper sensor_mode id through the identical sensor name to the physical readout mode
the physical readout registry range, table address, local index, descriptor, and register profile are parsed independently
tests reject direct group-0 mode 2 as the production 14-bit-HS register profile
all superseded direct-index feasibility claims remain excluded from implementation and release evidence
goals.title: HAL still-mode tokens are not physical sensor readout IDs

goals.origin: The official 14-bit-HS topology requests 9.000000fps, but the physical IMX861 path reports 8.845592fps with the observed 902 by 9024 timing pair, a 113.050667ms source period rather than the 111.111111ms period required for exact 9fps.
goals.required_behavior: A 9fps UI preset may be a nominal product label, but engineering reports, scheduling budgets, metadata, and release claims must retain the measured physical source rate and the slower whole-camera leaf-shutter rate. Exact 9.000fps may be claimed only after a new physical timing configuration and full sensor, shutter, RAW, storage, thermal, and fault validation.
required_evidence: the requested topology rate and reported physical sensor rate are captured from the same exact stock artifact
the active XHS and XVS pair reproduces the reported rate using an explicitly scoped timing-clock inference
6fps and nominal 9fps budgets state their exact periods and do not equate sensor source cadence with stored-file cadence
live release traces measure sustained FSync-to-FSync and successful 3FR-close intervals while the shutter remains held
rate fallback and long-exposure behavior are represented honestly in the UI and metadata
goals.title: Nominal burst labels do not replace measured physical cadence

goals.origin: Function-level recovery of the official packed EXMCU image, loaded at runtime base 0x08008200, identifies runtime handlers 0x080748d0 and 0x08074e7c for events 0x20 and 0x7d. They form a symmetric two-latch start gate: whichever event arrives first sets a latch; only the second enters the same production transaction at runtime 0x080743bc. The earlier values 0x0806c6d0, 0x0806cc7c, and 0x0806c1bc are file-offset-derived locations, not runtime virtual addresses. Replaying 0x7d or advancing either event early therefore does not create a safe per-frame repeat schedule.
goals.required_behavior: The 0x20 and 0x7d event pair remains a one-transaction readiness gate. No implementation may use either event, its latch, or an early call to runtime 0x080743bc as frame-rate control. Burst cadence requires an explicit scheduler with independently proven sensor, lens, frame, and storage readiness.
required_evidence: exact EXMCU binary hash and recovered functions bind both event handlers and both latch offsets
the transaction entry has exactly the verified two direct latch-gate callers
tests reject duplicate, early, reordered, or missing 0x20 and 0x7d events as additional captured frames
target-rate evidence identifies a separate bounded scheduler rather than counting gate entries
goals.title: EXMCU start latches are not a burst cadence scheduler

goals.origin: The official exposure controller is a singleton rooted at RAM 0x200049e0. Its recovered transaction entry receives only that shared context and mutates shared timing fields; the legacy start gate itself supplies no immutable per-frame ownership. Re-entering it while the previous sensor transaction is still active would overwrite shared state rather than create another frame context.
goals.required_behavior: Any high-speed path that overlaps sensor transactions must use a bounded pool of immutable per-frame sensor contexts and explicit ownership transitions. The legacy singleton transaction may not be re-entered before its current transaction completes, and shared timing, mode, callback, or result fields may not stand in for a frame identity.
required_evidence: exact singleton address, constructor, reset, transaction entry, and all direct callers are hash-bound
every overlapping exposure has a unique immutable frame id and separately owned sensor result context
fault tests delay and reorder sensor events without mutating or completing the wrong frame
pool exhaustion applies backpressure and abort or release returns every context exactly once
goals.title: The legacy EXMCU singleton is not reused as overlapping frame state

goals.origin: The successful official 14-bit HS trace sleeps and standbys the sensor, returns from physical capture mode 0x35 to live-view preparation, and completes the exposure sequence after every frame. Transfer finishes about 169ms after FSync and sequence completion about 220ms after FSync, so 6fps and nominal 9fps require the next sensor period to overlap work that the stock path still owns.
goals.required_behavior: A high-speed held-shutter path may retain physical mode 0x35 only after the exact stock sleep, standby, restore, and live-view-return branches are identified and replaced with a bounded interframe transition. Stock single-shot and final burst release keep the complete official restore behavior; every error, timeout, thermal limit, lens refusal, and shutter release must force the same safe restore exactly once.
required_evidence: a hash-bound call graph identifies the exact per-frame sleep, standby, timing-stop, restore, and mode-0x35-to-live-view operations
the retained-mode branch is reachable only from the dedicated held-burst preset and leaves stock single-shot unchanged
timing tests prove frame n plus 1 never reuses a sensor or lens resource still owned by frame n
release, cancel, timeout, storage backpressure, lens error, and thermal fault tests all restore live view and shutter idle exactly once
sustained live traces show equal FSync, sensor result, RAW, JLS, 3FR persistence, and buffer-return counts at the claimed rate
goals.title: High-speed leaf burst must replace stock interframe sensor teardown safely

goals.origin: The first EXMCU Ghidra project loaded the packed binary at 0x08000000 and treated file offsets as runtime addresses. That made SensorImx861 vtable targets land inside unrelated functions and shifted every recovered sensor and exposure address by 0x8200. The reset vector, source strings, SensorImx861 constructor literal, and 42-entry vtable independently prove runtime_address = file_offset + 0x08008200 for this execution region.
goals.required_behavior: Every EXMCU analysis records both packed file offset and runtime virtual address, uses runtime load base 0x08008200 for this exact binary, and excludes all reports made with the superseded 0x08000000 linear map until each claim is independently revalidated in a clean correctly mapped project. No patch location, call graph, or release claim may be derived from an unvalidated raw file offset.
required_evidence: the exact EXMCU binary hash is bound to the reset-vector pointer, mapped reset-handler bytes, and the rejected linear-offset bytes
multiple runtime string pointers map to the expected packed offsets with the same 0x8200 delta
the SensorImx861 constructor and all 42 vtable targets resolve to exact Thumb function entries in the clean runtime-mapped project
critical sleep, standby, prepare-mode, exposure-restore, transaction, and latch handlers record both packed offsets and runtime addresses
all legacy EXMCU conclusions used by later gates are rerun against the corrected project and old linear reports are not accepted as evidence
goals.title: EXMCU packed offsets are never used as runtime addresses

goals.origin: The generic libdcam framework exposes STILL_OP_BURST as operation 3, which initially appeared to be a ready-made native burst engine. Exact analysis of the X2D-specific libdcam_shooter_still_x2d plugin proves its capture-start path accepts only operation 2; operation 3 follows the unsupported-capture-operation path and returns 0xfffffc0b. The operation-2 path already installs reusable start-exposure, stop-exposure, shoot, finalize, buffer-count, and resource-readiness callbacks.
goals.required_behavior: The X2D held-burst implementation preserves capture operation 2 and extends its existing session lifetime. No build may switch capture parameters to generic operation 3 unless the X2D-specific shooter, all callbacks, error paths, and live behavior are separately adapted and completely validated.
required_evidence: exact hashes bind libdcam_frwk, libdcam_shooter_still_x2d, camera-service, and their recovered control flow
the generic framework's operation-3 validation is distinguished from the X2D plugin's operation-2-only acceptance branch
the active X2D path installs the verified per-frame shoot, start, stop, finalize, buffer-count, and readiness callbacks
binary and runtime traces prove every v9 preset keeps operation 2 and does not enter the unsupported-operation result
fault and release tests finalize one operation-2 session exactly once without leaking its resources
goals.title: Generic framework Burst operation is not the X2D still-shooter mode

goals.origin: The stock StateWaitForBuffersWithAbort is safe at the first exposure-session entry but cannot be reused unchanged between frames. It clears its callback-seen flag on entry, and the first readiness callback samples fullPressActive only when that flag was already set. If the user released the shutter during the preceding exposure and resources are immediately ready, an unmodified loop can advance to one unintended extra exposure.
goals.required_behavior: Every repeated-frame path samples the current full-press state before accepting a positive readiness result. Released means stop and finalize the session; held but not ready means remain bounded in the wait state; only held and ready may start exactly one next exposure. Release during any exposure must be observed before the next frame starts.
required_evidence: exact camera-service hash and instruction-level evidence bind the stock release handler, entry flag reset, readiness callback, and fullPressActive accessor
the dedicated interframe gate has an exhaustive held-by-ready truth-table test
release-before-entry, release-during-readiness, release-during-exposure, delayed callback, and callback-reordering tests cannot produce an extra frame
release and every error path reach StateStopExposureSession exactly once and preserve the official restore sequence
live held-and-release traces show no FSync, exposure ID, RAW item, or file appears after the accepted release boundary
goals.title: Interframe repeat gate checks shutter hold before resource readiness

goals.origin: The camera-service Ghidra project uses image base 0x00100000, while the production ELF executable segment is linked at virtual address zero. A preliminary v9 patch sketch copied Ghidra addresses such as 0x0028d794 and 0x00287c98 directly; the corresponding ELF virtual addresses are 0x0018d794 and 0x00187c98. Direct use would patch unrelated instructions even though the textual decompile appeared correct.
goals.required_behavior: Every camera-service patch site records Ghidra address, ELF virtual address, and file offset separately. The patcher derives or verifies the ELF virtual address from the exact symbol and image-base delta, maps it through the ELF program headers, and requires exact original instruction bytes before changing a copy.
required_evidence: the exact camera-service hash and ELF program headers are recorded
the relevant symbol-table entry contains every hook virtual address
each Ghidra address equals ELF virtual address plus the audited 0x00100000 image base
each file offset is obtained from the executable PT_LOAD rather than copied from a report
tests deliberately reject an unconverted Ghidra address and any mismatched original instruction
goals.title: Ghidra image-base addresses are translated before binary patching

goals.origin: A handoff summary recorded the v9 requirement-contract SHA-256 without its final hexadecimal character. The file itself hashes to 054829d4a5f20d6312d928fba3737ee9fafc6a4e952f4d02290c47098cd1bc9b. Copying the truncated value into an audit caused a correct artifact to fail identity binding.
goals.required_behavior: Every release or audit run recomputes SHA-256 directly from each current artifact and requires exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Summaries and prior reports are references only and may not supply an unchecked expected identity.
required_evidence: the hash is recomputed from the current file bytes during the run
the recorded digest matches the 64-character lowercase hexadecimal format
the requirement contract, candidate binaries, sensor configuration, regression file, and package each have separate identities
tests reject truncated, extended, uppercase, malformed, and stale digests
reports do not infer a missing package, live component, or active-slot hash
goals.title: Artifact hashes are recomputed and stored at full length

goals.origin: The isolated menu container is borrowed from hidden developer infrastructure. Reusing more than the intended row can accidentally expose AutoFocus test, RAW Bit Depth, video-audio, or other diagnostic controls in the retail Continuous panel.
goals.required_behavior: Drive Mode > Continuous registers exactly one native Burst Mode selector. The exact private key admits only vector row zero; all other menu keys preserve stock filtering, and no developer or image-quality control becomes newly visible elsewhere.
required_evidence: the compiled Continuous QML object points to one unique private submenu key
the exact-key filter returns visible only for row index zero and replays the displaced stock prologue for every other key
only the isolated videoSettingsAudio row zero is replaced and the hidden debug map alone is redirected
the stock image-bit-depth availability function and image-quality vector remain byte-identical
runtime menu enumeration shows one Burst Mode row and no leaked diagnostic controls
goals.title: Burst preset menu exposes one production control only

goals.origin: Earlier UI designs split frame rate and bit depth into separate controls or encoded 3/6/9 as exposure counts, allowing impossible or ambiguous combinations.
goals.required_behavior: The selector contains exactly four entries in this order: 16-bit 3fps, 14-bit 3fps, 14-bit 6fps, and 14-bit 9fps. They persist as one bounded value 0 through 3; no independent bit-depth toggle or fixed-count field participates in Continuous selection.
required_evidence: the display table allocates exactly four independently owned PropertyData entries
every cloned QString is replaced with the exact label and every entry stores its exact value
the persistence setter/getter accepts and round-trips only the defined domain in the burst context
the candidate contains no fixed-count hook and no Burst Length label
restart and mode-switch tests preserve the selected atomic value without changing stock single-shot bit depth
goals.title: Four burst presets are atomic labels and values

goals.origin: A menu can render and persist correctly while camera-service still ignores the value or routes it to an unsafe topology. Earlier versions were presented too early because successful patching or visible UI was mistaken for an end-to-end feature.
goals.required_behavior: Any artifact that changes only camera-gui remains explicitly non-installable and package-free. A v9 firmware candidate exists only after each persisted value reaches the verified backend dispatch, native leaf-shutter scheduler, matching sensor mode, RAW pipeline, storage completion, and rollback path.
required_evidence: the UI foundation manifest names no camera-service, sensor configuration, installer, or CIM output
installable and package-created fields remain false while any backend or live gate is incomplete
a four-value runtime dispatch matrix binds UI read-back to physical capture behavior
each accepted exposure reaches a valid 3FR close and returns its matching frame resources
the exact installed slot and component hashes are read back before any release claim
goals.title: A UI-only foundation is never promoted as working firmware

goals.origin: Current stock timing proves that removing per-frame session churn alone cannot reach 6fps or 9fps, while using electronic shutter or a diagnostic lens actuator loop would make the UI appear functional without satisfying the requested native capture chain.
goals.required_behavior: The 14-bit 6fps and 14-bit 9fps values remain disabled or unreleased until a dedicated operation-2 held-session scheduler safely overlaps the required cross-frame work and measures the claimed stored-file cadence. No fallback to electronic shutter, diagnostic burst commands, duplicated EXMCU start events, or a lower unreported rate is permitted.
required_evidence: a hash-bound scheduler call graph identifies the new per-frame cadence source and all readiness dependencies
static diff proves no electronic-shutter override or diagnostic Exposure_Burst_shooting path is selected
bounded frame ownership and backpressure tests pass at both target periods
live lens request and acknowledgement traces prove one native leaf cycle for every stored exposure
sustained FSync and successful 3FR-close measurements report actual cadence and any fallback honestly
goals.title: Nominal 6/9fps leaf-shutter presets cannot be silently substituted

goals.origin: Function-level recovery of the official X2D still-shooter plugin shows that operation 2 installs shoot, start-exposure, stop-exposure, finalize, total-buffer-count, and resource-readiness callbacks. _x2dss_shoot increments aggregate full-link and RAW BOUT/ROUT pending counters, while readiness rejects work when the full-link limit or a post-process buffer, metadata, or optional pre-process queue is full. A later review found that these shared counters and queue checks do not identify one immutable request context or prove that a unique RAW buffer was reserved before physical actuation. The earlier wording incorrectly elevated admission and backpressure evidence into a complete per-frame ownership proof.
goals.required_behavior: Every v9 repeated-frame request remains inside the verified X2D operation-2 path and preserves its full-link counter and three queue checks as mandatory admission and backpressure controls, but this is not a unique per-frame ownership proof. A new scheduler may decide when the physical leaf-shutter transaction is safe only after separately proving or adding one immutable request context and unique RAW-buffer reservation per accepted actuation. It may not bypass readiness, overwrite aggregate counters, invent one shared current-frame context, or trigger after capacity denial.
required_evidence: the exact X2D still-shooter binary hash and callback table bind all six operation-2 continuous-capture callbacks
the 0x4f4c, 0x4f4d, 0x4f4e, and 0x4f4f messages are bound to shoot, start, stop, and finalization behavior

the X2D _x2dss_shoot path increments total requested, full-link in-flight, RAW BOUT, and optional RAW ROUT aggregate counters before starting exposure, without treating those counters as a unique request or buffer identity
the readiness path denies capture at max in-flight or when post-process buffer, metadata, or optional pre-process capacity is exhausted
the final candidate separately proves a bounded immutable request context and unique RAW-buffer reservation dominates every accepted physical actuation
fault and saturation tests prove denied requests create no FSync and every accepted request returns its context, buffer, counters, and queue entries exactly once
finalization waits for active RAW consumers, reports the total request count, completes the capture request, and returns to live view exactly once
goals.title: Preserve X2D operation-2 admission checks without mistaking them for frame ownership

goals.origin: The official EXMCU contCap byte in SensorHdlr is driven by the dedicated cable-release input path: InputDeviceHdlr tracks plug-detect and cable-release latches, mirrors the release state into SensorHdlr property 0x7c, and clears it on release or disconnect. SensorHdlr::stopStream skips sensor sleep and standby for stop options 1 and 2 only while that byte is set. The public X2Bridge PreStartExpo, StartExpo, and StopExpo messages contain no contCap argument, so the stock top-shutter burst path cannot safely gain retained mode by assuming this private cable state is already active.
goals.required_behavior: A v9 held-burst implementation uses an explicit, bounded continuous-session control path from the operation-2 scheduler to EXMCU retained mode. It may reuse the proven SensorHdlr behavior, but it may not fake a cable-release event, globally disable sensor sleep or standby, or leave contCap asserted outside the dedicated held-burst session. Shutter release and every abort or fault clear retained mode and execute the complete stock final stop and restore exactly once; stock single-shot and top-button behavior remain unchanged.
required_evidence: the exact EXMCU hash binds the SensorHdlr singleton, contCap byte, stopStream options, and sleep plus standby branch
the InputDeviceHdlr plug-detect, cable-release latch, property 0x7c and 0x98 writes, source strings, and release or disconnect clear paths are mapped independently
the exact librcam hash proves the public 0x101, 0x301, and 0x501 X2Bridge exposure messages carry no generic contCap selector
a new or deliberately extended host-to-EXMCU session command has authenticated set, acknowledge, query, clear, timeout, and idempotent-finalize behavior without synthesizing physical cable input
truth-table and fault tests cover start rejection, held intermediate stop, normal release, disconnect, abort, timeout, storage backpressure, lens error, sensor-transfer error, and reboot recovery

live traces prove intermediate frames skip only the intended sensor sleep and standby while the final frame performs the complete official stop, lens restore, live-view return, and contCap clear exactly once
goals.title: EXMCU retained-sensor state is not a generic burst switch

goals.origin: The exposure bridge already consumes request/response pairs 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, and 11/12. Its fixed 12-entry command table has no spare exposure queue, so adding response 10 to that table by reusing an index would corrupt another command or service. Exact host and EXMCU recovery also proves a safer extension point: EXMCU's exposure dispatcher has no request-9 case, X2Bridge_Register_ReceiveCallback deliberately permits exposure response 10, and the receive callback invokes registered messages before the normal MsgId2Cmd queue lookup.
goals.required_behavior: The v9 burst-session control uses a dedicated exposure request 9 and response 10 callback without resizing, replacing, or aliasing any stock command queue. The response-10 path validates exact transport length, protocol version, magic, session token, operation, and status before accepting an acknowledgement because registered callbacks run before the stock generic header and size checks. BEGIN, QUERY, END, ABORT, timeout, and duplicate-finalize semantics are explicit and idempotent; unsupported or invalid responses leave retained mode cleared and fall back to the complete stock stop path.
required_evidence: exact librcam and EXMCU hashes bind the command table, MsgId2Cmd mapping, callback registration validator, receive dispatch order, and exposure packet switch
all 12 stock queue entries and the five exposure request or response pairs remain unchanged, with no new queue index or service alias
EXMCU adds only request-9 dispatch and response-10 acknowledgement while existing request cases 1, 3, 5, 7, and 11 remain byte-identical
the host registers response 10 through the proven callback LUT and a pre-dispatch guard rejects wrong length, version, magic, token, operation, or status before state is accepted
protocol tests cover BEGIN, QUERY, END, ABORT, duplicate END, stale token, malformed packet, missing response, reboot, disconnect, and mixed stock or patched component versions
every rejected, timed-out, or incompatible transaction keeps or returns the camera to the complete stock final-stop and live-view state without altering other X2Bridge services
goals.title: Burst-session protocol never aliases an existing X2Bridge queue

goals.origin: The official XCD 35-100E sequence already completes the 0x17 charge-during-readout lens command roughly 104 to 106ms before the current sensor transfer returns. Lens firmware state 7 then reports completion and returns its exposure state to zero, so the next lens preparation can potentially be staged during that remaining transfer. However, camx_v2 still performs set_power_state and still_transfer synchronously, and the next frame starts through a separate synchronous sensor start-exposure call. Treating the lens acknowledgement as whole-frame readiness would re-enter the stock singleton sensor transaction and corrupt frame ownership; duplicating the charge command would also disturb the proven lens state machine.
goals.required_behavior: A 14-bit native-leaf interframe scheduler may stage exactly one next-frame lens preparation only after the current frame's 0x17 acknowledgement has completed successfully and operation-2 backpressure has reserved a distinct frame context. It must not issue a duplicate charge command, start the next sensor exposure, issue the next open or close command, advance the frame id, or transfer ownership until the current still_transfer has returned successfully. Release, capacity denial, timeout, lens error, sensor error, or final frame cancels any staged preparation and executes the complete stock RestoreLens option 0 and idle path exactly once. Nominal 9fps remains unreleased until the synchronous singleton sensor receive path is replaced by bounded per-frame transactions that safely support overlapping transfers.
required_evidence: exact EXMCU, librcam, lens firmware, stock trace, and scheduler hashes bind the stop, charge, lens acknowledgement, sensor transfer, next start-exposure, restore, and idle states
a dependency graph distinguishes lens-ready, sensor-transfer-complete, RAW-buffer-owned, and storage-ready events and never treats one acknowledgement as all four
the interframe model permits one staged preparation after successful 0x17 completion but forbids next exposure, open or close, frame-id advance, and ownership transfer before still_transfer success
static and behavioral checks prove each accepted frame emits one charge command, no duplicated 0x17 or 0x18 command, and exactly one native leaf cycle
release, backpressure, timeout, lens failure, transfer failure, stale callback, and duplicate-finalize tests cancel staged work and perform stock final restore and idle exactly once

6fps and 9fps labels are not released on static feasibility alone; sustained live traces must bind FSync, lens acknowledgements, sensor results, RAW ownership, 3FR close, returned buffers, and measured stored-file cadence
goals.title: Leaf preparation may overlap readout but the next exposure may not reuse the stock sensor transaction

goals.origin: The first interframe dependency model returned direct references to its live lists. A snapshot taken before sensor-transfer completion was silently changed by later RAW ownership and next-frame events, so otherwise correct checks could report an impossible historical state or conceal an ordering regression.
goals.required_behavior: Every behavioral or state-machine audit freezes each evidence snapshot at the instant it is recorded. Later transitions, callbacks, list appends, map updates, or finalization must not change earlier evidence. Release decisions may never rely on a report whose historical states alias mutable runtime objects.
required_evidence: snapshot helpers copy or serialize all nested mutable collections instead of returning live references
a regression test records the pre-transfer snapshot, completes transfer and starts the next frame, then proves the earlier frame id, ownership, command lists, and trace remain unchanged
report generation and JSON serialization produce the same historical state when repeated after later model activity
every newly named firmware version reruns the immutable-snapshot test together with all previous behavioral gates
goals.title: Behavioral audit snapshots cannot be mutated by later events

goals.origin: Although libsensor_phy exports generic event-registration functions, the active EXMCU sensor path and the direct IMX861 fallback both call combo_rx_slec_wait_frame_end synchronously. That helper polls one receiver's current line number every 100us until it is stable, carries no frame id or immutable result context, and returns through the same sensor object. The surrounding start-transfer function enables the receiver, sends one transfer request, waits, then disables the receiver before returning. Therefore the existence of generic IRQ callbacks does not prove that two still frames can be received concurrently or matched safely.
goals.required_behavior: The nominal 9fps path may not re-enter, parallelize, or detach the stock still_transfer call. Before overlapping frame n plus 1 exposure with frame n receive, a replacement receive engine must reserve a distinct frame context and buffer, bind hardware sequence evidence to that frame id, deliver one terminal completion, and release the receiver and ownership exactly once. Generic combo-rx event registration is usable only after its event identity, ordering, loss, duplicate, timeout, and teardown behavior are proven for this physical mode and mapped into the operation-2 backpressure contract.
required_evidence: exact librcam, libsensor_phy, libsensor_imx861, sensor-mode, stock-trace, and candidate hashes bind both synchronous transfer implementations and the physical 0x35 path
static analysis proves whether frame-end events include a monotonic hardware sequence or buffer identity instead of only receiver-wide line state
a bounded per-frame context pool rejects reuse and pool exhaustion before any sensor start, leaf command, frame-id advance, or RAW ownership change
delayed, reordered, duplicated, lost, and stale completion tests can never complete or release the wrong frame
receiver enable, transfer request, completion, error recovery, final disable, and reboot recovery each execute exactly once for every accepted context
sustained live traces at the released nominal rate show a one-to-one mapping among leaf cycles, FSync, hardware receive sequences, RAW buffers, 3FR closes, and returned contexts
goals.title: The stock SLEC receive wait is not a per-frame asynchronous completion engine

goals.origin: The SLVS-EC registration used by the IMX861 EXMCU image system dispatches mapped receiver error events to sensor_slvs_ec_isr. Separately, the lower idi2vbus ISR counts raw completion-edge types only for FPS diagnostics and may mask the complete-interrupt bits after the first stream event. Those counters live in receiver IRQ scratch state, are not delivered through the registered callback, and contain no capture request id, RAW buffer id, or immutable sequence binding. Treating a diagnostic count as a completed photo would recreate the frame-context mismatch that previously caused pending saves and missing files.
goals.required_behavior: A replacement 9fps receive engine may use a proven hardware edge as one input, but it may not promote the existing FPS diagnostic count or mapped error callback directly to photo completion. Each accepted edge must be validated against an armed physical receiver epoch and bound to exactly one reserved capture context and RAW buffer before it can advance ownership. Interrupt masking, receiver restart, counter wrap, duplicate edges, stale edges, timeout, abort, and reboot must never complete the wrong context.
required_evidence: exact libsensor_phy and librcam hashes bind event registration, IRQ mapping, FPS counters, completion-interrupt masking, registered callback behavior, and the active still-transfer path
static analysis proves the registered IMX861 callback consumes mapped SLVS-EC event codes as error statistics and receives no capture frame id, RAW buffer id, or diagnostic counter value
static analysis identifies which raw idi2vbus edge corresponds to the physical end of the selected 0x35 frame and whether that edge remains enabled once per accepted still transaction
a new monotonic receiver epoch plus per-frame context binding distinguishes counter wrap, receiver restart, stale callback, duplicate edge, reordered edge, and multiple buffered frames
fault tests prove no diagnostic or error event can close a 3FR, return a RAW buffer, or decrement operation-2 ownership without the matching sensor transaction and storage completion
live traces correlate the chosen hardware edge with FSync, sensor result, RAW buffer, 3FR close, and context return for every stored frame before nominal 9fps is released
goals.title: Receiver diagnostic edge counters are not capture frame identities

goals.origin: The physical SLVS-EC Frame End event is mapped as event 0x0b, but the same receiver also reports 50fps live-view frame ends, so the event alone cannot identify a still photo. Independent recovery of the official same-version IMX861 EXMCU test resource maps the active SLVS-EC receiver channel to zero from resource offset 0x30 and the hardware VBUS frame-count channel to zero from the separate resource offset 0x34. The VBUS counter is only 16 bits and therefore wraps modulo 65536. The explicit frame-count clear helper is called by MIPI configuration, not by the recovered SLVS-EC configuration, enable, or disable paths; SLVS-EC top reset writes a reset mask whose effect on this counter has not been proven. A count observed without an explicit still-capture baseline could therefore belong to live view, a previous receiver generation, or a wrapped sequence.
goals.required_behavior: Every overlapping still-receive session binds the exact active receiver resource fields before use, stops or isolates live-view input, arms the still receiver, and then records a fresh VBUS baseline for a new capture generation. Each accepted frame must advance exactly one count modulo 65536 from that generation's expected value; 65535 to 0 is valid, while a duplicate, gap, reorder, stale generation, unbaselined event, or unexpected reset fails closed before any RAW ownership or storage completion changes. Receiver reset, reconfiguration, abort, timeout, mode switch, live-view restart, or reboot invalidates the generation and requires a new baseline. Neither event 0x0b nor the VBUS count alone may release a RAW buffer: the accepted count must also bind the matching operation-2 request, immutable receive epoch, reserved buffer, sensor result, and downstream completion.
required_evidence: exact hashes bind librcam, libsensor_phy, the same-version IMX861 EXMCU test binary, its SensorCfgInfo resource pointer, and the resource bytes proving independent SLVS-EC channel-zero and VBUS-count channel-zero fields
static analysis binds event 0x0b to physical SLVS-EC Frame End, proves that live view shares that event source, and binds the four 16-bit VBUS counter fields and per-channel clear bits

static call-graph evidence distinguishes the MIPI explicit-clear caller from SLVS-EC config, enable, disable, physical reset, and top-reset paths, without assuming the undocumented top-reset mask clears the counter

behavioral tests cover a fresh post-arm baseline, normal increment, 65535-to-0 wrap, duplicate count, skipped count, reordered epoch, stale callback, pre-baseline event, live-view contamination, reset, abort, timeout, and mandatory re-baselining

every accepted hardware count is joined to exactly one operation-2 request, receive generation, immutable epoch, reserved RAW buffer, sensor result, 3FR close, and buffer return; unmatched events cannot decrement or release anything

read-only live traces prove the active production resource values, baseline point, reset behavior, one-to-one stored-frame correlation, and sustained cadence before any nominal 9fps build becomes installable
goals.title: VBUS frame counts are capture-generation scoped and wrap-safe

goals.origin: The official ImageSystem interface already exposes get_frame_count at operation offset 0x220 and the production system monitor calls it while the camera device is streaming. That monitor keeps only a previous count, current count, and unchanged-sample counter; after 16 unchanged samples it reports a 1500ms stall and resets the image sensor. It contains no operation-2 request id, receive epoch, RAW buffer, sensor-result identity, or 3FR state. Reusing its mutable state as a burst baseline or completion callback would race the background monitor and could either release the wrong frame or reset the sensor during a legitimate still-transfer pause.
goals.required_behavior: A burst receive engine may call the same hash-bound ImageSystem get_frame_count operation, but it must maintain a separate capture-generation baseline and immutable per-frame bindings. It may not read, overwrite, reset, alias, or infer photo completion from the liveness monitor's previous count, current count, or unchanged-sample counter. Any expected stream pause, receiver reconfiguration, or retained-sensor transition must coordinate the monitor through its supported enable or disable lifecycle and reinitialize the monitor's own baseline on resume, without weakening the 1500ms recovery behavior for stock modes. A monitor-triggered reset invalidates every capture epoch and requires bounded abort, complete stock restore, and a fresh post-arm baseline.
required_evidence: exact librcam hash and public ImageSystem operation-table bytes bind get_frame_count at interface offset 0x220 to the IMX861 EXMCU VBUS-count implementation

instruction and decompile evidence binds the production stream-alive monitor call, camera-state and enable guards, previous and current count fields, 16-sample unchanged threshold, 1500ms report, and sensor-reset path
static call-site review proves no existing stock capture scheduler obtains a request-bound completion merely from the get_frame_count interface

behavioral tests keep liveness state and capture-generation state disjoint and cover normal increments, held burst, expected pause, counter wrap, monitor reset, abort, timeout, receiver reconfiguration, and resume

a monitor reset cannot mark a frame successful, close a 3FR, or decrement operation-2 ownership as completed; only the bounded abort path may reclaim its RAW buffer, and no stale hardware count may complete a new generation
read-only live traces show the monitor remains safe through every released preset and that all capture completions still bind request, epoch, buffer, sensor result, 3FR close, and context return
goals.title: The VBUS liveness monitor is not a capture completion context

goals.origin: The official global leaf-shutter single-capture state registers dedicated FSync and frame-end callbacks. Its FSync callback rejects zero, duplicate, and stale frame ids, writes the accepted hardware frame id into the common-still exposure record, and obtains the matching capture result. Its final-IRQ helper compares the actual frame id with that predicted record before emitting internal frame-over event 0x23. This is a stronger production identity chain than the receiver-wide VBUS count and avoids recreating the frame-id mismatch that previously left saves pending.
goals.required_behavior: Every v9 held-burst frame extends or reuses the official expm_register_irq_cb FSync and frame-end identity path. An accepted nonzero increasing hardware frame id must remain joined to one operation-2 request, capture result, receive generation, RAW buffer, sensor result, and 3FR close. The matching final IRQ may advance that frame to frame-over, but frame-over alone may not close storage or return ownership. VBUS count remains secondary diagnostic evidence and may never replace the callback frame id. Zero, duplicate, stale, reordered, mismatched, late-generation, or post-abort callbacks fail closed without completing a different frame.
required_evidence: exact librcam and candidate hashes bind global-single segment activation, exposure mode selection, FSync and frame-end callback registration, both callback bodies, the shared final-IRQ helper, frame-over state, and operation-2 capture ownership

static analysis proves the FSync callback accepts only a nonzero increasing frame id, marks a common-still exposure record with that exact id, and obtains the capture result through the official capture interface

static analysis proves the final-IRQ helper compares actual and predicted frame ids before event 0x23 and that frame-over disables exposure IRQs and returns through the official stream-control transition
a bounded behavioral model joins request id, generation, hardware frame id, capture result, RAW buffer, sensor result, and 3FR close and releases each resource exactly once

zero, duplicate, stale, reordered, mismatched EOF, duplicated EOF, delayed old-generation callback, abort, timeout, storage failure, and missing-close tests cannot mark a frame successful or release the wrong RAW buffer
read-only live traces correlate every released frame's registered FSync id, final IRQ id, capture result, sensor result, 3FR close, and returned operation-2 context
goals.title: Still-frame ownership uses the official IRQ frame identity

goals.origin: The production IMX861 EXMCU exposure-mode operation already coordinates the shared VBUS liveness monitor: exposure mode 1 disables it and sends sensor command 6 value 1, while exposure mode 2 enables it and sends command 6 value 0. Global leaf-shutter capture selects mode 1 before registering frame callbacks, and normal metering selects mode 2 when streaming resumes. Bypassing this lifecycle could let the 16-sample monitor reset the sensor during a legitimate held capture or leave stock live-view recovery unmonitored afterward.
goals.required_behavior: A held-burst generation starts only after the official mode-1 transition succeeds and the liveness monitor is disabled through its registered callback. Capture identity is then owned by the official frame IRQ chain, not by monitor state. Every normal completion, release, rejection, abort, timeout, sensor error, storage error, mode switch, disconnect, and reboot returns through the stock final transition and restores exposure mode 2 exactly once; mode 2 must re-enable the monitor with a fresh independent baseline. A failed mode transition creates no accepted exposure and cannot leave callbacks, retained mode, or monitor state half-switched.
required_evidence: exact librcam and candidate hashes bind the sensor_sysmonitor enable and disable callback slots, IMX861 exposure-mode implementation, global capture activation, normal-metering resume, and frame callback registration order
static analysis proves mode 1 disables the monitor before sensor command 6 value 1 and mode 2 enables the monitor before sensor command 6 value 0
static analysis proves global leaf-shutter capture requests mode 1 before registering FSync and frame-end callbacks and normal metering requests mode 2 before its resumed stream path
behavioral tests allow no capture baseline, request acceptance, leaf command, sensor start, or RAW ownership before successful mode-1 entry
normal release and every failure path restore mode 2 and a fresh liveness baseline exactly once while stale capture callbacks remain unable to complete a new generation
read-only live traces prove monitor disable, registered capture callbacks, matched frame ids, final capture cleanup, monitor re-enable, and normal 1500ms stock recovery behavior
goals.title: Capture and liveness monitoring follow the official exposure-mode lifecycle

goals.origin: The X2D operation-2 start-exposure callback stores its integer argument at shooter offset 0x2d4 and then dispatches message 0x4f4d. The physical shoot path uses that field only as a first-exposure metering condition together with the total-requested counter at 0x2d0. It then builds a fresh DCAM request and calls cam_shooter_start_expo with the native physical-shutter flag. The camera HAL forwards that request through PRE_START_EXPO and START_EXPO state-machine events, but does not promote the operation-2 ordinal to a hardware frame id. The authoritative still identity is created later by the registered librcam FSync callback. Confusing the ordinal with that IRQ frame id would allow repeated sessions, reset ordinals, or reordered callbacks to bind a RAW buffer to the wrong 3FR transaction.
goals.required_behavior: The operation-2 start-exposure argument remains a scheduler ordinal or first-frame control value only. It may gate stock metering and diagnostics, but it may not key a RAW buffer, sensor result, frame-over event, storage transaction, or operation-2 ownership release. Every accepted exposure instead reserves an immutable request context before physical start and binds that context to the nonzero increasing FSync frame id returned by the official librcam callback. A new session may reset its ordinal without resetting, fabricating, predicting, or reusing the hardware identity. Ordinal duplication, reset, gap, reorder, delayed callback, abort, timeout, and generation rollover all fail closed unless the matching FSync, final IRQ, sensor result, and 3FR close complete the same context.

goals.origin: The four-option UI reuses the otherwise inert af_test_mode property as a private persisted value. An initial backend bridge sanitized stale values only at the public getter while its internal bit-depth and topology selectors treated every nonzero raw value as 14-bit. A legacy value such as 6 or 9 could therefore display 16-bit 3fps while silently selecting the 14-bit high-speed path.
goals.required_behavior: The persisted burst domain is exactly 0 through 3 at every setter, getter, startup restore, live-view selector, effective-bit-depth selector, and exposure-session selector. Any stale, malformed, negative, or out-of-range value fails closed to preset 0 consistently at all of those boundaries. The value affects effective capture behavior only while the official SlowBurst/Continuous drive state is active; single-shot and every unrelated mode retain stock behavior. UI label, persisted value, effective bit depth, live-view group, exposure group, native leaf-shutter state, and reported live read-back must describe the same preset.

goals.origin: The first preset-backend bridge confused two class-relative offsets that both appeared as +0x260 in separate decompilations. LiveviewControl+0x260 points back to CameraObjectImpl, but CameraObjectImpl+0x260 is initialized as a non-pointer sentinel. Treating the latter as a LiveviewControl pointer and writing its +0x121 field could dereference an invalid address even though the isolated helper disassembled cleanly.
goals.required_behavior: A preset change may refresh the active live-view selector only through the proven CameraObjectImpl+0x58 state-machine pointer and the embedded LiveviewControl object at state-machine+0x780, using the stock LiveviewControl::setDriveMode entry point. It may never infer a reverse pointer from an equal numeric member offset, write a foreign object's private field directly, or call the refresh path before the state machine exists. The persisted value remains valid if no state machine is assigned, and the next stock setup path applies it safely.

static decompilation proves CameraObjectImpl+0x260 is not used as the LiveviewControl pointer and the candidate contains no direct write through that mistaken path

goals.origin: The official X2D still shooter has a want_f2f flag at object offset +0x490. When enabled, that branch skips physical stream-consumer activation and cam_shooter_start_expo, creates frame buffers from files, and injects them through _still_f2f_simulate_raw_generated. It can exercise upper RAW and storage plumbing without operating the IMX861, EXMCU, XCD lens, or leaf shutter, so timing from this path would falsely appear to prove a physical 6fps or 9fps burst.
goals.required_behavior: Every released burst preset runs with want_f2f disabled and reaches the native physical cam_shooter_start_expo(..., 1, ...) path, EXMCU lens commands, registered FSync identity callbacks, sensor receive completion, and per-frame 3FR persistence. F2F may remain available only as an explicitly identified diagnostic simulation; no production UI value, persisted setting, startup restore, or fallback may enable it, and its timer or file-backed frames may never count as physical cadence evidence.

goals.origin: The first local P14_6 scheduler draft retained a private session marker in shooter object padding and a three-bit state word in librcam. A marker based only on the saved preset could survive an abnormal session and reach a later stock request, while the first finalizer draft cleared restore ownership before checking whether RestoreLens succeeded. Either mistake could alter single-shot behavior or leave a physically prepared XCD leaf without a retry path.
goals.required_behavior: Every shooter start clears the private session marker before dispatch. It may be set again only when the effective capture path is the official continuous strategy and the sanitized preset is exactly P14_6. The exact marker alone may select private HAL mode 2, which librcam immediately normalizes to the official physical leaf mode. All stock presets, single-shot, non-continuous strategies, malformed values, P14_9, restart, mode switch, disconnect, abort, timeout, and stale requests remain unable to activate or inherit the private scheduler. Successful final restoration clears ownership exactly once; a failed final RestoreLens retains recoverable ownership so the next bounded finalizer or cleanup path can retry without issuing duplicate restore after success.
required_evidence: exact camera-service, shooter, HAL, librcam, UI, sensor configuration, package, active-slot, and live-component hashes bind every marker write, copy, translation, state transition, finalizer, and cleanup hook

instruction-level audit proves every shooter start clears a dedicated loader-zeroed private state word before mode dispatch and only continuous strategy zero plus the exact sanitized P14_6 capture-parameter marker can set it; no unproven shooter-object padding is used

instruction-level audit proves only the exact frame-request magic becomes HAL private mode 2, that mode is normalized before the stock physical leaf path, and P14_9 and electronic-shutter paths contain no activation route

a bounded state model covers inactive, active, staged, restore-debt, successful and failed pre-start, successful and failed stop, staged reuse, stock fallback, release, duplicated finalizer, failed final restore and successful retry

goals.origin: The installed BURST16-3FPS-V4 build was positively identified in the upgrade log. Its failed bursts reported DCAM_STATUS_STILL_EXPO_SENSOR_ERROR, still_transfer failed -152, and an invalid frame before any JLS or 3FR completion evidence. Earlier analysis treated the visible writing indicator and missing files as a downstream storage deadlock even though the first proven failure was the 16-bit sensor transaction. That build also changed mode 3 from 2.70fps to 3.00fps and altered the official group-0 topology, so those two changes cannot be isolated from each other by the available trace.
