A -152 sensor-transfer error, invalid RAW frame, or missing sensor receive completion aborts that frame and applies bounded recovery; it is never counted as a JLS, 3FR, or SSD failure. Downstream storage diagnosis begins only after the same ExposureId has a successful physical FSync, sensor receive, RAW result, and buffer identity.

goals.origin: An initial code-space scan added raw file offsets to 0x08000000 even though the analyzed exMCU_hb722_payload.bin is mapped from minimum runtime address 0x08008200. That 0x8200 error caused unrelated initialized data to be audited instead of the zero-filled file ranges and could have produced a branch to the wrong bytes in a future EXMCU patch.

Runtime address and file offset conversions use runtime = 0x08008200 + file_offset and file_offset = runtime - 0x08008200, reject underflow or overflow, and round-trip known dispatcher and cave anchors. No code cave is accepted from a raw zero scan alone: its correctly mapped runtime range must also contain no functions, symbols, references, relocations, or nonzero source bytes, must be reachable by the intended Thumb branch/calls, and must remain unchanged outside the declared patch ranges.

goals.origin: The lower combo receiver already emits physical SLVS-EC Frame End as event 0x0b and dispatches every IRQ event array to linked callback lists that can hold multiple callback and user-data pairs. The official IMX861 image system registers _dataintf_isr for its full lifetime, but that callback only accumulates receiver statistics; it does not identify or complete a photo. The official still path separately enables the SLVS-EC interrupt mask, waits synchronously for one receiver-wide line-stability condition, and disables the mask. Treating the stock statistics callback, event 0x0b alone, or the receiver-wide wait as a stored-frame completion would misassign live-view or stale edges to burst requests.
goals.required_behavior: A private retained P14_9 receive session leaves the official _dataintf_isr registration and behavior intact and adds at most one dedicated callback with an exact session-generation context on the proven SLVS-EC type and channel. The callback filters event 0x0b, performs only bounded non-blocking event capture, and never compresses, writes, closes, or releases a RAW buffer in IRQ context. An edge becomes a photo completion only after it is matched to the session generation, an armed official FSync or ExposureId, the expected modulo hardware frame-count increment, and the corresponding RAW buffer context. Session start enables the proven interrupt mask once after registration and baseline; finalization disables it once, unregisters the exact callback and context before freeing state, invalidates the generation, and preserves the stock callback. Duplicate registration, missing or reordered identities, shared live-view edges, reset, timeout, abort, disconnect, and delayed callbacks fail closed without completing or releasing another frame.

instruction-level decompilation proves official IMX861 init and deinit symmetrically register and unregister _dataintf_isr and that sensor_slvs_ec_isr only accumulates receiver statistics without photo, RAW-buffer, JLS, or 3FR identity

goals.origin: The individual audits proved an unused request-9/response-10 session channel, official operation-2 backpressure, increasing FSync frame identity, a secondary SLVS-EC event 0x0b, and a generation-scoped hardware frame count. They did not yet prove one combined transaction. A scheduler that treats either FSync or event 0x0b as sufficient, assigns events through an unbounded global FIFO, or actuates the next leaf shutter before operation-2 capacity is reserved can still close or return the wrong RAW context even when every isolated audit passes.
goals.required_behavior: P14_9 activates only from the sanitized 14-bit 9fps continuous preset and retains the official operation-2 capture session, physical XCD leaf-shutter start, and downstream RAW-to-3FR consumers. A guarded request-9 BEGIN acknowledgement establishes one generation and token before retained receive becomes active. Every physical actuation requires an already-reserved operation-2 request and unique RAW buffer. The official nonzero increasing FSync id is the primary identity; the expected modulo hardware count and private event-0x0b edge are secondary receive evidence and may arrive before or after FSync but may only be staged against the oldest eligible context in the same immutable generation. Success requires the same context to receive FSync, final frame IRQ, validated receive edge and count, sensor result, and successful 3FR close before ownership is returned. Capacity denial creates no exposure. Release drains accepted work before guarded END; timeout, invalid acknowledgement, identity error, reset, storage error, disconnect, or mode switch performs bounded ABORT, invalidates the generation, reclaims unfinished buffers only as aborted, and executes receiver teardown, stock final lens restore, exposure-mode restoration, and liveness-monitor restart exactly once. P14_6 and every stock mode remain byte-for-byte outside this path.
required_evidence: exact hashes bind the official X2D shooter, libduml camera HAL, librcam, libsensor_phy, EXMCU payload, sensor configuration, every dependent static audit, and the final candidate binaries

static analysis proves P14_9 alone selects the guarded request-9/response-10 retained session while all physical frames continue through operation 2, cam_shooter_start_expo with the native leaf flag, and the official FSync and final-IRQ callbacks

instruction-level verification proves each leaf actuation follows successful operation-2 readiness and unique context reservation, and that no private ISR, protocol callback, ordinal, VBUS count, or global current-frame variable can close storage or return a buffer

behavioral tests cover FSync-before-edge, edge-before-FSync, multiple in-flight frames, duplicate and reordered FSync, duplicate, missing and shared event-0x0b edges, modulo counter wrap, invalid response length, version, magic, token, operation and status, pool backpressure, release drain, timeout, reset, storage failure, disconnect, delayed old-generation callbacks, and exactly-once teardown and restore

goals.origin: The first request-9/response-10 protocol audit proposed an exact response-length guard in a registered X2Bridge receive callback. Fresh decompilation proves _X2Bridge_RxCallback receives payload, transport length, and bridge context, but invokes registered callbacks with only payload and user context before the stock header mapper and mapped-response size check. A response-10 callback therefore cannot know the transport length and could accept a truncated or oversized acknowledgement if validation is left there.
goals.required_behavior: The P14_9 response-10 path validates the transport length while it is still available at the _X2Bridge_RxCallback boundary or an equivalently proven pre-dispatch shim. It checks the minimum header length before reading the message id, then requires the exact response-10 length, exposure service, protocol version, magic, token, operation, retained-state encoding, and status domain before signaling the session. Invalid or stale response-10 packets are dropped fail-closed without waking a waiter, entering a stock command queue, or asserting the stock receiver. The registered callback may only consume a response already marked valid by the same immutable generation and token. Every non-response-10 packet and all stock callback and queue behavior remain unchanged.
required_evidence: exact official and candidate librcam hashes plus instruction-level decompilation bind _X2Bridge_RxCallback parameters, the registered-callback invocation that omits length, and the later stock mapped-response size check

instruction-level verification proves the candidate reads no response-10 field before a minimum-header check and compares the real transport length to one compile-time protocol size before any session state changes
the pre-dispatch guard is restricted to exposure response 10, preserves every stock callback and queue route, and cannot forward the same acknowledgement through both private and stock dispatch

behavioral tests reject zero, one-byte, truncated, oversized, wrong-service, wrong-version, wrong-magic, wrong-token, wrong-operation, malformed retained-state, invalid-status, duplicate, and delayed old-generation responses without waking or mutating the active session

goals.origin: The verified EXMCU code cave is flash-backed executable storage, not mutable session RAM, and the ExposureHdlr singleton ends immediately before another static object. Fresh reset and allocator analysis proves BSS ends at 0x2001bd60 and the heap begins at that same address through three independent boundary words. Storing the P14_9 active flag, token, generation, or reply scratch in the flash cave, beyond ExposureHdlr, or at the old heap base would corrupt code, an adjacent singleton, or live allocations.
goals.required_behavior: The final EXMCU patch reserves one aligned, bounded state block by moving the BSS end and every heap-start representation forward by exactly the same size. Reset zeroing covers the entire private state, the allocator begins only after it, the initial current-break word agrees with the moved boundary, and the allocator upper limit remains unchanged. Code and constants may live in the verified flash cave, but all mutable flags, tokens, generations, and reply scratch live only in the reserved RAM block. Cleanup zeroes the state idempotently, and no stock singleton, stack, heap allocation, initialized-data word, or unrelated RAM address overlaps it.
required_evidence: exact official EXMCU hash and reset-handler disassembly bind data copy 0x20000000..0x20004658, BSS zeroing 0x20004658..0x2001bd60, stack top 0x200a0000, and the intended reserved-state interval
exact allocator disassembly and initialized-data mapping bind all official 0x2001bd60 representations: reset BSS end, heap-size base, and initial current-break value

an exhaustive aligned and halfword-aligned literal scan proves no undeclared reference to the old boundary remains in the candidate and no reference targets the interior of the reserved block except declared patch helpers

binary diff and round-trip verification prove the three boundary words move by one identical aligned size, the heap upper limit stays 0x2009f800, reset still zeroes the enlarged BSS, and no adjacent initializer changes

instruction-level and emulated reset-allocation tests prove the state is zero before use, first allocation starts at the new boundary, available heap shrinks only by the reserved size, and repeated BEGIN, END, ABORT, request 11, disconnect, and reset cannot leak stale state

read-only live verification after any future candidate proves the active state address lies outside the heap, returns to zero after every terminal path, and stock EXMCU memory and exposure behavior remain stable
goals.title: EXMCU mutable session state is reserved from BSS without colliding with the heap

goals.origin: The first local EXMCU request-9 implementation assembled and its source listed the intended callees, but independent Ghidra disassembly showed three BL instructions in the long request handler landing four bytes after set_contcap and X2Bridge send. Short helpers assembled correctly, so source text, successful assembly, and even correct hook branches were insufficient to detect the per-block Thumb PC drift. Executing that binary would enter the middle of a function.
goals.required_behavior: Every patched Thumb B, B.W, BL, BLX, CBZ/CBNZ, conditional branch, veneer, and return path is decoded from the exact final candidate bytes at its actual runtime address. Each direct call must land on the first instruction of the declared callee in Thumb state; no target may be inferred from assembler source, labels, manifests, or intended addresses alone. Any mismatch, target inside a function, undecodable instruction, fall-through into padding, helper overlap, or changed instruction width fails the candidate before it can be combined with host binaries.
required_evidence: independent Capstone and Ghidra instruction reports bind the exact candidate hash, source address, encoded bytes, mnemonic, decoded destination, and expected function entry for every patched control-flow instruction

the audit explicitly covers the dispatcher hook, request-11 wrapper, disconnect hook, sensor-state calls, response sender, cleanup calls, stock continuations, all conditional labels, and every helper return

function-boundary reports prove each decoded direct-call destination equals a declared function entry rather than entry plus or minus an offset, and every local branch remains inside its owning helper or an approved stock continuation
stack and register analysis is performed on the decoded final instructions after any call-target correction, not reused from the pre-correction assembly
a binary round trip reproduces identical decoded destinations and fails when any call is intentionally shifted by two or four bytes
no host-side, EXMCU, lens, or package candidate advances while a final-byte control-flow target is unverified
goals.title: Every final Thumb call target is decoded from the candidate bytes

goals.origin: The first host response-10 guard used one global boolean and cleared it before rechecking the callback payload against the active token and generation. If an old callback was delayed across teardown and a newer session published its own guard first, the old callback could clear the newer guard, discard the new acknowledgement, and leave the waiter to time out. Sequential happy-path emulation did not expose this cross-generation interleaving.
goals.required_behavior: The pre-dispatch guard atomically reserves one guard-state slot, publishes a shadow operation, generation, and token before marking it ready, and rejects any second producer while the slot is building, ready, or callback-owned. The registered callback compares its payload with the published shadow identity before atomically changing READY to CALLBACK_OWNED, then rechecks the active session identity. A delayed callback with a different token, generation, operation, or user context leaves the newer guard and acknowledgement untouched. Success publishes the result and the IDLE plus ACK_READY transition with one aligned release store. Teardown invalidates the phase, cancels only its own guarded identity or waits for CALLBACK_OWNED to finish, and cannot reuse the state block until the guard is IDLE.
required_evidence: final-byte disassembly proves the guard uses exclusive load and store transitions IDLE to BUILDING to READY, the callback uses READY to CALLBACK_OWNED, and the shadow operation, generation, and token are published before READY
the guard-state and acknowledgement words share one aligned 64-bit pair and successful callback completion changes them to IDLE and ACK_READY with one release store

instruction emulation injects an old guarded callback after a newer token and generation have published READY, proves the old callback cannot alter the newer shadow or acknowledgement, and proves the legitimate newer callback still completes

concurrency and mutation tests cover two simultaneous guards, callback identity changes before and after claim, timeout cancellation, CALLBACK_OWNED teardown, repeated idempotent QUERY responses, token and generation wrap rejection, and no double acknowledgement
session-lifecycle analysis proves no state clear or rearm occurs while the guard is BUILDING, READY for another identity, or CALLBACK_OWNED, including disconnect and mode-switch paths
read-only live traces bind each accepted response 10 to one token, generation, operation, guard transition, and waiter wake while delayed old-generation responses leave the active session unchanged
goals.title: A delayed response callback cannot consume a newer P14_9 guard

goals.origin: The first P14_9 scheduler design treated the continuous-session shoot slot at offset 0x30 as the operation-2 reservation boundary. Hash-bound decompilation proves camera-service never invokes that slot: it calls offset 0x40 for readiness, 0x38 for total capacity, 0x18 for start exposure, 0x20 for stop, and 0x28 for finalization. The X2D slot sends message 0x4f4c. A subsequent dependency audit corrected an important error in the first review: the X2D plug-in does not link the generic base-still shooter, and its own external handler directly dispatches 0x4f4c and 0x4f4d to _x2dss_shoot with start_expo false or true. Generic base-shooter wait and save-context behavior therefore cannot be attributed to X2D. Neither the unused slot, aggregate X2D counters, readiness boolean, nor direct dispatch proves a unique request and RAW-buffer reservation before leaf actuation.
goals.required_behavior: No candidate may claim operation-2 frame ownership from session slot 0x30, message 0x4f4c, aggregate X2D pending counters, a resource-ready boolean, a sensor ordinal, or an EXMCU acknowledgement. P14_9 must use the actual X2D start path to reserve one non-reusable capacity ticket in every required stream consumer before each physical leaf-shutter actuation, then bind the one concrete buffer returned by hardware dequeue and its frame id exactly once to an immutable request context. A specific RAW buffer pointer need not exist before actuation when the verified framework deliberately reserves capacity first and selects the concrete queued object at dequeue; capacity admission must never be misreported as early buffer identity. Any multi-in-flight design must be established from the actual X2D plug-in and camera-service path, not imported from the generic base-still shooter. Reservation failure creates no exposure. Every accepted context completes only from its matching FSync, final receive evidence, sensor result, JLS result, successful 3FR close, and exactly-once buffer return. Stock modes retain their verified per-frame operation-2 order and successful storage behavior.
required_evidence: exact official camera-service and X2D shooter hashes plus instruction-level decompilation bind the continuous-session table layout and every official consumer of offsets 0x18 through 0x48
a complete field-reference audit proves camera-service 1.3.16.2 has no session-slot-0x30 invocation while the X2D implementation of that slot sends only message 0x4f4c

the X2D ELF dynamic dependency list excludes libdcam_shooter_base_still.so and X2D external-handler control flow directly maps 0x4f4c and 0x4f4d to _x2dss_shoot without importing generic base-shooter behavior

final candidate disassembly proves each P14_9 leaf actuation is dominated by successful bounded capacity reservation in every required consumer, and proves the later concrete dequeued buffer and frame id are bound once to the matching immutable request context without changing stock-mode routing

behavioral and instruction-level tests cover reservation exhaustion, two or more in-flight contexts, callback reordering, missing and duplicate completion, storage failure, abort, disconnect, mode switch, delayed old-generation events, and exactly-once context and buffer reclamation

read-only live traces correlate every P14_9 reservation with one native leaf actuation, increasing FSync, final receive evidence, JLS result, 3FR close, and buffer return; any unmatched actuation or context is release-blocking
goals.title: The operation-2 shoot callback is not mistaken for a frame reservation

goals.origin: An operation-2 audit combined the X2D callback table with libdcam_shooter_base_still.so control flow and concluded that X2D message 0x4f4d waits for zero in-flight work and saves a request context. Fresh ELF dependency analysis proves libdcam_shooter_still_x2d.so does not list the generic base-still library as a dependency, while X2D's own external handler directly maps 0x4f4c and 0x4f4d to _x2dss_shoot. The combined conclusion described an unrelated implementation and obscured the actual X2D frame-context boundary.
goals.required_behavior: Every static or live conclusion names the exact binary and verified caller-to-callee chain that supports it. Generic base-still functions may be used only as comparative design evidence unless an X2D runtime dependency, symbol binding, function pointer, or observed call chain reaches them. X2D ownership, wait, scheduling, and storage claims must come from the X2D plug-in, camera-service, its true dependencies, and hash-bound live logs. A missing call-chain proof is reported as unknown rather than filled from a similarly named library.
required_evidence: the exact X2D shooter hash and complete DT_NEEDED list prove whether libdcam_shooter_base_still.so is linked
X2D external-handler decompilation binds 0x4f4c and 0x4f4d to its own _x2dss_shoot paths
all audit reports distinguish X2D runtime evidence from generic base-still comparison evidence and contain no cross-library ownership inference
a call-graph or relocation audit is required before any generic base-still function is promoted to X2D runtime evidence
tests fail when a report claims X2D wait, request-context, or RAW-buffer behavior solely from the generic base-still library
final candidate analysis and live traces use only the verified X2D path for release claims
goals.title: Generic base-still behavior is not attributed to the X2D shooter without a real call chain

goals.origin: A hash-bound official-success log records StateCaptureSlowBurst selecting E_StreamGroup_Still14bitHs with eShutter false. Three distinct ExposureIds each enter _x2dss_shoot with start_expo true, complete operation-2 start, stop, and finalize in order, increment the lens shutter count from 272 through 274, and later finish B0000226.3FR through B0000228.3FR successfully. This disproves the detour through a generic timer shooter and establishes the actual stock X2D reference path.
goals.required_behavior: Stock 14-bit continuous capture remains on the native XCD leaf-shutter path and preserves the observed X2D SlowBurst per-frame operation-2 start, stop, finalize, unique ExposureId, and asynchronous successful 3FR storage behavior. P14_3, P14_6, and P14_9 may extend cadence only through this verified camera-service and X2D shooter path or a fully proven replacement with equivalent identity and cleanup. No electronic-shutter fallback, fixed frame-count interpretation, generic base-still substitution, or early storage-success claim is allowed.
required_evidence: the exact official log hash binds SlowBurst entry and exit, Still14bitHs selection, and eShutter false
three ordered frame cycles bind ExposureIds 3.368, 4.368, and 5.368 to _x2dss_shoot start_expo true and operation-2 start, stop, and finalize
lens shutter counts 272, 273, and 274 prove three native physical leaf actuations
measured exposure-start intervals are reported from the trace without turning one three-frame sample into a sustained-rate claim
B0000226.3FR, B0000227.3FR, and B0000228.3FR each have a write-end and successful completion event
every future candidate preserves this stock reference and adds hash-bound live evidence for its selected 3, 6, or 9 fps mode before release
goals.title: Stock X2D SlowBurst operation-2 leaf-shutter and 3FR path remains the reference

goals.origin: A frame-context audit first treated three X2D aggregate counters as proof that one exact RAW buffer had already been allocated before cam_shooter_start_expo. Hash-bound analysis of the real X2D utility and libdcam framework corrects that model: cam_shooter_start_expo traverses every source common consumer, waits for available capacity, and increments each consumer's cumulative total_request_buf_count before dcam_start_expo. The framework does not select a concrete queued buffer object at that point. The specific object appears when dcam_dequeue succeeds after capture, and the X2D RAW callback then copies hardware frame_buffer+0xb4 into newly allocated per-frame queue contexts. The ticket is real backpressure and must precede actuation, but it is not early buffer identity.
goals.required_behavior: Every burst actuation is preceded by one successful, non-reusable capacity ticket in every required source common consumer through the verified X2D cam_shooter_start_expo path. The ticket accounting cannot exceed available enqueued capacity after reserved camera-free buffers and cannot be replaced by X2D aggregate counters. After hardware dequeue, one concrete buffer object and its positive hardware frame id are bound exactly once to the matching immutable request context before post-processing or persistence. No context may consume two dequeued objects, no object or frame id may belong to two contexts, and timeout, dequeue failure, abort, disconnect, mode switch, storage failure, and delayed callbacks reclaim or invalidate tickets and objects exactly once without allowing an unreserved leaf actuation. Reports must state separately whether capacity reservation and concrete identity binding are proven.
required_evidence: exact official X2D shooter, libdcam framework and camera HAL hashes plus instruction-level call order prove request construction, per-consumer wait_for_enqueued_buffer, and dcam_start_expo

framework decompilation proves availability is computed from cumulative enqueued, requested and camera-free counts, total_request_buf_count advances only after capacity is available, and request-buffer accounting is bounded by the stream maximum

dequeue-path analysis proves the concrete object is obtained from dcam_dequeue after capture and the X2D RAW callback copies frame_buffer+0xb4 into separate queue contexts; no report claims a concrete pre-actuation buffer pointer without additional evidence

final candidate disassembly proves every selected 3, 6 or 9 fps leaf actuation uses the verified ticket path and binds each returned object and frame id once to its own generation and request identity

behavioral tests cover exhaustion, multiple tickets in flight, duplicate or reordered dequeue and FSync, missing buffer, timeout, abort, disconnect, storage failure, delayed old-generation callbacks, counter wrap and exactly-once reclamation

read-only live traces correlate each capacity ticket, native leaf actuation, concrete RAW object, increasing FSync id, sensor result, JLS result, 3FR close and return; any unmatched ticket, actuation, object or frame id blocks release
goals.title: Pre-actuation capacity tickets are not confused with concrete RAW-buffer identity

goals.origin: The P14_9 host-guard audit correctly looked up X2D-RG-073 by id but also required it to remain the final registry entry and hard-coded a total of 73 goals. Appending valid gates 074 through 077 therefore made an unchanged host-guard binary fail for registry ordering rather than for its own behavior. This coupled one historical proof to a temporary registry length and obscured real failures.
goals.required_behavior: Every audit identifies its required historical regression goals by stable id and validates the registry as a unique contiguous sequence whose total is derived from the current file. Appending a new permanent goal must not invalidate an older goal merely because it is no longer last. Tests and reports may record the current final id and count, but must never hard-code them unless the test is specifically proving that exact registry snapshot by hash. A missing, duplicated, reordered, weakened, or content-mismatched required goal still fails closed.
required_evidence: unit tests append a synthetic later goal and prove the historical goal remains discoverable and enforced by id
registry audits derive the contiguous expected id sequence and current total from the exact hash-bound registry
historical gate tests assert the required goal id and behavior rather than assuming it is the terminal row
candidate manifests and audit reports bind the exact current registry hash and are regenerated after any registry change
the full historical regression suite is rerun for every new candidate and no prior goal is removed or silently weakened
goals.title: Historical regression gates remain valid after newer gates are appended

goals.origin: The first host-side P14_9 artifact installed only a response-10 guard and callback. It did not send request 9, wait for the matching acknowledgement, or bind BEGIN and terminal operations to the physical capture lifecycle. Treating callback registration, transport send success, or a locally selected preset as proof that the EXMCU retained sensor state is active would allow a leaf actuation against an unconfirmed or stale remote session and could leave continuous-capture state enabled after a timeout.
goals.required_behavior: Only the exact sanitized P14_9 continuous preset may create a nonzero token and monotonically advancing nonzero generation, arm one guarded BEGIN, send the exact 24-byte request-9 payload, and wait for one matching response-10 acknowledgement with a finite timeout before the first native leaf-shutter actuation. Send success alone is never acceptance. Timeout, malformed or negative acknowledgement, mode switch, release, abort, disconnect, or deinit cancels only the same guarded identity, prevents new actuation, and performs a bounded END or ABORT followed by the stock RestoreLens/request-11 cleanup fallback. Guard BUILDING, READY, or CALLBACK_OWNED state is never blindly cleared or reused. Successful cleanup returns the host and EXMCU session to inactive exactly once while P14_6 and all stock paths remain unchanged.
required_evidence: exact final binary hashes and instruction-level disassembly bind P14_9-only activation, request construction, send call, bounded wait, acknowledgement validation, first-actuation dominance, and terminal cleanup hooks

the request bytes encode version, request id 9, operation, magic, nonzero token, nonzero generation, preset 3, zero flags and reserved bytes, and the response must match the same immutable identity before state activation

instruction and concurrency tests cover send failure, timeout before and during guard publication, delayed old response, duplicate response, negative status, wrong retained state, generation wrap, mode switch, release, abort, disconnect, deinit, RestoreLens failure and bounded retry without unbounded spinning or callback-thread blocking

binary diff and call-target audits prove the sender uses the verified X2Bridge context and _Bridge_SendMsg entry, never a stock command queue alias, and leaves every stock request, response, queue and callback route byte-identical outside declared hooks
behavioral tests prove no capacity reservation or leaf actuation occurs before a valid BEGIN acknowledgement and no new actuation occurs after terminal state begins

read-only live traces bind each BEGIN, END or ABORT request and response to one token and generation, show the first native leaf actuation only after BEGIN acceptance, and show retained state plus lens ownership cleared after every terminal path
goals.title: P14_9 retained mode is acknowledged before the first leaf actuation and tears down boundedly

goals.origin: The first P14_9 session final-binary audit tried to prove that _Bridge_SendMsg preserves x1 and x2 by applying a register-write regular expression to whole Ghidra listing lines. Byte columns and mnemonics preceded the operands, so the expression could miss a real write to the request-pointer or length register while still reporting PASS. The candidate bytes were independently checked elsewhere, but this audit shortcut could not support its stated ABI claim.
goals.required_behavior: Every final-binary ABI or register-preservation claim is evaluated from parsed instruction operands tied to the exact candidate and independent disassembly, not from assembler source, free-form listing lines, or the mere presence of a load or call. The verified Bridge sender must load only the underlying transport object into x0, preserve x1 and x2 until the call, and call the exact decoded transport entry. A write to either forwarded register, a different object-field load, a shifted call target, an unparsed instruction, or disagreement between independent decoders fails closed.
required_evidence: the Ghidra parser records mnemonic and operand fields separately for every audited instruction
the exact pre-call sequence proves x0 is loaded from the verified bridge field while x1 and x2 are never destinations
Capstone and Ghidra agree on every instruction byte, operand role, and decoded call destination in the audited entry
mutation tests write x1 or x2, change the bridge-field offset, shift the call target, and corrupt parsing; each mutation is rejected
the final report binds the exact listing hashes, candidate hash, function boundary, first call target, and parsed pre-call operands
goals.title: Final binary ABI audits parse decoded operands instead of matching formatted text

goals.origin: After appending a permanent regression goal, a full-suite run reached binary-audit tests before the corresponding patch-builder tests had refreshed stale manifests. The same unchanged EXMCU candidate first failed and later passed in one run depending on which test regenerated its manifest. This exposed hidden dependence on mutable generated files and made the result sensitive to test collection order rather than candidate bytes.
goals.required_behavior: Every audit or test that consumes a generated manifest or report either regenerates it from the exact current sources and registry before evaluation or verifies an immutable hash-bound snapshot supplied as an explicit input. Running an audit alone, first in the suite, last in the suite, or after stale outputs exist must produce the same result. Registry changes invalidate and rebuild every dependent manifest and report before any release gate is evaluated; no later test may repair an earlier failure as a side effect.
required_evidence: clean, stale-output, audit-first, builder-first, and randomized-order test runs produce identical candidate hashes and PASS or FAIL results
dependency metadata binds every generated manifest and report to the exact source, registry, upstream binary, and upstream report hashes
round-trip tests compare path-normalized semantic manifests where output paths are intentionally variable and exact bytes everywhere else
tests fail when a stale registry hash or upstream report hash is injected and then pass only after the declared regeneration step
the complete historical suite passes from a clean evidence directory without relying on artifacts rewritten by earlier tests
goals.title: Generated evidence is reproducible and independent of test execution order

goals.origin: The first receiver-overlap design selected hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer_warp at linked address 0x00086c80 because its name appeared to wrap the global-shutter transfer. Exact operation-table and command-dispatch analysis later proved that the production X2D IMX861 still path instead calls imgsys operation +0x48, sensor-interface operation +0x130, hb_exmcu_ops_call_cmd command 0x0c, jump-table case 12 at 0x0008aedc, and the call at 0x0008aee4 into hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer at 0x00086050. A wrapper-only patch would install cleanly while changing no real X2D capture behavior.
goals.required_behavior: Every receiver-overlap or still-transfer modification is anchored to the exact hash-bound production X2D call chain from camx stop exposure through IMX861 imgsys still transfer, hb_exmcu command 0x0c case 12, and the real global-shutter transfer entry. A symbol name, operation-table resemblance, unreachable wrapper, static byte match, or successful package installation is never accepted as proof that the live capture path changed. Every declared hook must have a proven caller and successor on the selected X2D mode, and all non-selected modes remain byte-identical outside those declared hooks.
required_evidence: exact official and candidate librcam hashes bind the imgsys operation table, sensor operation table, hb_exmcu call_cmd switch, case-12 call site, PLT target and real transfer entry
independent disassembly proves the production chain reaches 0x00086050 through command 0x0c and call site 0x0008aee4
the candidate diff contains the intended hooks on the proven production path and no effect is claimed from changing only 0x00086c80 or another unproven wrapper
mutation tests redirect the case-12 target, patch only the unused wrapper, alter the command id, or break one operation-table edge; each mutation fails the audit
read-only live traces show the selected P14_9 session executing the patched production transfer path before any cadence claim is released
goals.title: P14_9 patches the production IMX861 still-transfer route rather than an unused wrapper

goals.origin: The real global-shutter transfer waits for SLVS-EC line reception and reports a line count, while the X2D shooter separately starts RAW stream consumers before actuation, increments one expected-frame counter per shoot, binds the dequeued hardware buffer and frame_buffer+0xb4 id in its RAW callbacks, and decrements the counter only from those callbacks. Continuous-capture finalization waits for both RAW counters before terminal cleanup. Treating a stable line count or a deferred transfer return as if the photo, JLS encoding, 3FR close, or buffer recycling had completed would recreate the earlier no-file, permanent-writing and frame-ownership failures.
goals.required_behavior: P14_9 may defer only the lower receiver wait needed to release the serial stop-exposure path. At most one receiver generation may remain pending. Before the receiver is reused, before terminal END or ABORT, and before interrupt disable or teardown, that exact pending generation must be drained with a bounded wait, return success, and report the expected line count. The deferred call may supply only the immediate line-count contract required by the caller; it must never decrement X2D shooting counters, publish a RAW frame, recycle a buffer, advance JLS or 3FR state, or claim persistence. Actual success remains owned by the existing dequeued RAW callback, positive hardware frame id, per-frame context, downstream completion and file close. Send failure, receiver timeout, line mismatch, missing RAW, mode switch, abort or teardown fails closed and performs bounded recovery without starting another leaf actuation.
required_evidence: exact X2D shooter disassembly proves stream consumers and expected-frame counters are established before cam_shooter_start_expo and only RAW callbacks decrement the two counters
continuous finalizer disassembly proves both real RAW counters are awaited before the terminal message and receiver teardown

final candidate disassembly proves one-generation pending state, bounded drain before reuse and terminal cleanup, expected-line validation, and no call to shooter completion, buffer-release, JLS, 3FR or storage-success functions

instruction and behavioral tests cover first frame, sustained frames, final frame, early release, send failure, delayed receiver, timeout, bad line count, missing RAW callback, duplicate callback, mode switch, abort, deinit and stale generation without fake success or double cleanup

read-only live traces correlate each native leaf actuation with one receiver drain, one concrete RAW buffer and frame id, one shooting-counter decrement, one JLS result and one successful 3FR close before any 9 fps release claim
goals.title: Receiver-drain acknowledgement is never substituted for RAW-frame completion

goals.origin: The first composed v9 candidate carried only the extracted EXMCU payload even though the official programming path sends /etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont. Hash-bound decompilation of official EXMCU FUN_080a21a8 proves that the updater reads a 512-byte container header, requires magic 0xBEEFC0DE, checks the declared payload size, zeroes the checksum field at offset 0x0c, and verifies a CRC across the complete header and payload. Installing a raw payload or reusing a stale official header would therefore fail before the patched firmware could run.
goals.required_behavior: The final v9 system component replaces only /system/etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont with an official-header-compatible container. Its magic, version, type, payload-size field, fixed header layout, and CRC match the recovered production validator; extraction yields the exact audited P14_9 payload. All unused header bytes and every other firmware container remain official. The raw payload is an intermediate input only and is never a package member or programming target. The container remains local-only until package, rollback, and live gates pass.
required_evidence: exact official EXMCU and decompilation hashes bind FUN_080a21a8 to the 512-byte header, magic, payload-size and checksum validation route
the recovered CRC implementation reproduces the stored checksum and exact bytes of the official exMCU_hb722.cont from its extracted payload
candidate round-trip extraction reproduces the exact audited P14_9 payload hash and the final system target is /system/etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont
mutation tests reject altered magic, version, type, payload size, checksum, payload bytes, reserved header padding, and truncation
the composed manifest and package audit contain the validated container but never the standalone raw payload, and every unrelated container remains official
read-only post-install verification binds the active slot file hash, successful container acceptance, EXMCU firmware identity and retained-session trace before release
goals.title: EXMCU payload is wrapped in the validated production container

goals.origin: A Windows connection check searched friendly names and an unrelated VID_2AEF pattern, then reported that no camera was present. Existing hash-bound live discovery evidence and the official USB probe identify this X2D II body as the composite device USB\VID_2756&PID_000B with multiple MI_00 through MI_05 child interfaces. The narrow check could therefore report a connected camera as absent and delay or misroute live verification.
goals.required_behavior: Every live preflight detects the X2D II from its audited parent USB identity USB\VID_2756&PID_000B and all present composite child interfaces, independent of localized or generic friendly names. RNDIS, MTP/PTP, WinUSB and parent-device observations are reported separately and then joined to the same physical USB instance. Absence is reported only after present-device enumeration checks the audited identity; stale saved logs, empty removable-drive letters, a missing friendly name, or failure of one interface class never proves disconnection.
required_evidence: the exact prior live discovery report hash binds USB VID_2756 PID_000B and its observed MI_00 through MI_05 children to the X2D II
the standalone read-only preflight uses Windows present-device enumeration and does not load Phocus, send camera commands, mount storage, or alter USB state
unit tests recognize parent and child identities with blank or generic friendly names and reject unrelated vendor, product and stale non-present instances
the live report records all matched instance ids, interface suffixes, parent identity, timestamp and whether camera absence is conclusive

every later identity, slot, component and runtime-path probe is permitted only after the audited USB identity is presently enumerated or an independently proven direct transport identifies the same body
a future connected run captures the exact present composite interfaces before any package or camera write
goals.title: Live camera presence uses the audited composite USB identity

goals.origin: The historical slot-1 rollback helper proves only four files in the inactive Android system partition and then changes the active-slot metadata. The v9 candidate modifies five Android-side binaries plus exMCU_hb722.cont, while the official hbl-upgrade path programs EXMCU separately through ApplicationUpgrade in addition to running the Android OTA engine. A system-slot switch can therefore leave the patched EXMCU running and cannot by itself prove a complete v9 rollback.
goals.required_behavior: A v9 rollback uses the exact pinned official X2D II 1.3.16.2 CIM, or an independently equivalent and fully proven procedure, to restore both the Android system state and the official EXMCU container. Completion requires the intended official system slot to be active, all five Android-side target hashes to match the official system tree, the official EXMCU container to be accepted and running, and affected persistent capture settings to be returned to a stock-compatible state. Merely switching slots, checking the four historical v8 files, or finding the official container on disk is never reported as complete rollback. No replacement candidate may be installed until this complete route and its post-rollback verification remain available.
required_evidence: the exact official CIM hash, size and internal update artifacts are pinned, including hbl-upgrade, hbl-post-upgrade, program_nodes.sh and the official EXMCU container
script-level evidence proves the official flow runs the Android OTA engine and separately sends exMCU_hb722.cont through ApplicationUpgrade, so a slot-only rollback is explicitly rejected
the verified partition map binds system and system_2 to mmcblk0p16 and mmcblk0p17 without treating either storage slot as the EXMCU target
offline hashes bind the official and candidate camera-gui, camera-service, shooter, camera HAL, librcam and EXMCU container identities

mutation tests reject an omitted shooter, HAL, librcam or EXMCU check, a wrong official CIM, candidate bytes masquerading as official, an incorrect slot map, a missing ApplicationUpgrade step and a system-only rollback declaration

read-only post-rollback verification records active-slot identity, all five Android component hashes, official EXMCU acceptance and runtime identity, stock-compatible persisted capture state, normal UI, single capture and successful 3FR close before rollback is declared complete
goals.title: Rollback restores both the Android system slot and the independent EXMCU state

goals.origin: The first one-shot v9 live attestation sent seven read-only shell commands through the factory TCP tunnel but waited the full 60-second receive timeout after each command even when the camera had already returned its output. A complete six-component identity read therefore appeared stalled and would waste roughly seven minutes. The transport had no explicit end-of-output contract and silence could not distinguish completion from truncation.
goals.required_behavior: Every bounded multi-command live probe appends a unique explicit completion marker whose bytes are included in the factory command-capacity check. The receiver returns as soon as that exact marker is observed, including when it is split across response packets, and never accepts a different, partial or stale marker. Missing markers, no packets, disconnects and truncated output fail closed without promoting partial identity evidence. Only one probe owns a given live attestation session at a time, and early completion never changes camera state or weakens the command read-only allowlist.
required_evidence: unit tests prove immediate return after the exact marker and no additional receive call
fragmentation tests split the marker across two camera response packets and still recognize it exactly once
wrong, partial, missing and stale markers are rejected or remain bounded by the declared timeout
every marked command remains below the recovered SUTEST text capacity and passes the read-only command audit
a connected live run records all six official or candidate component hashes, slot state and EXMCU runtime identity without waiting the old per-command timeout
the report binds the exact probe, registry, camera USB identity and command-output hashes while recording that no capture or camera write occurred
goals.title: Read-only live probes finish on an explicit response marker

goals.origin: The official update has two EXMCU sources: hbl-upgrade sends the outer CIM record exMCU_hb722.cont directly to ApplicationUpgrade before Android boots, while hbl-post-upgrade can recover from /system/etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont. Replacing only the system copy would let the official outer record overwrite the v9 EXMCU during installation and leave installation and recovery using different firmware identities.
goals.required_behavior: Every v9 package carries the exact audited production EXMCU container twice: as the outer encrypted CIM record exMCU_hb722.cont and as /system/etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont in the inactive-slot system image. Both copies must round-trip to the same pinned candidate hash and payload. The raw EXMCU payload is never packaged. Every other outer CIM record and every system byte outside the six audited target files remain official. The official rollback CIM must similarly restore matching official outer and system EXMCU containers.
required_evidence: hash-bound hbl-upgrade evidence identifies the outer exMCU_hb722.cont record as the ApplicationUpgrade input
hash-bound hbl-post-upgrade evidence identifies /system/etc/firmware/exMCU_hb722.cont as the post-boot recovery input
independent CIM decrypt and OTA Brotli round-trip recover both v9 copies and prove their SHA-256 values are identical to the audited production container
system new.dat locality proves that only camera-gui, camera-service, shooter, camera HAL, librcam and the system EXMCU container changed
outer CIM record comparison proves that only ota.zip, hbl-upgrade and exMCU_hb722.cont changed and that the standalone raw EXMCU payload is absent
mutation tests reject a stale official outer EXMCU, a stale official system EXMCU, unequal copies, a raw payload record and any unapproved outer or system change
goals.title: The packaged EXMCU container is identical in the outer CIM and Android system

goals.origin: The first v9 package-builder invocation derived the project root from the reverse directory with one parent level too many and searched for the composed candidate outside the x2d2 workspace. The builder failed before producing bytes, but the error shows that an unchecked path calculation could consume the wrong firmware tree or create artifacts outside the governed project.
goals.required_behavior: Every package, audit and installer entry point resolves the x2d2 project root from its own location or an explicit argument, then verifies the expected AGENTS.md, work/reverse tree, exact official CIM, exact composed manifest and exact regression registry before creating output. No implicit current-directory assumption or unchecked parent count may select inputs. A wrong root fails before any large file is created and can never fall back to another similarly named firmware tree.
required_evidence: unit tests invoke the package builder from unrelated working directories and resolve the same x2d2 root
negative tests reject a root missing AGENTS.md, the official CIM, the composed manifest or the exact registry hash before patching starts
the package report records absolute source and output paths and binds all source hashes
the production invocation proves every generated artifact remains under work/reverse/builds/v9_package_local
no package or camera transport is invoked when root validation fails
goals.title: Package tooling resolves and verifies the actual project root before building

goals.origin: A v9 release run invoked pytest without the established project-only collection boundary. Pytest recursively collected third-party test suites under vendor, producing hundreds of unrelated import errors instead of evaluating the 137 top-level X2D II test modules. The candidate was not promoted, but an ambiguous full-suite command wastes time and can obscure the real release result.
goals.required_behavior: The release regression command collects only the governed top-level X2D II test modules and explicitly excludes vendor, generated builds, extracted runtimes and review artifacts. The saved JUnit report must identify the exact collection boundary, contain no collection errors, and report every project test and subtest with zero failures, errors or skips. A vendor collection failure can never be reported as a candidate regression and a partial project run can never be reported as full.
required_evidence: the release command or checked-in pytest configuration explicitly excludes vendor and other non-project trees
a collection-only test proves all 137 current top-level test modules are included and no nested third-party test module is included
the final JUnit report has zero collection errors, failures and skips and is bound by SHA-256 to the release review
the release report records the test-module count, test-case count and exact command scope
negative tests reject a JUnit report produced by recursive vendor collection or by a subset of top-level project tests
goals.title: The full project regression suite excludes vendored third-party self-tests

goals.origin: The first v9 installation attempt called Phocus UpdateFirmware as if it returned an integer status. Static analysis later proved the export is void and a headless CIM call only validates the file before waiting for a confirmation callback. The call returned immediately, no bytes were transferred, the camera never disconnected, and the unchanged official slot was incorrectly described as a successful installation.
goals.required_behavior: A CIM update is initiated through a verified Phocus confirmation path or an independently proven equivalent transport. A native function return, file validation, package hash, or absence of an exception is never installation success. Success requires visible or protocol-level transfer progress, the expected camera update and USB disconnect/reconnect cycle, and read-only post-reboot attestation of the intended active slot and every candidate component hash. Missing confirmation, transfer, reboot, or matching hashes fails closed as not installed.
required_evidence: static ABI evidence records UpdateFirmware as void and identifies its confirmation callback dependency
installer tests reject any result inferred from a fabricated integer return value or a headless validation-only call
the live record captures user-visible or protocol-level transfer start, monotonic progress, completion and the camera USB transition
post-reboot attestation binds the active slot plus all Android and EXMCU candidate hashes to the exact package hash
timeout, cancelled confirmation, no transfer, no reboot, unchanged official hashes and partial component updates are each reported as not installed
no release or user test is requested from a package that merely exists on the computer or appears in a file picker
goals.title: Firmware installation success requires an observed transfer and post-reboot attestation

goals.origin: A broad calibration-log query scanned a large active blackbox and emitted thousands of lines through the factory TCP shell. The camera shell worker remained occupied after the host timed out, later probes received stale output, and the USB session had to be power-cycled before installation could safely continue.
goals.required_behavior: Every live blackbox query is read-only, narrowly filtered, output-capped, command-capacity checked, and terminated by an exact marker within a finite deadline. Calibration, capture, firmware installation and shutdown never start while a diagnostic worker is active. A timeout quarantines the session: later output is treated as stale, no new command or camera write is issued, and a clean reconnect plus short identity probe is required before installation. The old valid calibration remains untouched when a recalibration attempt fails.
required_evidence: unit tests enforce command capacity, output caps, explicit markers, finite timeouts and stale-response rejection
negative tests simulate a timed-out grep followed by delayed packets and prove they cannot satisfy a later identity or release gate
the live workflow records that no calibration, capture or firmware write overlaps a diagnostic command
after any diagnostic timeout a power-cycle or independently proven worker reset is followed by a small fresh identity response
calibration-failure review verifies the previously installed calibration remains readable and valid before any firmware installation
the installation record binds a clean diagnostic state and contains no inherited blackbox output
goals.title: Live blackbox diagnostics are bounded and never overlap calibration or installation

goals.origin: The first live v9 P16_3 capture reserved internal file B0000265, then the SLVS-EC receiver stopped at 686 lines, raised DCAM_STATUS_STILL_EXPO_SENSOR_ERROR and returned -152. No FullRaw callback or 3FR close existed, while the metadata worker rejected frame id 0 and timed out repeatedly. Treating the reservation or the persistent storing indicator as evidence of a slow SSD sent diagnosis to the wrong subsystem.
goals.required_behavior: Every capture is tracked through separate reservation, sensor-transfer, valid RAW identity, JLS, 3FR close and destination-specific write states. A transfer with fewer than the exact topology line count, a sensor error, -152, invalid frame id or missing FullRaw callback terminates the burst, cancels the reserved storage transaction and reports a pre-RAW capture failure. It is never described as an SSD throughput failure and no later frame may inherit its exposure, frame or metadata identity.
required_evidence: the hash-bound live-forensics report identifies B0000265 as reserved on internal SSD but absent from FullRaw and successful 3FR-close records
the same report binds line count 686, DCAM_STATUS_STILL_EXPO_SENSOR_ERROR, -152, rejected metadata frame id 0 and the subsequent metadata-queue timeout series
behavior tests inject each pre-RAW failure and prove capture stops, the reservation is cancelled, pending-save returns to zero and no 3FR is advertised
frame-identity tests prove a reset frame or later valid RAW cannot be paired with the failed exposure metadata
a live validation records the exact expected line count, valid FullRaw identity, JLS completion and 3FR close for every accepted P16_3 frame
goals.title: A sensor-transfer failure cannot be misreported as a storage failure

goals.origin: After the failed B0000265 attempt, B0000266 through B0000270 each produced a valid FullRaw and successful 3FR close, but all five paths were /mnt/media_rw/TETHERED/100HASBL while Phocus controlled capture storage. The camera browse view remained on the internal SSD, so completed tethered photos appeared to the user as missing internal files.
goals.required_behavior: Capture validation records and reports the actual destination for every exposure. Internal SSD, CFexpress and tethered writers are separate outcomes. A successful TETHERED close proves photo formation and host transfer only; it never satisfies an internal-storage gate. A standalone camera mode must select an available camera-local destination before capture, and disconnecting Phocus must not leave a stale tethered route.
required_evidence: the hash-bound live-forensics report proves five FullRaw plus successful 3FR closes on TETHERED and zero internal-SSD closes for B0000266 through B0000270
tests classify identical filenames by their concrete writer path and reject a destination-agnostic success counter
mode-transition tests cover Phocus connect, tethered capture, disconnect and return to internal SSD without stale routing
the UI displays or browses the same concrete destination that owns the completed file
live standalone validation proves every expected file closes under /mnt/media_rw/ssd or the explicitly selected CFexpress volume
goals.title: Tethered completion never counts as an internal-storage save

goals.origin: The live v9 build installed receiver-overlap hooks inside hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer, a common function also reached by P16_3. Although helper branches intended to emulate stock behavior when 9fps was not selected, the first 16-bit capture stopped at 686 rather than the normal 690 receiver lines. Intentional fallbacks and static branch checks were insufficient proof that the stock path was unchanged.
goals.required_behavior: P16_3, P14_3, single shot, preview and every non-P14_9 path execute the exact official transfer instructions, ordering and receiver ownership without entering an experimental helper. P14_9 dispatch occurs before the official transfer entry or through a separately relocated function whose selection is explicit and hash-bound. A condition inside a globally patched stock transfer is not accepted as isolation.
required_evidence: binary locality proves the official transfer function bytes are identical for the complete non-P14_9 route
runtime tracing proves non-P14_9 captures never enter overlap state, deferred wait, retained IRQ or experimental drain helpers
differential emulation covers success, timeout, error, abort, mode switch and disconnect against the exact official function
live P16_3 and P14_3 captures each receive the exact topology line count and complete RAW-to-3FR closure before P14_9 is enabled
mutation tests reject any candidate whose experimental hook remains in a common transfer function even when guarded by a preset check
goals.title: Experimental 9fps transfer code is absent from nonselected capture paths

goals.origin: The v9 backend combined the official 16-bit group-0 topology with the stock SlowBurst state and a new option-12 loop, then described it as a stock per-frame native path. That combination does not exist in the official firmware. The live failure showed that changing the stream group and looping the SlowBurst graph is not proof of a valid 16-bit continuous transaction.
goals.required_behavior: P16_3 is implemented as an explicit repeated native 16-bit leaf-shutter transaction derived from the official successful single-shot sequence. Every frame performs the required exposure, readout, RAW identity, processing ownership and terminal acknowledgement before the next permitted actuation. The loop stops immediately on any incomplete stage. The 3fps label is accepted only after measured cadence; until then the exact measured rate is reported.
required_evidence: a function-level map proves StateGroupStillSession constructs both official StateCaptureSingleContinuous option 5 and StateCaptureSlowBurst option 4 graphs, and identifies the exact ready-state sequence selector
the P16-only selector changes exactly the checkReadyForCapture callsite from official drive 6 to sequence 0 while every other caller still receives the byte-identical global sessionDriveMode result
no manifest or UI audit calls the mixed SlowBurst plus group-0 route stock or proven
behavior tests prove next-frame admission depends on valid prior RAW identity and all mandatory leaf and receiver acknowledgements
two-frame then sustained offline harnesses preserve unique exposure, frame, metadata and buffer ownership and stop cleanly on every injected fault
binary-diff tests prove the complete official SlowBurst constructor, option 4, normal completion target and buffer-wait entry remain byte-identical and that no option-12 helper is emitted
live validation starts with two complete 16-bit frames, then measures sustained cadence while proving every 3FR closes on the selected local destination
goals.title: P16_3 uses a proven repeated native leaf-shutter transaction

goals.origin: The first v9 menu helper reversed the data and length registers for QString::fromUtf8(QByteArrayView). The installed menu therefore displayed the unrelated cloned text No Lens instead of the four burst choices and invoked undefined behavior in the UI process. QML presence and a successful binary patch did not validate the runtime string object.
goals.required_behavior: Every injected burst label constructs a valid QString with x0 holding the UTF-8 data pointer, x1 holding the exact byte length and x8 holding return storage for the audited AArch64 overload. The runtime menu contains exactly 16-bit 3fps, 14-bit 3fps, 14-bit 6fps and 14-bit 9fps with values 0 through 3, and no cloned source label survives.
required_evidence: instruction-level tests assert the exact argument registers, UTF-8 lengths, return storage and destructor ordering for all four labels
binary round-trip and independent audit bind the corrected camera-gui hash and every emitted string byte
a behavioral harness constructs and destroys every option repeatedly without invalid memory access or unrelated text
runtime menu-model inspection proves the four exact labels and values rather than relying on a screenshot of the QML shell
touching every option proves the selected value reaches persistence and the matching backend route
goals.title: Burst-menu QString construction follows the exact AArch64 ABI

goals.origin: The v9 live log recorded 75 fatal camera-service cycles with QSettings::FormatError followed by camera.ini no profile loaded yet. The saved short camera.ini contains only reset stubs plus an unexpected D/t entry and lacks the normal Default settings. The logs prove malformed or truncated persisted state and a crash loop, but do not identify which process or interrupted write created the file.
goals.required_behavior: Burst-preset persistence uses the existing supported settings owner and an atomic replace protocol. Startup validates the complete camera.ini before publishing it; malformed, truncated, unknown or interrupted files are quarantined and replaced from a valid backup or safe defaults without a fatal restart loop. The implementation does not claim a specific writer as root cause unless trace evidence identifies it.
required_evidence: the hash-bound forensic report records both saved camera.ini files, QSettings format failures and fatal no-profile cycles without inventing the writer
power-loss and torn-write tests interrupt every write boundary and always leave either the old complete file or the new complete file
exact-hash Qt runtime analysis proves QSettings atomic sync is enabled by default, SettingStore calls sync, and no candidate path disables atomic sync
mutation tests cover truncation, duplicate or malformed sections, invalid values, missing Default data and unrelated engineering keys
startup recovery quarantines the bad file, loads a safe profile once and keeps camera-service stable without repeated fatal exits
live restart and power-cycle validation preserve the selected 0-through-3 preset and all ordinary camera settings
goals.title: Burst-setting persistence is atomic and malformed camera.ini recovers safely

goals.origin: The composed v9 set with camera-gui 72b6d765, camera-service 90966133, shooter 4bb64c72, HAL 61f7f361, librcam 536122f8 and EXMCU container 22753a26 was installed and produced the No Lens UI, malformed settings startup loop and a 16-bit pre-RAW transfer failure. Keeping its old package and installer callable creates a risk of accidental reinstallation after official recovery.
goals.required_behavior: Every builder, packager and installer rejects the exact live-failed component set and any package containing it. Historical artifacts remain available only as forensic evidence and are visibly marked revoked and non-installable. A replacement version receives new component and package hashes and cannot inherit PASS results from this set.
required_evidence: a checked-in revocation registry binds all six failed component hashes plus the old composed manifest and package identities
unit tests prove builders, package audits and camera installers reject the revoked set before any camera contact or output package creation
existing historical directories are marked forensic-only without deleting evidence
all replacement reports bind the new registry hash and rerun every applicable regression goal from X2D-RG-001 onward
read-only live attestation proves official recovery or a later fully qualified component set before any user test
goals.title: The live-failed v9 component set is permanently revoked

goals.origin: During the v9 replacement review, three external-component hashes in the new backend report were copied from a live-summary note rather than recomputed from the local official 1.3.16.2 files. The camera-service output binary was unaffected, but the evidence manifest incorrectly identified the official HAL, librcam and EXMCU container until an independent file-hash test caught it.
goals.required_behavior: Every source, unchanged external component, candidate component and package identity is computed directly from the exact file named in the same report. A hash copied from prose, a prior report, a live prefix or another component class is never accepted. Tests compare the complete declared mapping against fresh hashes of all named files and reject a mismatch before composition, packaging or camera contact.
required_evidence: the backend test independently reads and hashes the official camera GUI, X2D shooter, camera HAL, librcam and EXMCU container instead of comparing a constant to itself
the report records the full source path, size and complete 64-character SHA-256 for every identity
mutation tests change each source file or declared hash in turn and fail before any output set is composed
the composed review recomputes every component hash again and does not reuse a layer manifest value without checking the file
live attestation distinguishes on-camera file hashes, container hashes and payload hashes and never substitutes one class for another
goals.title: Every declared official component hash is recomputed from the exact source file

goals.origin: The first SingleContinuous audit decoded the complete executable segment as one stream. Embedded data or an undecodable word stopped Capstone before the real call at 0x16b090, so the report incorrectly claimed StateCaptureSingleContinuous had no direct caller even though StateGroupStillSession constructs it. That false negative hid the official option-5 route and encouraged unnecessary custom state-machine work.
goals.required_behavior: Every release-relevant direct-call audit decodes bounded function bodies or every aligned four-byte word in the ELF .text section, records the owning symbol, and cross-checks constructor calls against an independent exact disassembly or decompile. An empty caller set is never accepted when another artifact contains a conflicting call. The official hash-bound map must retain the StateGroupStillSession calls to both StateCaptureSingleContinuous and StateCaptureSlowBurst and the exact ready-state selector call.
required_evidence: the corrected audit binds official camera-service SHA-256 and reports the direct SingleContinuous call at 0x16b090 owned by StateGroupStillSession
the same audit reports the direct SlowBurst construction and option values 5 and 4 from exact instructions
the ready-state report binds the sessionDriveMode call at 0x16cf8c, official drive-6 sequence 1 and default sequence 0
unit tests fail if any caller, owner, option, call target or switch mapping changes
release review rejects a stale route report with an empty caller list or the old v1 schema
goals.title: AArch64 capture-route call discovery cannot stop at embedded data

goals.origin: The retired P14_9 receiver-overlap prototype returned success from hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer before slec_wait_end_receiving completed and wrote the expected 690-line count into the caller output. The upper IMX861 still-transfer function therefore accepted a frame whose RAW data and physical completion were still pending. This can advance FSync, metadata, JLS and 3FR ownership without a formed photo and exactly matches the observed shutter-actuation-without-storage failure class.
goals.required_behavior: No capture path may publish a successful sensor-transfer return, expected line count, valid RAW identity or releasable buffer until the physical receiver has completed that exact generation and its result, line count, hardware frame identity and sensor status have all been validated. P14_9 may overlap leaf preparation or independently owned receiver generations, but it may not emulate synchronous success. Every asynchronous completion must rejoin the exact request and exposure context before JLS or 3FR admission; timeout, mismatch, early return or missing ownership fails closed and cancels the reservation.
required_evidence: binary audit proves no helper stores the expected 690-line count or returns zero as a substitute for slec_wait_end_receiving completion
the official synchronous transfer function remains byte-identical on all non-P14_9 paths and any P14_9 dispatch occurs before its entry or in a separately owned implementation
a per-generation model binds request id, exposure id, hardware FSync frame id, receiver result, exact line count, RAW buffer, JLS completion and 3FR close before buffer release
negative tests delay or omit receiver completion and prove the upper IMX861 transfer, FullRaw callback, JLS and 3FR writer cannot observe success
mutation tests recreate the retired fake-line-count and early-zero-return sequence and require the release gate to fail
live validation records physical receiver completion before FullRaw, JLS and destination-specific 3FR close for every accepted frame
goals.title: Sensor transfer completion cannot be synthesized before physical RAW receipt

goals.origin: The withdrawn long-lived-session prototype changed the common SlowBurst graph and therefore allowed an experimental repeat path to affect 16-bit and stock 14-bit capture. A preset check inside shared code is not sufficient isolation after the live storage regression.
goals.required_behavior: P14_6 and P14_9 use a separately constructed, separately validated capture-state instance. The official SingleContinuous, SlowBurst, common exposure-session transitions and common buffer-wait entry remain byte-identical. The private route is published only after every expected child, transition and target is validated at runtime; any mismatch leaves the official P14_3 route active and makes high-speed presets unavailable.
required_evidence: binary audit proves the complete official SingleContinuous and SlowBurst constructors plus common exposure-session and buffer-wait code are byte-identical
runtime graph validation proves the private state has the expected child counts, normal and error transition targets, private wait object and private vtable before its ready flag is published
route tests prove preset 0 selects only official sequence 0, preset 1 only official sequence 1, and presets 2 or 3 select the private sequence only when its ready flag is true
failure injection at every allocation, child lookup and transition check leaves the private ready flag false and falls back to official P14_3 behavior without a dangling transition
release tests prove mode switching, shutter release, buffer backpressure, error, timeout and teardown stop or finalize exactly once without leaking state into a later capture
goals.title: High-speed P14 state is isolated from official P16 and P14_3 graphs

goals.origin: The first P14_6 candidate only staged the next leaf-shutter preparation. It did not retain the upper exposure session or impose a six-frame cadence, so a future long-lived loop could run near the selected sensor source rate while the UI falsely reported 6fps.
goals.required_behavior: The 14-bit 6fps preset uses a proven production-compatible native XCD leaf-shutter and sensor timing path or a nonblocking monotonic admission gate that targets 166.667 milliseconds per accepted frame. It never derives truth from a menu label, test-only sensor name, blocking UI-thread sleep or the nominal 9fps source. Every admitted frame still completes physical RAW receipt, identity binding, JLS, 3FR close and buffer return.
required_evidence: a hash-bound production mode map proves whether IMX861_11K9K_14b_M0_B_6P is reachable through the retail cam-info, topology, EXMCU and leaf-shutter path rather than merely present in engineering JSON
if native 6P is not fully proven, an audited nonblocking monotonic timer gate enforces the six-frame cadence without sleeping or blocking the camera-service or UI event loop
offline scheduling tests cover early and late completions, clock wrap, release, error, thermal stop and buffer pressure without bursts faster than the configured budget
binary and runtime traces prove preset 2 cannot execute preset 3 cadence and preset 3 cannot inherit a six-frame limiter
live stored-file measurements bind lens acknowledgements, FSync, receiver completion, RAW identity, JLS completion, 3FR close and returned buffers for every frame before the 6fps label is released
goals.title: P14_6 has a proven native six-frame-per-second cadence

goals.origin: Retail cam-info proves that TPLG_IMX861BQR_STILL_14BIT selects the B_5P descriptor whose declared rate is 6.00fps, but the matching production configuration keeps both dsp_fast_preview_rltm and async_dsp_rgrg in noncontinuous mode. Routing sustained P14_6 directly to that graph would repeat the same capture-versus-storage mismatch that previously left actuations without formed 3FR files.
goals.required_behavior: A sustained P14_6 route uses a processing graph whose complete RAW, DSP, JLS and 3FR path is explicitly continuous and whose buffer ownership is independently validated. The stock B_5P topology is not selected merely because its sensor descriptor says 6.00fps while its production processing flags remain noncontinuous. Until a complete continuous B_5P clone is proven, P14_6 uses the isolated H_9P continuous graph with a nonblocking six-fps admission gate.
required_evidence: the hash-bound production-mode audit maps the stock STILL_14BIT topology to B_5P and records both noncontinuous processing flags
the same audit maps STILL_14BIT_HS to H_9P and records both continuous processing flags
binary route tests prove P14_6 cannot select the stock B_5P graph unless a separately named continuous clone and its complete topology hash are present
buffer-pressure tests prove each accepted P14_6 RAW generation reaches valid JLS and destination-specific 3FR close before its buffer is reusable
mutation tests flip either required continuous flag or route P14_6 to group 1 and require the release gate to fail
live validation measures stored files rather than shutter sounds and proves no pending-save, metadata or buffer ownership survives release, error or mode switch
goals.title: P14_6 cannot reuse a noncontinuous production processing graph

goals.origin: The isolated P14_6/P14_9 state machine is larger than every remaining audited executable cave in camera-service. Reusing an arbitrary function, converting the writable data segment to RWX, consuming the interpreter or note bytes, or silently replacing an existing program-header role would create a new loader and recovery risk unrelated to capture performance.
goals.required_behavior: Additional helper code occupies a separately mapped read-execute PT_LOAD with no writable permission and no overlap with any official load range. The expanded program-header table, interpreter string, Android and GNU notes, PHDR coverage, GNU EH frame, GNU stack, RELRO and every original PT_LOAD remain semantically intact. Mutable helper state occupies only a bounded zero-initialized extension of the existing read-write BSS. Exact section and program-header relocation is reversible, hash-bound and accepted only after independent parser, mapping and package round-trip checks.
