required_evidence: a byte-exact inventory proves the foundation has insufficient audited executable cave space and records every remaining zero-filled run
independent ELF parsing proves the new RX segment is page-aligned, non-writable, nonoverlapping and within AArch64 direct-branch range of both hooks
the interpreter and complete original PT_NOTE payload are copied byte-for-byte, their program headers and section headers point to the mapped copies, and the enlarged PT_PHDR covers every entry
all original load permissions, GNU EH frame, GNU stack and GNU RELRO headers remain unchanged except for the explicitly bounded RW BSS memsz extension

mutation tests reject RWX permission, overlapping file or virtual ranges, stale phnum or PHDR size, broken interpreter or notes, section-header disagreement, oversized code and any byte changed outside declared spans plus appended payload
the package round-trip reproduces the exact extended binary without stripping the appended segment, and rollback restores the exact official camera-service hash
goals.title: Injected high-speed code cannot overwrite or weaken official ELF loader metadata

goals.origin: A private Qt state, cloned vtable and delayed callback outlive the instruction that creates them. An allocation failure, constructor exception, state-machine rebuild or delayed callback after state exit could otherwise leave a dangling object, unwind through helper code with no registered frame metadata, or re-enter a later exposure generation.
goals.required_behavior: Every helper allocation is nonthrowing or is covered by valid registered unwind and cleanup metadata; no C++ exception may cross an injected frame that the runtime cannot unwind. The private state remains unreachable until construction, graph validation, transition mutation, vtable cloning and all transitions succeed. Entry and exit invalidate delayed generations, QObject context ownership cancels callbacks on destruction, and both destructor forms clear the published route before delegating to the exact official destructor. Rebuilding the state machine cannot reuse stale pointers or callbacks.
required_evidence: binary audit proves each injected call is either statically nonthrowing, uses a checked nothrow allocation, or lies inside registered unwind coverage with a tested cleanup landing path
failure injection at every allocation and constructor boundary leaves the private route unpublished and the official states usable
vtable audit proves private entry, exit and both destructor routes preserve the AArch64 ABI and delegate to the exact official functions once
timer tests cover exit, destruction, reconstruction, release and mode change between scheduling and invocation and reject every stale generation
address-sanitized or equivalent host harnesses prove no use-after-free, double delete, leaked transition or stale global pointer across repeated state-machine construction and teardown
live restart and mode-cycle validation shows the official route remains available after any private initialization failure
goals.title: Injected session initialization and timer callbacks are lifetime and exception safe

goals.origin: The first isolated route helper selected private sequence 8 whenever the saved preset was 2 or 3. Because the preset persists while the user can switch to single shot, interval, bracketing, self timer or other drive modes, that check alone would have redirected unrelated captures into the high-speed state.
goals.required_behavior: Private sequence 8 is selectable only when the official ready-state selector has already resolved the current drive mode to stock SlowBurst sequence 1, the private graph is release-published ready, and the current preset is exactly P14_6 or P14_9. Every other official sequence remains unchanged regardless of the persisted preset value.
required_evidence: instruction audit proves the private route tests official sequence 1 before reading the private ready flag or preset
exhaustive route tests cover every official sequence value with all four saved presets and select sequence 8 only for the two allowed combinations
mutation tests remove or invert the sequence-1 guard and require the release gate to fail
UI mode-cycle tests preserve the saved preset while switching through single, interval, bracketing, timer and continuous modes without changing their official routes
live validation proves a saved 6fps or 9fps preference does not alter any non-continuous shutter action or storage transaction
goals.title: A saved high-speed preset cannot hijack non-continuous drive modes

goals.origin: The first isolated high-speed session implementation added a 167/167/166ms upper-state admission gate for P14_6 and no software limiter for P14_9. That alone cannot establish either rate: the successful official XCD trace still spends about 274-275ms in each physical exposure sequence and about 169ms from FSync through RAW transfer. Selecting the H_9P sensor graph or scheduling the next Qt state sooner does not prove that the lens, EXMCU, receiver and storage path accepted another formed frame.
goals.required_behavior: The 14-bit 6fps and 14-bit 9fps UI choices are enabled and described as working only when the same hash-bound candidate contains a complete native XCD leaf-shutter schedule for that rate and proves it through physical FSync, exact receiver completion, RAW identity, JLS completion, destination-specific 3FR close and buffer return. An upper-state timer is only an admission ceiling; it cannot create or prove physical cadence. A requested frame that is late, unformed, mismatched, dropped or not closed to storage must reduce or stop admission rather than being counted toward the advertised rate.
required_evidence: the composed manifest maps each visible preset through UI persistence, camera-service state selection, sensor topology, EXMCU and lens commands, receiver generation, JLS and 3FR close in one exact component set
offline schedule tests model the measured 274-275ms official leaf sequence and 169ms transfer dependency and reject a 6fps or 9fps claim when only the upper-state timer or H_9P source rate changes
P14_6 evidence proves the next lens preparation is safely overlapped, consumed once and finally restored without beginning the next physical exposure before the exact prior dependencies permit it

P14_9 evidence proves every additional overlap generation has independent request, exposure, FSync, RAW-buffer and completion ownership; absence of that implementation keeps the 9fps choice unavailable
live sustained traces measure accepted stored files rather than shutter sounds and show equal exposure, receiver, RAW, JLS, 3FR-close and buffer-return counts at the claimed cadence
mutation tests remove the physical scheduler, receiver join or stored-file completion while retaining the UI label and require release failure
goals.title: A burst-rate label requires the matching end-to-end physical leaf-shutter cadence

goals.origin: The injected-code runtime harness originally recorded only the first page of a multi-page executable extension. A failure-path stub placed on a later page then attempted to map an already mapped page, preventing the intended constructor and callback exception tests from running even though the production extension itself was fully mapped.
goals.required_behavior: Every executable page in an appended segment is enumerated exactly once by the instruction harness before any helper or stub is installed. Failure-path tests must execute helpers located on the first, interior and last mapped pages without remapping, silently skipping or shadowing production bytes.
required_evidence: the harness derives its mapped-page set from the exact appended segment virtual address and memory size rather than a single extension base page
mapping audit rejects partial coverage, duplicate mapping and any executable page outside the declared segment
runtime tests execute representative helpers or stubs on the first, interior and last executable pages
mutation testing restores single-page bookkeeping and requires the failure-path suite to fail before candidate acceptance
the report binds page coverage to the exact appended segment size and candidate binary hash
goals.title: Instruction harness must model every page of an appended executable segment

goals.origin: The repeated state-machine lifetime audit found that HelperMachine.run installed a new Unicorn code hook on every invocation but never removed the previous hook. Reusing one emulated process could therefore dispatch the same external call multiple times, hide a double callback, or make an exactly-once teardown assertion depend on how many earlier helpers had run.
goals.required_behavior: Each emulated run owns exactly one bounded code hook and removes it in a finally path after success, stop, assertion, or emulator error. Reusing the same HelperMachine must execute each stub and stop target exactly once per run, with no callbacks, counters, register writes, or stop reasons inherited from an earlier invocation.
required_evidence: the runtime harness retains the hook handle returned for one run and removes that exact handle in a finally block
same-machine repetition invokes one external stub exactly once on every iteration and leaves no increasing callback multiplier
an exception raised by a stub still removes the hook before the next run
mutation testing omits hook removal and requires the repeated-run assertion to fail
the report binds the reusable-harness result to the exact helper code, appended-segment inventory and candidate binary hash
goals.title: A reusable instruction harness cannot accumulate stale execution hooks

goals.origin: After X2D-RG-111 was added, three active v9 layer builders declared the required range through X2D-RG-111 but still wrote goal_count 110. The composed test happened to count the registry dynamically, so stale layer metadata could survive until a later composition or review and make one binary appear bound to two different gate sets.
goals.required_behavior: Every builder, layer report, composed manifest and test derives the regression goal count, ordered range, last goal and registry SHA-256 from the same exact registry bytes used for that candidate. No hard-coded count may disagree with the declared last goal, and a new gate invalidates every stale manifest until it is rebuilt and rerun.
required_evidence: each active builder parses the exact registry and derives goal_count and last_goal instead of carrying an independent stale count
tests require ordered contiguous ids from X2D-RG-001 through the declared last goal and require goal_count to equal that list length
the composed review recomputes the registry hash and rejects any layer whose count, range, last goal or hash differs
mutation tests change only the declared count, range, last goal or registry hash and require failure before packaging or camera contact
all previous build manifests become stale evidence after this gate and cannot be reused for a new candidate
goals.title: Release metadata cannot disagree with the regression registry

goals.origin: The live-failed P14_9 prototype released the serial stop-exposure task by returning zero and writing a synthetic 690-line count while the SLVS-EC receive was still in flight. The replacement design needs nonblocking scheduling, but using the ordinary success value at any layer would recreate the unformed-RAW and missing-3FR failure even if the later drain logic were otherwise correct.
goals.required_behavior: A deferred P14_9 receive uses a distinct nonzero internal PENDING value from the production transfer call through the IMX861 transfer validator. Only the CAPSEQ scheduler may recognize that value as permission to prepare the next native leaf-shutter exposure; it never becomes sensor success, a completed RAW, a JLS admission, a 3FR close or a releasable buffer. Before receiver reuse or session teardown, the exact pending generation must return a real receiver result and exact line count; mismatch or timeout enters the official sensor-reset failure path and stops further admission.
required_evidence: binary audit proves the deferred helper never stores 690 into the caller line-count pointer and never returns zero for a pending generation
instruction tests trace the same distinct PENDING value through the production command-12 call, IMX861 validator and CAPSEQ-only branch without reaching the ordinary sensor-success branch
the next transfer drains the previous generation before enabling receiver reuse and accepts only a real zero result plus exactly 690 observed lines
686 lines, timeout, duplicate pending publication, stale epoch and generation mismatch all enter failure or abort without a RAW, JLS or 3FR completion event
official P16_3, P14_3 and P14_6 paths tail-call the original synchronous receiver and cannot observe the P14_9 PENDING value
mutation tests restore the retired early-zero return or synthetic line write and require the complete release gate to fail
goals.title: Deferred receiver work is never reported as sensor or photo success

goals.origin: The first composed v9 receiver-integrity audit sliced librcam.so with a disassembly virtual address as though it were a file offset. The executable PT_LOAD segment has a nonzero virtual base, so the check compared unrelated bytes and could falsely report a protected receiver function as unchanged.
goals.required_behavior: Every binary comparison, hook inspection, mutation and protected-function audit resolves each virtual address through the exact candidate ELF program headers before reading file bytes. An unmapped address, non-file-backed range, segment crossing or direct virtual-address slice is a hard release failure.
required_evidence: the shared ELF resolver translates the protected function start and every hook to the expected file offsets in both official and candidate binaries
function-range audits compare the mapped file-backed bytes and allow changes only at the explicitly declared instruction addresses
tests prove the virtual address differs from its file offset for librcam.so and still identify the intended instruction bytes
mutation tests use a direct virtual-address slice and require the audit to detect that it examined the wrong bytes
all hash, disassembly and patch-span evidence records both virtual address and resolved file offset
goals.title: ELF virtual addresses are never used as raw file offsets

goals.origin: The first fail-closed P14_9 draft drained the final receiver generation from a finalize sentinel that the shooter sent only after two _wait_shoot_done calls. A malformed last frame produces no RAW completion, so the shooter could wait for up to its retry limit before ever reaching the drain that diagnoses the missing frame.
goals.required_behavior: When a P14_9 continuous session ends or aborts with a receiver generation pending, the shooter requests the lower finalize/drain transaction before either upper _wait_shoot_done call. A successful early drain then preserves both official RAW waits and the ordinary final message. Other presets retain the exact official order. If the early finalize transaction repeatedly fails, the path skips impossible RAW waits, enters the existing final-message error handling, and never reports a stored photograph.
required_evidence: binary audit proves the P14_9-only early-finalize hook executes before both official _wait_shoot_done call sites
the early helper is gated by the distinct P14_9 session marker and P16_3, P14_3 and P14_6 replay the original first wait instruction directly
instruction tests cover early-drain success, non-P14_9 bypass, bounded retry, retry exhaustion and the unchanged later official finalize message
a malformed last-frame model proves the drain runs and returns failure without waiting for an absent RAW completion
mutation tests move the drain after either RAW wait or remove the P14_9 gate and require release failure
goals.title: The final deferred frame is drained before upper RAW waits

goals.origin: A historical P14_9 session builder pointed at a mutable v9_leaf_6fps_r2_local directory. A later rebuild replaced its camera-service foundation, so an unchanged historical audit could no longer reproduce its candidate and failed before testing behavior. The original session output and byte-complete patch manifest survived, allowing the lost foundation to be recovered only after reversing every declared patch.
goals.required_behavior: Every historical regression layer consumes an immutable exact-hash foundation. If an original foundation is missing, a deterministic fail-closed reconstruction must bind the forensic output and manifest by hash, verify every non-overlapping after-anchor, reverse only the declared equal-size spans, and require the recovered binary to match the original foundation hash. Mutable current-build directories may never serve as historical inputs.
required_evidence: the forensic session output and its original manifest are preserved under immutable hash-bound names
reconstruction verifies the exact patch label set, rejects overlaps, checks every after-anchor and reproduces the declared original foundation SHA-256
tampering with the forensic output, manifest, patch set, offset, before bytes, after bytes or expected foundation hash fails before any historical candidate is rebuilt
historical builders reference the reconstructed immutable directory rather than a mutable current-build directory
running historical audits alone, before or after current candidate builds, produces the same byte-exact result
goals.title: Historical foundations are immutable or exactly reconstructible

goals.origin: The complete project suite could report every assertion as passing while repeatedly printing Windows access-violation traces from Unicorn memory mapping. Test modules were inserting different dependency roots and the process loaded the unvalidated 2.1.4 runtime instead of the project-pinned 2.0.1 runtime, making the otherwise green result noisy and ambiguous.
goals.required_behavior: Before any test module is collected, the suite verifies and loads one exact-hash Unicorn Python binding and native library. Every in-process emulator must use that same module identity and version even if a historical module later changes sys.path. A mismatched, missing or already-loaded foreign runtime is a hard collection failure; an incompatible emulator must run in an isolated subprocess rather than contaminate the release process.
required_evidence: the root test bootstrap verifies the exact hashes of the pinned Unicorn package entrypoint, binding and native DLL before importing it
runtime tests prove the loaded module is version 2.0.1 from the governed vendor directory and remains the same object after the legacy dependency path is inserted first
a clean subprocess repeatedly maps and executes representative ARM and ARM64 pages with the pinned runtime and emits no fatal-exception or access-violation signature
mutation tests reject a foreign module path, wrong version or changed pinned file hash before project tests execute
the complete top-level regression suite passes with no native exception signature in its captured output
goals.title: The complete regression suite uses one pinned emulator runtime without native exception contamination

goals.origin: The first full-log capture-chain analyzer keyed every event only by numeric frame_id. X2D II reuses frame numbers after camera-service restart, and unrelated receiver line-count messages can arrive after a completed RAW. The analyzer therefore contaminated the successful frame 345 for B0000266 with an older failed instance and falsely classified a known complete tethered photo as unformed.
goals.required_behavior: Every live capture verdict scopes a sensor frame by at least camera-service process or boot/session identity plus numeric frame_id, then joins it to the matching exposure_id, capture name and destination. A later or earlier reuse of the same numeric frame_id, delayed EXMCU trace, log rotation, unrelated sensor-mode line count, preview, reservation, or adjacent timestamp can never supply or remove a RAW, JLS, 3FR-close or buffer-return event for another capture instance.
required_evidence: the capture-chain analyzer records a unique instance key containing process or boot/session identity and numeric frame_id for every native sensor FSync
a regression fixture places a failed 686-line frame 345 before a successful frame 345 from a restarted camera-service and proves the successful capture remains independently complete
receiver line counts are accepted only while the matching RAW receive is active and line-count messages after RAW completion, timeout or sensor error cannot contaminate the closed frame
explicit exposure_id-to-frame and exposure_id-to-filename joins take precedence over file adjacency or outer log timestamps, which may be delayed for EXMCU traces
the saved B0000265 failure resolves to 686-line unformed frame 599 followed by blocked frames while B0000266 independently resolves to a complete tethered RAW-to-3FR chain
mutation tests restore global numeric-frame indexing or accept post-completion line counts and require the live-evidence gate to fail
goals.title: Live capture evidence is joined by scoped identity rather than a reused frame number

goals.origin: The first current-camera capture-chain export requested 4000 filtered blackbox lines and invoked the TCP test transport without its completion-marker stop condition. The camera remained healthy, but the read-only request reached its 45-second deadline without returning the unique marker, so no local evidence file was accepted.
goals.required_behavior: Every live diagnostic command has a strict remote-output bound that fits the audited transport budget and passes its unique completion marker into the receive loop. A stale marker from an older request, a missing current marker, oversized output, partial response or timeout is rejected without producing evidence or changing camera state.
required_evidence: the capture-chain preset reads a bounded recent source window and returns no more than 800 filtered lines containing every native RAW-to-3FR stage token
the diagnostic caller passes the same unpredictable marker both in the shell command and as the transport receive stop condition
tests reject a delayed marker from an older request and accept only exactly one current marker across split response packets
the live read-only capture-chain export completes within its timeout and records byte count, response packet count and SHA-256
mutation tests remove the transport stop marker or restore the 4000-line output bound and require the diagnostic gate to fail
the diagnostic report and command audit both prove that no capture, setting, slot, package or camera write occurred
goals.title: Live capture diagnostics are bounded and close on their unique marker

goals.origin: The retained v9 Phocus helper still declared release approval for the permanently revoked six-component package and assumed slot 1 was active while the restored camera was actually running the official system from slot 2. Reusing or bypassing that stale path could attribute old evidence to the corrected five-component candidate or aim a fixed system_2 OTA at the active partition.
goals.required_behavior: Every deployment preflight binds the exact current five-component hashes, current regression registry and current manifest, permanently rejects the revoked six-component package, derives active and inactive slots from a fresh read-only attestation, and proves the package target is the inactive slot. A fixed slot-2 package presented while slot 2 is active is blocked before transfer; changing the active slot requires a separate read-only proof that the preserved slot is exact official firmware. Missing live evidence or a local-only candidate never becomes package or transfer permission.
required_evidence: the current deployment contract names exactly the five corrected Android component hashes and proves sensor topology, camera-info and EXMCU remain official
the retained revoked-package installer advertises RELEASE_APPROVED false and the revoked CIM is rejected before camera contact
tests cover official active slot 1, official active slot 2, mixed components, inconsistent slot flags and an invalid target slot
active slot 2 plus a fixed slot-2 target produces a blocked normalization requirement with no package transfer, slot write, reboot or capture
active slot 1 can reach only the package gate while the candidate remains local-only and cannot authorize transfer without a separately audited current package
every new candidate reruns this gate using exact hashes and a fresh live slot attestation; no result from the revoked package or another slot state may be reused
goals.title: Deployment tooling binds the current candidate and never targets the active system slot

goals.origin: The first corrected five-component package plan compared paths and hashes but did not compare file sizes. Its camera-service candidate was 136580 bytes larger than the official inode while the retained new.dat patcher explicitly supported only equal-size files, so the plan could pass even though archive construction was impossible.
goals.required_behavior: Before a candidate reaches package eligibility, every changed file is checked against the exact packaging primitive that will carry it. A size-changing ELF must either be transformed into a runtime-equivalent same-size image with a structurally valid loader layout, or use an independently audited filesystem rebuild that updates inode, allocation bitmap, free-space counters, transfer list and integrity metadata. A plan that merely names the right files or hashes cannot pass.
required_evidence: the package plan records official size, candidate size, delta and the selected filesystem update primitive for every changed target
an equal-size patch route rejects any nonzero size delta before producing system.new.dat or a CIM

a same-size ELF transformation proves the injected RX bytes, virtual addresses, interpreter, notes, unwind index, dynamic symbols and runtime data are equivalent while the output inode size remains official
independent ELF and OTA round-trip audits reconstruct the exact transformed file from the final package rather than reusing the builder output
mutation tests enlarge one component, corrupt the embedded segment offset or restore a stale size-blind package plan and require release failure
every future component hash change reruns this gate and binds its result to the exact candidate, package and regression-registry hashes
goals.title: A package plan must prove every replacement fits the actual filesystem update method

goals.origin: The first inactive-slot read-only attestation lost the completion marker for a command. The tool recorded only a generic transport error and ran cleanup only after a confirmed mount response, so a mount command that executed but lost its marker could leave the temporary read-only mount behind and hide the exact failing stage.
goals.required_behavior: Every inactive-slot attestation records the exact stage and bounded response diagnostics for a missing marker. Once a mount command has been attempted, cleanup and an independent post-cleanup mount-state check run unconditionally, even if the mount response, a hash response or the cleanup response loses its marker. A missing marker never becomes successful evidence, and an unverified cleanup state is a hard failure.
required_evidence: the report identifies the exact failed stage and records only bounded packet, chunk, byte-count and response-hash diagnostics rather than unbounded camera output
a mount-attempt flag is set before the remote mount command and forces cleanup even when that command raises or returns without its unique marker
an independent final mount-state query runs after every mount attempt and the attestation cannot pass unless it proves the temporary mountpoint is absent
tests inject missing markers at mount, hash and cleanup stages and prove cleanup is attempted, final state is checked and the report remains failed
tests inject a failed unmount that remains visible in the final mount-state query and require an explicit cleanup failure
one bounded live read-only run proves the inactive official slot hashes exactly and leaves no temporary mount while performing no persistent write, slot change or capture
goals.title: A lost live-diagnostic marker cannot skip volatile-mount cleanup

goals.origin: The corrected five-component candidate cannot be written to the camera until its real UI and capture paths are proven, while static inspection alone cannot provide that proof. A RAM-only validation path is useful only if it cannot silently become a second installer, depend on unproved SELinux behavior, strand stopped camera services, or leave changed settings behind.
goals.required_behavior: A volatile validator starts only from a fresh exact-official live identity and a separate exact execution token. Candidate executables and libraries are hash-checked in RAM, mapped through the stock linker without bind-mounting or modifying system files, and run only after a live benign linker and SELinux capability probe passes. A watchdog is armed before official services stop. Every success, failure, timeout or disconnect restores the exact prior camera settings and official init-managed processes; inability to prove recovery triggers a reboot that clears all RAM state.
required_evidence: the bundle contains no CIM, OTA, partition device, updater, slot operation, system remount or bind-mount primitive and records execution_authorized false until the live gate issues the exact token

the runtime-only camera-service differs from the composed candidate solely in the one fixed plugin-config path literal, and the copied GUI and three capture libraries retain their exact composed hashes
the runtime plugins configuration redirects only the X2D still-shooter path while all other official plugin paths remain byte-semantically unchanged
static policy evidence and a harmless live probe prove the hbl camera domain can read and map its tmpfs files through the official linker before either camera process is stopped

the watchdog starts before service disruption, candidate service starts before candidate GUI, and injected failures at download, identity, service, GUI, settings and timeout stages all converge on one bounded rollback
rollback proves the original camera.ini identity, exact official five-component hashes, and both init-managed processes; otherwise it reboots and a fresh official identity attestation is mandatory
the final live report binds the exact bundle, scripts, candidate hashes, active slot, process identities and observed UI/capture evidence and never upgrades volatile success into package permission
goals.title: Volatile runtime validation is identity-locked and automatically restores official operation

goals.origin: The first volatile-runtime script armed its watchdog before service shutdown but wrote the disruption marker only after stopping both official camera processes. A failure or disconnect between the two stop commands could therefore leave the GUI stopped while rollback incorrectly concluded that no recovery was needed.
goals.required_behavior: Before the first official camera process is stopped, the exact rollback script has been hash-checked, its watchdog process is demonstrably alive, and a durable-in-RAM disruption marker has been written successfully. From that point onward every failure path invokes the same rollback. If the marker cannot be written or watchdog liveness cannot be proved, no official process is stopped.
required_evidence: the activation order is exact: payload verification, settings snapshot, watchdog launch, watchdog PID liveness proof, disruption-marker write, GUI stop, then camera-service stop
the disruption-marker write is checked and failure occurs before any stop command
the common failure handler launches rollback whenever the pre-stop marker exists, including failure between the GUI and service stop operations
independent static and mutation audits move the first stop ahead of the marker or remove watchdog liveness and require failure
the generated execution and live-probe tokens bind the exact runtime payload identity and neither authorization file is included in the bundle
a live rehearsal later interrupts each post-marker stage and proves both official init services and the exact previous settings are restored, otherwise the camera reboots to clear RAM
goals.title: Rollback ownership is established and proved alive before the first camera process stops

goals.origin: The first volatile-runtime bundle invoked the stock linker from the factory test shell and proved only that the camera domain could map tmpfs files. It did not prove that the remote command shell itself was in the camera-service domain or that the resulting candidate service and GUI retained that domain. Because an explicit linker preserves its caller domain, the same command launched from another domain could map successfully yet lose camera-device and IPC access.
goals.required_behavior: Before either official camera process is stopped, static provenance and a harmless live loader probe must prove that the exact remote transport executes as u:r:hbl_camera_service:s0, that files created in /mnt receive the expected hbl camera tmpfs label, and that an exact stock executable copied to RAM and mapped through the exact stock linker still runs as u:r:hbl_camera_service:s0. Activation independently rechecks its own domain and every staged file label before disruption, then checks the actual service and GUI process domains after launch. Any wrong, missing or merely inferred domain blocks activation or invokes rollback.
required_evidence: static evidence binds the exact camera-test init service, its hbl_camera_service_exec file label, the init-to-hbl transition, stock-linker execute_no_trans permission and hbl tmpfs map permission
a bounded harmless live probe records the parent HBL-shell domain, /mnt probe-file label, exact stock shell and linker hashes, and the child domain after the RAM copy is mapped by the stock linker
the probe accepts only u:r:hbl_camera_service:s0 for both parent and child and u:object_r:hbl_camera_service_tmpfs:s0 for the RAM file, then proves cleanup even after a missing marker or failed stage

the domain-proof token binds the exact runtime payload identity, expected domain, stock linker identity, stock probe-executable identity and probe implementation identity and is never included in the bundle
activation rechecks its own domain and every staged executable and library label before writing the disruption marker or stopping a service
after candidate service and GUI launch, activation reads each exact PID security context and rejects any process outside u:r:hbl_camera_service:s0 through the common rollback path
independent mutation tests reject a shell-domain caller, wrong tmpfs label, changed linker or probe executable, missing cleanup proof, removed pre-stop check or removed post-launch domain check
goals.title: Volatile candidate execution retains the exact camera SELinux domain

goals.origin: The first RAM-only runtime bundle treated /system/bin/linker64 as a userland ELF launcher for files copied under /mnt. Live probing proved that /mnt is mounted noexec, direct execution of an exact stock shell copy fails with status 126, and directly invoking Android linker64 merely prints its helper-program banner and exits with status 0 without entering the requested program. The old probe therefore mistook a successful helper exit for candidate execution.
goals.required_behavior: The direct-linker RAM activation route is permanently revoked. No loader, installer or validation gate may accept an exit code, process birth or static map permission as proof that candidate code ran. Before any official service is stopped, a harmless live probe must observe an unforgeable marker emitted from inside the intended target program and bind it to the exact executable mapping, process domain and mount policy. A noexec source, linker helper banner, missing target-entry marker or unproved executable mapping blocks activation without issuing either authorization token.
required_evidence: a bounded live report records the exact /mnt mount row with noexec and the exact HBL camera-service parent domain
an exact stock shell copied to the same RAM path receives the expected tmpfs label and exact source hash
direct /system/bin/linker64 invocation records the Android helper banner and status 0 while proving the target-program marker never ran
direct execution of the same RAM copy records permission denied and status 126 while proving the target-program marker never ran
the RAM probe directory is removed and independently proved absent even after a missing response marker or failed stage
the old volatile bundle and its activation token are permanently revoked and cannot be regenerated as executable or pending-live artifacts
any replacement validation route proves actual target entry, exact candidate mappings and rollback ownership before the first camera-service or GUI stop
goals.title: A successful linker exit must prove candidate program entry

goals.origin: The revoked v9 package changed six Android files and also replaced and flashed EXMCU, while its fixed OTA always targeted system_2. Reusing the official upgrade launcher would still write EXMCU and charger firmware, and relying only on a computer-side slot preflight could let a stale or bypassed check aim the fixed system_2 OTA at the running system.
goals.required_behavior: The replacement validation package changes exactly camera-gui, camera-service, the still shooter, the camera HAL and librcam inside system_2. Camera-info, sensor topology, EXMCU and all other outer records remain exact official bytes. The camera-side launcher accepts only X2D II, independently requires official slot 1 active and slot 2 inactive before any upgrade-side write, authenticates the exact OTA and embedded engine, and contains no reachable RT-node firmware write. A stale slot state, extra system target, extra outer replacement or RT-node action blocks construction or installation.
required_evidence: the package builder has an exact five-file allowlist and rejects the revoked six-component tree before creating an output directory
the generated updater script targets system_2 and contains no system_1 target while all non-system OTA payloads reconstruct to official hashes
the generated camera-side launcher verifies X2D II product identity, active slot 1, inactive slot 2, OTA SHA-256 and embedded-engine SHA-256 before its first persistent upgrade action
the launcher action path invokes only the guarded Android update engine and never invokes ApplicationUpgrade, BcMCUUpgrade, CCG3Upgrade, send_fw, write_app, write_bcmcu or write_ccg3
an independent CIM round trip proves only ota.zip and hbl-upgrade changed in the outer container and that EXMCU, charger, loader and post-upgrade records remain official

mutation tests add EXMCU to either replacement set, restore the official RT-node action block, change the target slot, remove either payload digest check or bypass the camera-side slot guard and require failure
a fresh read-only live attestation proves exact official slot 1 is active and bootable and exact slot 2 is inactive before transfer; official slot 1 remains the verified rollback system
goals.title: A five-component A/B validator cannot write the active slot or RT-node firmware

goals.origin: The first revocation matcher rejected a candidate when any listed component hash matched any revoked entry. The failed RAM-loader entry listed the complete five-file payload for forensic identity, although four files are also unchanged members of the corrected disk candidate. That overbroad any-match rule would permanently block the valid candidate for sharing unrelated bytes with a failure caused by the noexec loader route.
goals.required_behavior: Every revocation entry declares how its component identities match. A component known bad by itself may use any-listed-component matching; a failed combination or transport route uses exact-complete-set matching and rejects only when every named component is present with the listed digest. Artifact revocation remains exact by artifact name and hash. Forensic identity can remain complete without silently widening the ban.
required_evidence: the revocation registry declares and validates an explicit component_match_policy for every entry
the original live-failed six-component build rejects each individually listed bad component exactly as before
the RAM-loader entry rejects its exact complete five-file payload and its exact activation artifacts
the corrected candidate sharing four files with the RAM payload but using the corrected camera-service is accepted by component revocation matching
mutation tests reject missing or unknown policies, reject an exact revoked set, and accept partial or one-digest-different combinations for exact-complete-set entries
package authorization runs revocation matching before creating its output directory and binds the exact current revocation-registry hash
goals.title: Revocation matching cannot condemn valid components shared with a failed route

goals.origin: A later independent disassembly of stock camera-gui call site 0x3d19c0 proved that the selected QString::fromUtf8(QByteArrayView) overload receives the byte length in x0, the UTF-8 data pointer in x1 and hidden return storage in x8. X2D-RG-097 recorded the opposite x0/x1 order, and the r2/r3 menu followed that stale claim, creating undefined behavior even though its static QML strings looked correct.
goals.required_behavior: X2D-RG-097 remains historical evidence but its register-order sentence is superseded. Every injected call to this exact overload must reproduce the hash-bound stock call convention: x0 is the exact byte length, x1 is the label data pointer and x8 is valid return storage. No audit may infer a C++ ABI from a prototype when an exact stock call site is available.
required_evidence: the audit binds official camera-gui SHA-256 and stock call site 0x3d19c0 plus its exact callee
independent disassembly proves x0 equals 11, x1 addresses each exact label and x8 addresses distinct live return storage before all four calls
instruction and lifetime tests cover construction, option insertion and QString destruction for every label
mutation tests swap x0 and x1, reuse stale return storage, alter a label length or target another overload and require failure
live menu-model inspection shows exactly 16-bit 3fps, 14-bit 3fps, 14-bit 6fps and 14-bit 9fps and contains neither No lens nor any cloned source text
goals.title: Injected QString calls are copied from the exact stock overload ABI

goals.origin: The first v9 installation log proves that the running official camera service deinitialized for Upgrade, post-upgrade refreshed the lens database, the system entered Maintenance without rebooting, camera initialization reattached the lens, setAvSelectedInternal changed 255 to 0, and SettingStore immediately aborted because camera.ini had no loaded profile. Subsequent starts found QSettings::FormatError. The exact writer of the malformed file is still unproved, but the unsafe event ordering is proved.
goals.required_behavior: Any package or recovery path that completes without an immediate reboot must keep camera hardware deinitialized until a complete valid settings profile is loaded, or suppress every persistent property callback during that interval and replay it only after profile activation. Lens-database notification, RT-node restart, lens attach and aperture initialization may never reach SettingStore while the profile is unavailable. A malformed settings file is quarantined before camera-service starts and can never create a restart loop.
required_evidence: a hash-bound timeline preserves the exact Upgrade, notify_lens_db_update, Maintenance, initCamera, setAvSelectedInternal and fatal SettingStore order without claiming an unknown writer
an event-order harness exercises rebooting and non-rebooting post-upgrade outcomes with lens attached and detached and proves no persistent setter runs before profile readiness
fault tests interrupt settings sync, RT-node programming, lens-database replacement and maintenance entry and always retain either the old complete camera.ini or a validated replacement
camera-service startup with both observed malformed file shapes quarantines them once, loads safe defaults and remains alive
a live read-only upgrade-transition trace later proves zero QSettings format errors, zero no-profile writes, stable camera-service and GUI, and an unchanged or atomically updated valid camera.ini
goals.title: Upgrade-to-maintenance reinitialization cannot write settings without a loaded profile

goals.origin: The first full v9 CIM explicitly recorded multiple PENDING release gates and eligible_for_camera false, yet it was still copied to the camera and installed. Human confirmation and a successfully formed CIM bypassed the release metadata that was supposed to protect the camera.
goals.required_behavior: Package construction, transfer and camera-side launch require a separate exact-hash authorization token generated only by the all-gates aggregator after every applicable goal passes for the same binaries, configuration, package, active-slot attestation and rollback evidence. A manual confirmation cannot substitute for that token. Local-only, revoked, stale, PENDING, NOT_RUN or failed artifacts have no callable transfer route.
required_evidence: the builder emits no CIM or transfer helper before the exact aggregate PASS token exists
the computer-side transfer tool and camera-side launcher independently verify the same candidate, package, registry, slot and rollback identities
mutation tests change each bound hash or status, reuse an older token, omit live evidence and provide manual confirmation and require refusal before transfer
historical v9 packages with eligible_for_camera false and the revoked component sets are rejected by every retained deployment entry point
a release audit enumerates every file-copy, Phocus, USB and camera-upgrade entry point and proves none can accept an unauthorized candidate
goals.title: A local-only or incomplete candidate is cryptographically impossible to transfer

goals.origin: The first v9 menu copied the stock shutter_count entry whose visible label was No lens, then treated PropertyData offset 0x0 as the display QString. Independent constructor and copy-constructor disassembly proves offset 0x0 is the persistent property key, the visible label is the QString at offset 0x18, and the integer value is at offset 0xc0. The live menu consequently retained No lens and no longer carried the intended af_test_mode key.
goals.required_behavior: Each of the four cloned PropertyData objects keeps af_test_mode at offset 0x0, destroys and reconstructs only its visible label QString at offset 0x18, and writes only its atomic preset value at offset 0xc0. No source-template label or unrelated field may survive or be repurposed.
required_evidence: hash-bound stock disassembly proves the eight-QString PropertyData copy layout, including key offset 0x0, label offset 0x18 and value offset 0xc0
the injected helper addresses four distinct label objects at offsets 0x18, 0x118, 0x218 and 0x318 and four values at 0xc0, 0x1c0, 0x2c0 and 0x3c0
the helper never destroys or reconstructs offsets 0x0, 0x100, 0x200 or 0x300 and a behavioral harness proves all four keys remain af_test_mode
mutation tests restore the old offset-zero writes, alter the object stride or value offset, leave No lens in any visible row or change any persisted key and require failure
live menu-model inspection later proves the exact four labels and four values and a selection trace proves all four writes target af_test_mode
goals.title: Burst menu mutation preserves the property key and replaces the real display label field

goals.origin: X2D-RG-129 named 0x3d19c0 as the stock QString call site. Exact disassembly shows 0x3d19c0 begins the argument-preparation window, while the BL instruction that invokes QString::fromUtf8 is at 0x3d19d4. The register conclusion was correct, but the evidence address was imprecise.
goals.required_behavior: ABI audits bind the complete stock instruction window 0x3d19c0 through 0x3d19d4 and explicitly identify 0x3d19d4 as the call instruction. Reports may cite 0x3d19c0 only as the start of argument preparation, never as the BL site.
required_evidence: independent disassembly records ADRP and ADD for x1, MOV w0 with the exact length, ADD for x8 return storage and BL at 0x3d19d4
the callee identity at 0xf3d1d0 and exact official camera-gui hash are bound to the same report
all generated manifests distinguish stock_argument_window from stock_call_site
mutation tests label 0x3d19c0 as the call, move the BL target or omit any argument-preparation instruction and require failure
goals.title: Stock ABI evidence distinguishes the argument-preparation window from the actual call instruction

goals.origin: The first recovery overlay declared a new root init service but omitted a seclabel. Existing X2D II shell-script services explicitly run as u:r:shell:s0, and the vendor policy grants that domain the required system-file execution and system-data read, create, rename and write permissions. A host shell test alone could not detect an init-domain execution denial.
goals.required_behavior: Any pre-camera-service settings guard must declare the exact proven u:r:shell:s0 domain, use a script carrying the generic system_file context, and restrict its data mutations to the system_data_file camera configuration directory. Missing, different or unproved process and file contexts fail closed before package construction.
required_evidence: hash-bound official init files show an existing root shell-script service with seclabel u:r:shell:s0
the generated guard service declares exactly the same seclabel and remains synchronous before camera-service
hash-bound file contexts map the new system script to system_file and data config files to system_data_file
hash-bound vendor policy grants shell the exact execute, read, create, write and rename permissions needed by the guard
mutation tests remove or alter the seclabel, script or data context, or any required policy rule and require failure
live read-only boot evidence later proves the guard completes before camera-service with zero SELinux denial and a valid camera.ini
goals.title: Camera settings recovery runs in a proven SELinux execution domain

goals.origin: Parallel read-only hash and slot-state requests were sent through the single X2D II factory TCP tunnel. Responses crossed between callers, two requests returned no packets, and the camera temporarily stopped responding even though no firmware or slot data was written.
goals.required_behavior: Every retained live-camera tool uses one shared exclusive transport lock per body, permits only one in-flight request, waits for a complete response or bounded timeout, then observes a recovery interval before the next connection. A timeout, missing marker or malformed response stops the sequence and probes reachability before any retry. Parallel Promise, process or thread access to the factory tunnel is forbidden.
required_evidence: a transport harness launches competing callers and proves the shared lock keeps their socket lifetimes non-overlapping
every response is bound to a unique completion marker and cannot be accepted by another caller
timeout and missing-packet tests stop later stages and perform no slot, mount, firmware or camera-setting write
all live installers, diagnostics, attestors and rollback tools import the serialized transport wrapper or independently prove equivalent locking
a static audit finds no parallel execution path that can call the camera factory TCP port
a live read-only sequence later completes identity, hashes and slot checks without camera UI stall, tunnel loss or crossed output
goals.title: The camera factory tunnel is strictly serialized and rate limited

goals.origin: The official-slot normalizer depended on a live attestor pinned to an older regression-registry hash, composed-candidate manifest and rollback-audit report. Later legitimate local edits made that recovery preflight fail before camera contact even though the preserved official slot and its component hashes were unchanged.
goals.required_behavior: The emergency official-slot recovery path authenticates only immutable recovery inputs: camera identity, current slot flags, exact official inactive-slot component hashes, the official rollback image identity and the narrow slot-switch command. Mutable candidate manifests, current regression-registry hashes and unrelated release reports may be recorded but can never block restoration to the exact official slot.
required_evidence: the recovery attestor has no mandatory dependency on a candidate manifest or candidate release status
changing the candidate build, regression registry or stage-review report does not change a successful official-slot preflight
changing any official component hash, official image hash, camera identity, bootability flag or slot target blocks before the slot write
the switch command changes only the two active-slot flags, reads both back and restores the original selection if read-back fails
post-reboot evidence binds slot 1 plus every official camera-critical component hash before declaring recovery complete
the same recovery path remains callable when the active slot contains a known failed candidate or its GUI and camera service are unstable
goals.title: Official recovery cannot be blocked by mutable candidate metadata

goals.origin: The withdrawn v9 P16_3 run used an approximately 4.7 second exposure. The first physical 16-bit readout stabilized at 686 lines instead of the required 690, returned still_transfer -152, and produced no complete RAW or 3FR. Error recovery then admitted later frame activity while the prior root Bayer RAW was still missing. The user had already released full press, so the later frames are not evidence of a requested sustained burst and must not be described as such.
goals.required_behavior: A displayed burst rate is a maximum cadence, never an unconditional timer. Every P16_3, P14_6 and P14_9 path waits for the previous frame's real exposure stop, exact sensor line count, physical receiver completion, valid RAW identity and buffer-ownership transition before admitting any operation that can start or masquerade as the next still frame. Long exposures automatically reduce cadence. Any timeout, line-count mismatch, receiver error or missing RAW terminates the burst and restores stock live view without issuing recovery frames through the still pipeline.
required_evidence: a hash-bound timeline preserves full-press release, the approximately 4.7 second exposure, expected 690 versus observed 686 lines, still_transfer -152, the missing root Bayer RAW and the later recovery activity without calling that activity a user-requested burst
instruction and state-machine audits prove the requested FPS is only a lower-bound interval and cannot bypass exposure, receiver, RAW-identity or buffer-readiness gates

fault tests inject long exposures, 686-line and other short reads, receiver timeout, missing RAW, stale frame ID and release-before-completion and require one clean abort with no subsequent still actuation
two-frame and sustained harnesses prove every admitted next frame follows the prior frame's exact physical completion token and never a timer, predicted line count or synthesized success
live validation covers short and multi-second shutter times in all four presets and binds equal FSync, physical RAW, JLS and closed 3FR counts or a clean fail-closed stop
goals.title: Long-exposure burst admission cannot outrun physical RAW completion

goals.origin: The withdrawn v9 preset bridge changed the drive value used by the live-view selector when P16_3 was selected. Live logs later show normal camera operation retaining E_StreamGroup_Still16bit where the stock preview path should use the 12K 11-bit live-view topology, matching the user's noisy-screen report and repeated preview processing timeouts.
goals.required_behavior: Selecting or persisting any burst preset leaves the normal preview, display and AF source topology byte-identical to official firmware. P16_3 may select the official 16-bit still group only inside a real capture transaction after live view is stopped, and must restore the official live-view topology after the transaction. No menu setter, drive-mode setter or idle-state refresh may route preview through a still-capture group.
required_evidence: binary diff proves the official live-view drive setter and selector callsite are byte-identical and no injected helper rewrites drive 6 to a still-only route
behavior tests select and persist every preset while idle and prove the preview group, frame rate, AF source and display path remain stock
capture tests prove P16_3 enters the 16-bit still group only between capture start and terminal cleanup and returns to stock live view on success, release, timeout and sensor error
mutation tests restore the retired live-view hook or retain Still16bit after capture and require failure
live read-only traces later show stock preview topology before and after each preset, no sustained preview polling timeout and no user-visible noise regression
goals.title: Burst bit-depth selection cannot replace the stock live-view topology

goals.origin: After the r5 camera-service and camera-gui bytes changed, the deployment preflight, rollback contract and saved offline package authorization still named the older r2/r4 manifest and component hashes. That stale identity could make an obsolete archive look like the current candidate even though it lacked the newest preview and long-exposure protections.
goals.required_behavior: Every package plan, rollback contract, deployment preflight and authorization gate resolves one exact current manifest and its exact component hashes. Changing any candidate binary, UI model, regression registry or package layout invalidates every earlier authorization and archive. Retired complete component sets remain explicitly revoked and cannot be promoted by copying or renaming their reports.
required_evidence: the current deployment, rollback and package-plan modules bind the same manifest path, registry hash and five component hashes
a candidate change makes every prior release-gate document fail before an output directory or camera transport is opened
the retired pre-RG138 five-component set is represented by an exact-complete-set revocation entry
tests reject a renamed old archive, a mixed old/new component set presented under the current manifest, and an old authorization paired with new bytes
the all-gates report is regenerated from the current hashes and never reuses PASS evidence from an earlier named version
goals.title: A current candidate cannot reuse a retired package identity or release gate

goals.origin: The current sensor-completion audit correctly returned a list of named PASS/FAIL rows, but the final offline reviewer treated that list as a dictionary and crashed after the full regression suite had passed. This prevented a complete release decision and could hide a failed final gate behind an unhandled exception.
goals.required_behavior: The final reviewer explicitly validates each supported audit-result shape, treats unsupported or malformed check collections as failure, completes without exception, and emits a hash-bound non-release report. A successful unit suite is not a substitute for executing the reviewer itself.
required_evidence: a test executes the final reviewer against the exact current manifest, reports and JUnit file and receives a complete result instead of an exception
dictionary checks require every value to be true and list checks require every row to carry PASS status
a malformed check collection and an injected failed list row both fail closed
the final report binds the current manifest, regression registry, revocation registry, package gate and full-suite JUnit hashes
the package-construction gate remains blocked and no archive or camera write occurs when live evidence is incomplete
goals.title: The final offline reviewer must execute every declared audit schema

goals.origin: The final reviewer and package-construction gate trusted the tests attribute declared by a JUnit testsuite. Their own end-to-end test supplied only the small fixed set of required-module testcase rows while claiming 518 tests in the header, and that synthetic report was accepted as a complete current suite.
goals.required_behavior: Release reviewers count and validate the real testcase elements, require a complete non-empty identity for every row, reject duplicate identities and inconsistent outcome totals, and require every current v9 test module to be represented. A large aggregate tests attribute can record framework subtests but can never satisfy the minimum full-suite threshold by itself.
required_evidence: the prior inflated synthetic JUnit with only a handful of testcase rows is rejected even when its tests attribute exceeds the threshold
the current pytest JUnit contains at least the established materialized-testcase baseline and every current v9 test module
blank or duplicate testcase identities and aggregate outcome counts that disagree with failure, error or skipped child nodes fail closed
both the final reviewer and package-construction gate consume the same strict JUnit evidence rules
the post-suite final reviewer is executed separately against the exact newly generated full-suite JUnit hash
goals.title: JUnit aggregate totals cannot substitute for materialized test cases

goals.origin: The package-construction gate required the candidate manifest to say release_eligible true with no blockers, while the deployment contract and package plan required that exact same manifest to remain local-only with release_eligible false. No report could satisfy both conditions, and the gate had no separate hash-bound candidate capture report for the four live presets.
goals.required_behavior: The composed candidate manifest remains immutable, local-only and hash stable. A separate candidate live-evidence document binds the exact manifest, registry and component hashes and proves the four preset capture, preview-restoration and storage transactions. The construction gate consumes that external evidence without changing the manifest and remains blocked when it is absent, stale, incomplete or merely inferred.
required_evidence: the deployment contract, package plan and construction gate all accept the same unchanged local-only manifest identity
a valid separate live-evidence schema binds the exact manifest hash, registry hash, five component hashes and the volatile candidate runtime identity
each preset has real leaf-shutter capture evidence, stock preview before and after, equal nonzero FSync, physical RAW, JLS and closed 3FR counts, and stored-file validation
mutating any evidence hash, preset identity, bit depth, cadence, preview state, storage count or persistent-write flag blocks promotion
the current default remains blocked before archive creation because no complete candidate live-evidence document exists
goals.title: Package promotion cannot require mutation of the immutable candidate manifest

goals.origin: The archive authorization helper checked only a small set of top-level release-gate fields. A hand-written JSON object with PASS status, current registry, revocation and manifest hashes, and the expected slots could satisfy that helper without containing the construction gate checks, JUnit proof or candidate live-evidence hash.
goals.required_behavior: Before creating any output directory, the archive builder reruns the construction gate against the canonical current evidence files and requires the supplied release-gate document to be exactly equal to that recomputed result. Top-level fields alone, a copied stale gate, omitted checks or omitted evidence hashes can never authorize construction.
required_evidence: the former minimal forged PASS document is rejected before an output directory exists
the authorization helper requires the complete check map, complete evidence-hash map, strict JUnit summary, non-install purpose and camera-install false state
the archive builder recomputes the gate from the current recovery, deployment, full-suite JUnit and candidate live-evidence files and compares the entire document
mutating or omitting any nested check, evidence hash, JUnit field or live-evidence binding fails before archive construction
the current default blocked gate and every historical PASS gate remain unable to create or overwrite an archive
goals.title: The archive builder must reconstruct the release gate from canonical evidence

goals.origin: The first volatile-runtime design embedded a reusable deterministic execution token in the staged bundle. Anyone or any stale script able to invoke the factory shell could replay that token without proving which host preflight, runtime identity or camera session had been approved.
goals.required_behavior: Every volatile activation receives a fresh external authorization bound to the exact runtime identity, one 256-bit session nonce and the hash of the completed host preflight. The token is absent from the reusable bundle and source manifest, is readable only by root in the parent control tmpfs, and cannot authorize another session, runtime or preflight.
required_evidence: bundle and source scans prove no complete activation token or reusable token digest is embedded
the controller generates a fresh 64-hex nonce and writes the completed preflight before constructing the token
the activation script validates token mode, owner, SELinux context, runtime identity, session nonce and preflight hash before stopping an official process
wrong, stale, truncated, duplicate and cross-session tokens fail without process disruption or persistent camera writes
the token and its exact session control directory are removed during successful rollback and bounded failure recovery
goals.title: Volatile candidate activation requires an external single-session authorization

goals.origin: Early volatile staging assumptions checked content hashes but did not completely bind the transfer destination, byte count, file mode, owner and SELinux context. The token also initially used the executable mount context even though it lives in the parent hbl service tmpfs.
goals.required_behavior: The host may transfer only the exact manifest-declared runtime files plus one session token into exact volatile allowlisted paths. Every transfer uses a temporary part file, accepts only the audited camera peer, proves the exact byte count and hash before rename, and rechecks final hash, size, mode, root ownership and the path-appropriate SELinux context before activation.
required_evidence: path validation rejects traversal, shell metacharacters, unexpected filenames and every destination outside one exact runtime or session directory
the one-shot server rejects a non-camera peer and short, long, interrupted or duplicate transfers
each payload follows part, hash, chmod, atomic rename, final hash, size, owner and context verification
the executable tmpfs remains bounded, nosuid and nodev while the parent control tmpfs retains its separate hbl service context
mutation tests for content, size, mode, uid, gid, context and manifest identity fail before official process disruption
goals.title: Volatile payload transfer is exact, confined and independently attestable

goals.origin: Successive volatile-runtime reviews found a fixed rollback lock, possible PID reuse, incomplete verification that init-owned official processes had stopped, and a settings backup that was not yet proven byte- and metadata-identical to its source. Any one could leave mixed official and candidate processes or restore the wrong persistent settings.
goals.required_behavior: Each session has unique control and rollback state. Activation proceeds only after both official processes are stopped by init and no matching PID remains, the settings file still matches its preflight snapshot, and the watchdog is proven alive. Rollback signals only candidate PIDs whose proc executable matches the staged path, restores settings bytes plus uid, gid, mode and SELinux context exactly, restarts the official services with their stock init environment, proves their official executable hashes, and reboots on any incomplete restoration.
required_evidence: concurrent and stale sessions cannot share a rollback lock, token, PID file, status file or settings backup
tests inject delayed init stop, surviving official PID, settings drift and dead watchdog and require activation to stop before candidate launch
PID reuse and proc-executable mismatch never signal an unrelated process
success and every injected fault restore the exact settings hash, size, uid, gid, mode and SELinux context and prove both official processes
rollback code is loaded before unmounting its executable tmpfs and any failed restoration invokes the preserved official reboot route
goals.title: Candidate process handoff and rollback preserve exact official runtime state

goals.origin: The new volatile controller generated a unique marker for every factory-shell command, but the retained standalone official-component attestor still used one fixed __V9_DONE__ marker. A delayed response from an earlier request could therefore satisfy a later read-only attestation.
goals.required_behavior: Every live controller, recovery probe and standalone attestor generates a fresh unpredictable completion marker for each command, includes that marker's maximum length in the factory transport capacity proof, accepts exactly one occurrence of the current marker and rejects stale, partial, missing or duplicate markers.
required_evidence: source and mutation tests cover the standalone attestor as well as wrapped controller calls
two consecutive commands demonstrably receive different markers of the audited fixed maximum length
fragmented current markers close correctly while stale and partial markers never close the request
zero or multiple occurrences of the current marker fail without accepting partial component identity
the full current live-tool suite passes after any marker, command or transport change
goals.title: Every retained live tool uses a fresh response completion marker

goals.origin: The first full r11 host-orchestration simulation reached candidate verification, then rejected its own combined status and two-PID read because the marked command was 334 bytes, above the 232-byte factory tunnel capacity. The earlier static command inventory had omitted that runtime-generated command.
goals.required_behavior: The release gate enumerates every camera command generated by activation, status, rollback, transfer and recovery paths with a maximum-length session nonce and completion marker. Multi-value reads are split into independently marked commands, and no camera process is disrupted unless all commands needed to verify and recover that session have already passed the exact byte-capacity check.
required_evidence: the retired combined status, service-PID and GUI-PID command is reproduced and rejected as over capacity
status and both PID reads use three separately marked allowlisted commands and each remains below the transport limit
the static inventory covers activation success, pre-disruption cleanup, active status, manual status and rollback commands rather than only transfer helpers
mutation tests add one byte beyond the capacity, restore the combined read or omit a generated command and require failure before camera contact
a full host-orchestration harness reaches the active state and exercises both pre- and post-disruption recovery without any unvalidated command
goals.title: Every dynamically generated factory command must fit the transport

goals.origin: The first RG148 full-suite run found one test that correctly expected an RG148 report and last-goal identifier, then contradicted itself with a leftover hard-coded registry length of 147. The duplicated version constants turned a complete implementation into an avoidable failed release pass.
goals.required_behavior: Every current-candidate assertion derives goal count, last goal and hash from the same loaded registry or one shared release identity. A test or release gate must never mix a current goal identifier with a separately copied stale count, hash, report name or candidate path.
required_evidence: the live capture-chain binding test compares its report count, last goal and hash to one loaded registry rather than a duplicated numeric constant
current release modules name one consistent candidate generation, JUnit report and last regression goal
mutation tests reject a mismatch in registry count, last goal, hash, candidate path or report identity
a clean full-suite run materializes every current v9 test module with no stale-binding failure
the post-suite reviewer reconstructs the current identity from canonical files and remains blocked on missing live proof
goals.title: Current-registry assertions must use one atomic identity

goals.origin: The first live nested-tmpfs probe passed its offline policy audit but failed on the camera because context=system_file requested a filesystem relabelto operation that the hbl_camera_service domain is denied. The mount command did not report its exit status or stderr, so the initial report incorrectly surfaced only an empty mount-state result instead of the kernel AVC cause.
goals.required_behavior: An executable RAM route must not relabel the whole tmpfs. It must use a policy-proven per-file creation context, and every directory, mount, copy, mode, execution and cleanup mutation must return a named exit status with bounded diagnostic output. Static permission inference can never substitute for one harmless live execution proof and exact cleanup verification.
required_evidence: the retired context=system_file mount is reproduced in a mutation test and rejected before camera contact
the exact official policy proves per-file system_file creation, writing and execution while ordinary hbl_camera_service_tmpfs files remain nonexecutable
every live mutation reports a stage-specific exit status and the failed stage preserves bounded stderr instead of only an empty follow-up read
a harmless exact-stock-shell copy executes from the new RAM route in the hbl_camera_service domain and the mount plus directory are then absent
the runtime transfer path creates every destination with the proven per-file context and reruns the complete current suite before any candidate process is started
goals.title: Live execution probes must model SELinux relabelling and expose every mutation result

goals.origin: The corrected nested tmpfs mounted successfully on the live camera, but cp --preserve=context used /system/bin/sh as its source. That source is shell_exec, not system_file, so the camera denied the label copy and returned CP_RC 1 before any executable identity or target-entry proof could run.
goals.required_behavior: The harmless probe and every volatile payload transfer seed their destination from one exact stock file whose live hash and SELinux label are both verified as system_file. Payload bytes overwrite that already-labelled inode without replacing it. Using an executable source, assuming a source label from its path, or accepting a failed context-preserving copy is forbidden.
required_evidence: the exact official /system/etc/hosts hash and live system_file label are verified before the first RAM mutation
the former /system/bin/sh context-preserving copy is reproduced as a mutation and rejected because it requests shell_exec
the context seed, payload-byte overwrite and mode change are separate bounded commands with separate exit codes
the final staged file retains system_file while its hash equals the intended stock probe or candidate payload rather than the seed file
the same proven seed primitive is used by every runtime payload transfer and the complete current suite is rerun before candidate execution
goals.title: A per-file context seed must already carry the intended target label

goals.origin: The second live nested-tmpfs probe verified that /system/etc/hosts already carried system_file, yet cp --preserve=context still returned SEED_RC 1 because cp first created an ordinary tmpfs inode and then attempted a forbidden security.selinux setxattr relabel. A correct source label cannot make a post-creation relabel permissible.
goals.required_behavior: The harmless probe and every volatile executable payload set the current shell's SELinux fscreate context, create the destination inode through a verified shell-builtin redirection in that same process, and immediately restore the default fscreate context. Payload transfer may only truncate and overwrite that existing inode. cp --preserve=context, chcon, restorecon, external helpers whose exec clears fscreate, and any unverified post-creation relabel are forbidden.
required_evidence: the live RG151 failure is preserved with an exact system_file source, SEED_RC 1 from security.selinux setxattr denial and verified complete cleanup
official policy proves setfscreate plus creation and execution of system_file, while the live shell proves echo and colon are builtins before any mutation
setting fscreate, creating the inode and restoring the default context occur in one bounded shell command with separate exit statuses
mutation tests reject cp --preserve=context, external context writers, missing reset, creation after reset and any destination whose final label or bytes are wrong

an exact stock-shell payload executes from the created inode in the camera-service domain, cleanup is exact, and every runtime executable transfer uses the identical creation primitive before candidate execution
goals.title: Executable RAM files must receive their label at inode creation

goals.origin: The RG152 live probe verified the exact official camera-service domain and shell builtins, then both fscreate set and reset returned 1. strace showed write to /proc/self/attr/fscreate failing with EACCES, and the live kernel audit log recorded an enforcing avc denial for setfscreate. The offline split-policy analysis had incorrectly treated that permission as available.
goals.required_behavior: A security permission that is essential to staging or execution is unavailable whenever the enforcing live kernel denies it, regardless of a static policy-model result. The fscreate route is retired. Any replacement RAM execution route must avoid filesystem-wide relabel, post-creation relabel and setfscreate, and must pass a harmless live stock-binary execution proof before it is used for any candidate payload.
required_evidence: the exact RG152 failure report is preserved with FSCREATE_RC 1, RESET_RC 1, complete cleanup and no candidate execution or persistent write
bounded strace and kernel AVC evidence identify EACCES and the denied setfscreate permission in the enforcing hbl_camera_service domain
the offline policy audit reports the disagreement instead of claiming the live permission is proven, and mutation tests reject static-only authorization
the replacement route requires none of context mount relabel, cp preserve-context, chcon, restorecon or fscreate and rejects any recurrence before camera mutation
