an exact stock payload enters target code through the replacement RAM route, remains in the expected domain, cleans up exactly, and the complete current suite is rerun before candidate execution
goals.title: Live AVC evidence overrides static SELinux permission inference

goals.origin: The first deterministic ext4 image builder wrote its build timestamp at superblock offset 0x150 instead of 0x108. That field is the high half of the block count, so the image falsely declared 16,777,217 block groups even though its internal construction checks passed. An independent ext4 parser caught the defect before any camera contact.
goals.required_behavior: Every generated filesystem image is validated by a parser independent of the builder and by a second implementation before it can be referenced by a live or packaging path. The validation binds its exact size, block geometry, group count, inode layout, feature flags, labels, modes and payload hashes. Any malformed, multiply interpreted or internally self-certified image remains local-only.
required_evidence: the original wrong superblock offset is reproduced by a mutation test and rejected because the independently parsed group count is not exactly one
the canonical image has deterministic bytes and UUID and independently parses as one-group ext4 with the declared block and inode sizes
all embedded payload bytes, modes and security.selinux labels are read back by an independent parser and match the manifest exactly
a second filesystem implementation recognizes the image without structural errors and no builder-owned parser result can substitute for that check
mutations of block counts, feature flags, directory entries, extents, xattrs, payload bytes or manifest hashes fail before camera contact
goals.title: Synthetic filesystem images require independent structural validation

goals.origin: The r14 composed manifest contained an early foundation-layer preset table that still labelled P14_6 and P14_9 schedulers NOT_IMPLEMENTED while later layers declared both implementations present. Although the final binary composition was separate, the contradictory machine-readable states made it possible for a reviewer or release tool to accept the wrong layer as the final feature truth.
goals.required_behavior: The composed manifest publishes one authoritative resolved contract for every user-visible preset. Intermediate layer reports are explicitly scoped as foundations and cannot be consumed as final status. Composition fails when any final preset is missing, unresolved, duplicated, contradicts its UI label, changes the stock P16_3 or P14_3 transaction, or lacks its required native-leaf, RAW-completion and persistence semantics.
required_evidence: the final manifest has exactly one resolved record for P16_3, P14_3, P14_6 and P14_9 matching the four displayed menu choices
every embedded intermediate preset table is marked foundation_only and the release reviewer ignores it as final truth
no authoritative final record contains NOT_IMPLEMENTED, inferred, placeholder or an unbound scheduler identity
mutation tests restore the contradictory r14 foundation/final interpretation, remove a resolved preset, swap bit depth or cadence, or alter shutter semantics and require composition failure
the final reviewer derives UI, backend, native leaf-shutter, physical RAW completion and storage expectations from the same resolved contract
goals.title: A composed candidate cannot publish contradictory feature states

goals.origin: The first RG155 full-suite run found eleven historical r14 ephemeral-runtime tests that still expected bundle construction or ACTIVE_R14_EPHEMERAL after RG153 live AVC evidence and the revocation registry had permanently retired that fscreate route. Registry hash drift happened to block the path, but rebinding its old builder would have made the unsafe route executable again.
goals.required_behavior: Every builder, host controller and audit belonging to the revoked r14 fscreate route fails closed with an explicit permanent-revocation result before artifact creation, USB enumeration, transport, transfer, service control or camera mutation. Historical tests verify refusal and forensic identity instead of expecting successful activation. Rollback-only evidence remains readable, but cannot be used to authorize activation.
required_evidence: the exact r14 runtime manifest, activation script, rollback script and live AVC forensic report are bound to the permanent revocation row
the retired builder refuses before source validation and creates no output directory or file
the retired activation controller returns permanent revocation before USB presence checks, remote commands or transfers
mutation tests reject removal, delay or conditionalization of the early revocation barrier and never assert an ACTIVE status
the current reviewer consumes only the route's revocation audit and a clean full-suite run contains no test that treats the retired route as usable
goals.title: A live-failed execution route must remain non-runnable in code and tests

goals.origin: The 2026-09-03 live check found active slot 1 byte-exact official and both slots marked bootable and successful, so the old deployment planner reported the fixed slot-2 target ready for its package gate. A separate read-only hash attestation then proved inactive slot 2 still contained the exact five modified components from failed composed r2 rather than official firmware.
goals.required_behavior: Every deployment, package, normalization and rollback decision that relies on an inactive slot requires a fresh read-only content attestation bound to the same active-slot state. Slot active, bootable and successful flags are metadata only and can never substitute for exact component hashes. A missing, stale, opposite-state, failed or nonofficial inactive proof blocks before package construction, transfer, slot changes or reboot.
required_evidence: the live inactive-slot report and the composed-r2 manifest prove an exact five-component hash match while active slot 1 and both slot flags remained healthy
an active-slot-1 preflight with no inactive proof or with the observed r2 proof returns BLOCKED_INACTIVE_TARGET_NOT_EXACT_OFFICIAL
only a fresh proof for inactive slot 2 with all eight exact official hashes and verified mount cleanup can advance to the still-closed package gate
tests reject bootable and successful flags, stale proof, opposite active-slot state, partial hashes and failed cleanup as substitutes for content identity
the complete current suite and final reviewer bind the exact active attestation, inactive attestation, candidate manifest and registry without reusing older slot evidence
goals.title: Bootable slot flags never prove inactive firmware identity

goals.origin: The 2026-09-03 exact-official 1.3.16.1 tethered apply attempt passed package, battery, idle and storage preflight, then the PhocusApi64 UpdateFirmware export returned integer zero immediately. Five minutes of USB and runtime-log monitoring showed no transfer, update state, disconnect or reboot. Static decompilation further proved the native export has void semantics while the old Python binding incorrectly declared an integer HUPGRADE result.
goals.required_behavior: A tethered firmware controller must mirror the supported Phocus initialization and dispatch path for the exact camera and package type, and it must treat the UpdateFirmware call return as semantically void. No success, write, reboot or slot claim may be made unless independent live evidence observes accepted transfer or update state, the expected disconnect and reconnect cycle, and exact post-boot slot and component attestation. An unsupported or no-op CIM path fails closed without retrying on the camera.
required_evidence: the failed 2026-09-03 apply report is preserved with exact official package identity, native return zero, five-minute observation window and verified absence of any USB update cycle
the Phocus 4.1.1 managed and native decompilations bind the real initialization sequence, UpdateFirmware call site, void native export semantics and package-extension branches
tests reject interpreting zero or any register residue as HUPGRADE_OK and reject initialization paths missing required window, timer, notification, IPC or message-loop behavior
a harmless supported-path probe proves that the chosen host route reaches the intended camera update handler before any firmware payload is transferred

completion requires independent transfer progress, camera-side update evidence, disconnect and reconnect, active-slot transition where expected, exact official component hashes and a verified rollback state
goals.title: A host updater return value never proves camera update acceptance

goals.origin: During the exact-official 1.3.16.2 camera-side restore, the factory shell stopped responding immediately after the single stock-updater dispatch and remained unavailable until the expected full USB reboot. The live sampler therefore missed the short IsUpgrading state and initially failed closed, while the post-boot stock log preserved exact doUpgrade Success, startUpgrade metadata, current.cim copy and download-complete records, and the runtime updater reported UpgradeProcessFinishedOk(23).
goals.required_behavior: When the live management channel disappears during a real upgrade, completion may use exact persistent camera-side updater evidence after reboot as the acceptance proof. Persistent evidence must be bound to the exact package UUID, type and size and to the same single invocation. It never substitutes for the independently observed USB disconnect and reconnect, expected slot transition, both-slot byte identity or final idle state. A missed live state must not trigger an automatic retry.
required_evidence: the original fail-closed restore report is preserved with one invocation, the exact disconnect and reconnect timestamps, slot transition and both exact official slot attestations
the persistent stock log contains exact doUpgrade Success, startUpgrade UUID/type/size, source-to-current.cim copy and download-completed records for the pinned official package
the post-boot stock updater reports UpgradeProcessFinishedOk(23), is_processing false and persist.hbl.is_upgrading zero
mutation tests reject a wrong UUID, type, size, missing success/copy/completion record, non-idle final state, repeated invocation, missing USB transition or missing slot identity
reconciliation writes a separate derived report without overwriting the raw live report and never dispatches another update
goals.title: A transient monitor outage cannot erase persistent camera-side upgrade acceptance

goals.origin: After the official 1.3.16.2 restore changed the active slot from 1 to 2 and post-boot attestations proved both slots byte-exact official, the offline reviewer still loaded the earlier R15 active-slot-1 and failed-r2 inactive-slot-2 reports and labelled that pre-restore state as current. The report was locally consistent but factually stale.
goals.required_behavior: Every reviewer, deployment decision and package gate orders live evidence across camera state-changing events and identifies the newest proven state. Evidence captured before a later restore, slot switch, reboot or install is historical only and cannot be labelled current or authorize a target. When the newest state lacks a fresh follow-up proof, the live result remains pending rather than falling back to an older convenient state.
required_evidence: the pre-restore slot-1 official and slot-2 failed-r2 reports remain preserved and are explicitly labelled historical and superseded
the later restore report is bound by exact timestamps, observed USB reboot, slot-1-to-slot-2 transition and post-boot active and inactive component attestations
the offline review reports the newest observed state as active slot 2 with both slots official and never repeats the old failed-r2 state as current
deployment and package planning remain blocked for a fixed slot-2 target while slot 2 is active, without silently reusing the older active-slot-1 report
mutation tests reject reversed or missing evidence order, a mismatched post-boot slot, incomplete component identity and any fallback from missing current proof to superseded evidence
goals.title: A later camera state transition supersedes earlier live-slot evidence

goals.origin: The current archive-construction gate required complete live behavior from the exact candidate even though the only proven volatile execution routes had been permanently retired. That created a circular dependency: no current archive could be built for controlled inactive-slot validation, while no exact candidate could produce live UI and RAW-to-3FR evidence without a runnable image.
goals.required_behavior: A dedicated canary-construction gate may authorize creation of an offline archive, but never camera installation. It requires the complete current offline suite, exact candidate and registry hashes, a fresh active-slot-2 official baseline, a fresh inactive-slot-1 exact-official proof, a read-only slot-1 normalization preflight, and an explicit fixed-slot-2 target. Camera installation remains separately blocked until the generated archive passes an independent decrypt, filesystem reconstruction, locality and launcher audit and a fresh post-normalization live gate proves official slot 1 active with official slot 2 inactive. The canary is used only to acquire missing live evidence and must retain automatic official rollback conditions.
required_evidence: the construction gate is canonically reconstructed from exact evidence and declares camera_install_eligible false
missing or stale current JUnit, manifest, registry, revocation, active-slot, inactive-slot or normalization evidence blocks before creating an output directory
the package independently decrypts and reconstructs exactly five Android component changes while every RT-node payload remains official and unreachable from the launcher action
a separate install gate requires fresh official slot 1 active, exact official slot 2 inactive, exact package and roundtrip hashes, one camera-side updater dispatch and a verified rollback package
candidate boot or any UI, preview, capture, storage or service failure triggers the bounded official rollback path and cannot be promoted as release evidence
goals.title: Canary archive construction and camera installation require separate gates

goals.origin: On 2026-09-04 the r16 v9 archive was installed even though its composed manifest and package report declared installable false, its canary construction and independent package audits declared camera_install_eligible false, and the manifest still named camera.ini recovery as not implemented or proven. The exact candidate booted from slot 2, camera-service aborted in the known no-loaded-profile failure class, the UI lost its stable backend, and the body had to be rolled back to the byte-exact official slot 1.
goals.required_behavior: Every camera transfer and stock-updater dispatch is callable only through one deployment controller that independently requires an exact, current install-authorization artifact with camera_install_eligible true. A construction-only gate, a structurally valid package, user confirmation, or a manual camera-side command can never substitute. The controller also rejects any candidate manifest containing an unimplemented startup, settings, UI, capture, persistence or rollback requirement. On a post-boot service or UI failure it records the live fault once and performs only the pre-attested official rollback path without retrying the candidate.
required_evidence: the hash-bound 2026-09-04 incident report preserves the exact r16 package and component identities, one updater dispatch, slot-2 candidate attestation, camera-service SIGABRT, user-observed UI regression and slot-1 official rollback attestation
all retained transfer, copy and updater-dispatch entry points require the same exact install-authorization schema and reject camera_install_eligible false before camera contact

mutation tests present the r16 construction gate, package audit, package report, user confirmation and direct-dispatch request separately and every case is refused before transfer or updater invocation

the install gate rejects any authoritative or embedded candidate state containing NOT_IMPLEMENTED, PENDING, NOT_RUN, inferred, placeholder or an unresolved malformed-settings and pre-profile-write condition
a startup harness covers all four persisted presets with valid, malformed, truncated, absent and interrupted camera.ini states and proves a loaded profile precedes every persistent callback

live qualification requires stable camera-service and camera-gui uptime, zero new tombstones, the exact runtime menu model and backend route, valid settings persistence, complete RAW-to-3FR closure and the pre-attested official rollback route
goals.title: Archive-construction evidence can never authorize a camera install

goals.origin: The r16 UI was described as an independent burst menu, but its runtime submenu key remained debugModeMenu and its persisted value remained af_test_mode. That coupled a user-facing production control to hidden diagnostic identities and made static menu appearance insufficient proof of an independent setting path.
goals.required_behavior: The current GUI and camera service start from the exact official components and rename the selected unused meta-property slot end-to-end to burst_preset without changing its layout. The Continuous submenu uses burstModeMenu. No allocated runtime section may retain af_test_mode, setAf_test_mode, af_test_modeChanged or debugModeMenu. Legacy af_test_mode entries are rejected rather than migrated implicitly, while burst_preset accepts exactly 0 through 3 and remains separate from capture implementation.
required_evidence: the official camera-gui and camera-service hashes, every exact in-place runtime-string edit and unchanged file sizes are bound to the foundation report
allocated-section scans prove every old diagnostic runtime identity is absent and the dedicated menu, property, setter and changed-signal identities are present
the QML unit round-trips Continuous to burstModeMenu and the four rows all write burst_preset values 0, 1, 2 and 3
guard tests preserve all four dedicated values across repeated startup and quarantine every legacy af_test_mode entry
camera exposure, sensor topology, RAW processing and storage components remain byte-exact official in this settings-only foundation
goals.title: Burst controls require dedicated runtime menu and setting identities

goals.origin: The first recovery guard moved an invalid camera.ini to quarantine before renaming the validated replacement into place. A reset or write failure in that interval could leave the live path absent even though both operations occurred in the same directory.
goals.required_behavior: Recovery first validates and synchronizes a same-directory replacement, copies the invalid source to a temporary forensic snapshot, atomically publishes that snapshot, and only then atomically renames the replacement over the still-present camera.ini. Startup removes stale temporary files, validates the committed result, and a pre-profile persistent callback returns safely instead of aborting the camera service.
required_evidence: the guard source contains no move of live camera.ini to quarantine and orders snapshot copy before the same-directory replacement rename
valid, malformed, truncated, absent, legacy-key, duplicate-key and stale-temporary-file cases pass the executable guard harness
the camera-service patch changes only the exact no-profile conditional branch to the audited clean epilogue and leaves normal loaded-profile writes untouched
official QSettings construction enables atomic sync, SettingStore invokes sync and QSaveFile commit is reached without direct-write fallback for the filesystem path
startup-order tests require guard completion and successful profile loading before normal persistent callbacks; target power-loss and live restart proof remain explicit release gates
goals.title: Settings recovery never exposes a missing live camera.ini

goals.origin: The first dedicated-property guard rejected any file containing the old af_test_mode key. Without a previously validated backup, that policy would replace the whole otherwise-valid profile database with safe defaults and discard unrelated exposure, focus and user-profile settings.
goals.required_behavior: When an otherwise-valid camera.ini contains one or more legacy af_test_mode assignments, startup snapshots the original file, removes only those exact assignments into a same-directory temporary file, validates the complete sanitized profile, and atomically commits it. The old value is never migrated to burst_preset. Any additional structural corruption still falls back to a separately validated backup or safe defaults.
required_evidence: an executable guard test starts with a legacy key plus unrelated official settings and proves every unrelated byte-line survives while no burst_preset value is inferred
the original legacy-bearing file is retained as the invalid forensic snapshot before the sanitized replacement is committed
a file containing both a legacy key and another malformed structure cannot pass through legacy sanitization
valid dedicated burst_preset values 0 through 3 remain unchanged across repeated startup runs
all startup-recovery and atomic-replacement gates are rerun against the exact updated guard hash
goals.title: Removing a legacy burst key never resets unrelated camera settings

goals.origin: After legacy cleanup was added for the live camera.ini, an otherwise-valid known-good backup containing af_test_mode still failed validation and fell through to safe defaults when the live file was separately damaged or absent.
goals.required_behavior: Recovery first prefers a valid dedicated-key backup. If that backup is structurally valid except for legacy af_test_mode assignments, it removes only those assignments, validates the sanitized complete profile and atomically restores it. No legacy value is converted to burst_preset, and unrelated settings survive.
required_evidence: an executable harness combines an invalid live file with a legacy-bearing backup and proves unrelated backup settings survive
the restored file contains neither af_test_mode nor an inferred burst_preset assignment
a malformed backup remains ineligible even after legacy-line removal and falls back to safe defaults
valid current and valid dedicated-key backup precedence remain unchanged
all settings-foundation hashes, startup tests and independent audit results are regenerated after the guard change
goals.title: A legacy known-good backup is sanitized before default reset

goals.origin: The first settings foundation renamed af_test_mode only in camera-gui and camera-service. A complete allocated-segment inventory then found the same generated camera-property proxy in the boot-time msg2dbus service and in camera-expose, hex-writer and odindb-send. Leaving those clients on the retired identity would create a split D-Bus schema despite the GUI appearing correct.
goals.required_behavior: Every official executable with an allocated runtime reference to the selected property slot is rebuilt from its exact official hash using same-size identity edits. camera-gui, camera-service, msg2dbus, camera-expose, hex-writer and odindb-send use burst_preset, setBurst_preset and burst_presetChanged wherever their original generated proxy exposed the old identity. No unrelated executable, code path or capture behavior changes.
required_evidence: a complete scan of the official system bin, lib, lib64 and etc trees identifies every file containing the old identity and distinguishes allocated runtime strings from non-runtime symbol tables
each modified client is bound to its exact official input and exact output hash with unchanged file size
allocated PT_LOAD scans find no af_test_mode, setAf_test_mode or af_test_modeChanged in any modified runtime component
the boot-time msg2dbus service and both ends of the GUI-to-camera-service property path expose the same dedicated identity
independent delta checks prove every auxiliary client changed only the declared equal-length property, setter, signal or diagnostic-format string spans
goals.title: A renamed camera property is consistent across every official runtime client

goals.origin: The dedicated burst_preset property retained the official unsigned-short setter semantics, which accepted arbitrary values. A stale or mismatched D-Bus client could therefore persist a value outside 0 through 3 even though the menu exposed only four entries, forcing avoidable startup recovery on the next boot.
goals.required_behavior: The public CameraObject burst_preset setter accepts only 0, 1, 2 and 3. Any larger unsigned-short value returns without changing the current setting or invoking persistence. Valid values and the stock settings-lock behavior follow the original CameraSettings setter path. Profile restore remains on the stock private setter after the startup guard has validated the file.
required_evidence: the exact official public setter entry is replaced by one audited branch into a zero-filled executable cave while the remainder of its original body stays byte-exact
the helper compares the requested value with 3, rejects unsigned values above it, preserves the original settings-lock test and tail-branches to the untouched stock private setter for valid writes
machine-code emulation proves values 0 through 3 reach the stock setter unchanged, values 4 and 65535 return without reaching it, and a locked settings object rejects every value
startup guard tests independently accept every valid persisted preset and reject duplicate, malformed and out-of-range values
independent delta review proves the new code changes only the declared public-setter hook and helper cave and contains no capture, sensor, RAW or storage operation
goals.title: The public burst setting rejects values outside its four-entry domain

goals.origin: The retired preset backend and the dedicated settings foundation both used the executable cave beginning at 0x7ca854. Applying the older backend after the new foundation would silently overwrite the 0 through 3 rejection helper and could reintroduce the same settings and startup regressions that the rebuild was intended to remove.
goals.required_behavior: Every capture-routing layer starts from the exact hash of the current dedicated settings foundation. It may extend the valid-write helper only by an exact replacement that retains rejection of values above 3 and the stock settings-lock behavior. All additional helpers occupy disjoint, previously zero-filled spans inside existing executable segments; no program header is extended and no retired af_test_mode runtime identity is restored.
required_evidence: the backend input hash equals a reproducible build of the current settings foundation rather than an older v9 or raw official camera-service
machine-code emulation proves the composed setter still rejects invalid and locked writes while valid values persist through the untouched stock private setter before refreshing effective bit depth
the control and selector helper spans are non-overlapping, begin from the exact expected foundation bytes and fit entirely inside already mapped executable regions
all ELF program headers remain byte-exact to the settings foundation and allocated runtime scans retain only burst_preset identities
the composition report keeps P14_6 and P14_9 noninstallable until their separate native leaf-shutter schedulers and RAW-to-3FR completion paths are implemented and verified
goals.title: Capture routing must compose with the settings foundation without overwriting it

goals.origin: The retired native-leaf marker layer hooked the HAL stopped-state exit and forwarded its private finalize sentinel for every stopped capture session, relying on downstream code to turn it into a no-op when the private state was clear. That still inserted experimental calls and timing into P16_3 and stock P14_3 teardown, contrary to the required isolation and capable of reproducing unrelated capture or storage regressions.
goals.required_behavior: Only an exact P14_6 or P14_9 marker may arm private leaf ownership, translate a private mode, stage the next leaf preparation or send the private finalize sentinel. P16_3, P14_3, single capture, invalid values, stale state and failed marker propagation must use the official request, HAL and librcam behavior without a private message, state transition or synthetic success.
required_evidence: instruction-level tests prove capture-parameter markers are zero for P16_3, P14_3 and invalid values and distinct only for P14_6 and P14_9
the shooter clears stale marker state before every session and copies private request magic only after the matching current capture marker is observed

the HAL stores a bounded private-session flag only after exact request-magic translation and the stopped-state finalize hook returns through the stock path without calling the private sentinel for an unarmed session
librcam emulation proves stock modes cannot set ACTIVE, STAGED, NEEDS_RESTORE or P14_9 state bits and cannot call private prestart, restore or sentinel handling
mode change, marker mismatch, error, finalization and deinit tests prove private ownership is cleared or recovered without altering the official P16_3 and P14_3 RAW-to-3FR path
goals.title: Private leaf-session messages must never run in stock P16_3 or P14_3 sessions

goals.origin: The retired P14_9 deferred-transfer candidate released the serial CAPSEQ path while the previous SLVS-EC receive was still active. Exact IMX861 driver recovery later showed that start_exposure and start_transfer both mutate one sensor object, including exposure fields at +0x620, +0x628 and +0x630, state at +0x650, and the same timing-generator and receiver instance. Starting the next exposure before the previous receive is terminal can overwrite shared state or disable and reconfigure hardware still owned by the preceding frame, reproducing shutter actuation without a formed RAW, permanent writing, error 20 or a deadlocked camera.
goals.required_behavior: P14_9 must not admit another sensor exposure merely because a host wait was converted to a private PENDING result. Before the next exposure, the previous receive must be terminal, or an independently audited sensor-side engine must provide a separate immutable generation, timing-generator or receiver ownership context that is joined to the exact request, hardware frame, RAW buffer and 3FR-close transaction. Shared IMX861 fields and the same receiver or timing generator may never be reused while the previous generation is active. Missing, stale, duplicated or mismatched ownership fails closed through bounded official recovery and never becomes synthetic sensor, RAW or persistence success.
required_evidence: exact driver analysis proves start_exposure writes shared offsets +0x620, +0x628, +0x630 and +0x650 and operates the same timing-generator object used by start_transfer
exact transfer analysis proves the official call keeps ownership through the real SLVS-EC receive wait and that no per-frame receiver context argument exists
an executable state model rejects a second exposure while a receive generation still owns the shared sensor object and accepts the stock drain-before-reuse order
the retired deferred-transfer candidate is explicitly classified as unsafe and is not used as a foundation for a new camera binary

any future concurrent design binds request id, generation, hardware frame id, RAW buffer id, sensor result and 3FR close before releasing ownership, while P16_3 and P14_3 remain byte- and behavior-identical to stock
goals.title: Deferred RAW receive must not re-enter the shared IMX861 global-shutter controller

goals.origin: The first private 6fps state engine restarted its 167/167/166 ms clock before the asynchronous resource-readiness result was known. If readiness arrived late, the delay was charged to the next frame and could shorten the following exposure-to-exposure interval; starting the clock only after the previous receive completed would instead add a second full period and collapse cadence toward 3fps.
goals.required_behavior: For P14_6, the repeating 167, 167 and 166 ms budgets begin only when the official readiness callback returns true and is about to admit that exposure. The next exposure is considered only after the preceding stop/readout transaction has reached its real terminal event and any required internal-capture buffers are free. Early completion waits only the remaining budget; late completion proceeds without an additional full-period delay. False, duplicated, stale, changed-preset or failed readiness never advances the cadence epoch. P14_9 and all stock modes do not use this limiter.
required_evidence: exact state-graph analysis proves the private frame-complete transition enters WaitForBuffers only from the official 0x3ea terminal event after stop/readout completion or pending-buffer release
instruction-level inspection proves wait entry and cadence timer expiry only request official readiness and never restart or advance the cadence epoch
instruction-level inspection proves only the first valid P14_6 ready=true callback for the current wait state starts or restarts the clock and advances the 167/167/166 phase

an executable timing model covers immediate readiness, delayed readiness, receiver-over-budget, false retries, duplicate callbacks and preset changes without allowing shared-sensor re-entry or a sub-budget exposure interval
P16_3, P14_3, P14_9, invalid values and all failure paths retain stock or fail-closed behavior without cadence-state contamination
goals.title: P14_6 cadence is anchored to actual exposure admission

goals.origin: After the P14_6 admission callback was corrected, its helper grew through 0x906024 and overlapped the native-leaf layer's former fixed helper slot at 0x906000. The exact-zero precondition stopped the build, but reusing the old address would have overwritten the end of the cadence callback and recreated UI, capture or storage failures in a composition that looked valid at the individual-layer level.
goals.required_behavior: Each new binary layer must derive or audit the complete occupied interval map of the exact input binary before choosing executable or writable storage. Every new helper, state word, relocated metadata range and loader extension must be pairwise disjoint from all earlier-layer ranges and fit inside a segment with the required permissions. A hook may replace an earlier hook only when its exact before bytes are bound, the replacement is explicitly declared as a chaining composition, and the earlier behavior is reached through a verified tail path. A prior fixed address is never reused merely because it was empty in an older input hash. Any undeclared overlap, nonzero cave byte, range drift or permission mismatch fails before an output directory or package is created.
required_evidence: the exact input binary and its preceding manifest are hash-bound before composition
an interval audit includes every preceding helper, state, hook, metadata and guard range plus every proposed new range and proves pairwise disjointness
all proposed code spans are fully file-backed executable bytes and begin with the exact expected zero content while private state is loader-zeroed writable memory
boundary mutation tests move or enlarge a preceding helper into each proposed slot and the build refuses before writing output
the final composed binary independently disassembles every helper and proves all earlier-layer helpers and official protected ranges remain byte-exact
goals.title: Every composed executable helper span is disjoint from every earlier layer

goals.origin: A broad symbol search found SENC shutter continuous-mode and output-count controls and initially made a sensor-side burst engine look plausible. Architecture-correct call recovery later showed that the production IMX861 driver uses timing-generator APIs but does not call senc_shu functions, while the observed production output_mode=1 shutter sequence belongs to the 100 Hz ADS6401 ToF sensor and the remaining callers are test or timecode paths. Treating those calls as XCD evidence could revive the unsafe deferred-transfer design and again produce shutter actuation without a formed RAW or 3FR file.
goals.required_behavior: No XCD leaf-shutter or main-camera burst capability may be inferred from a generic SENC symbol, an ADS6401 sequence, a test binary, a timecode generator or an unproven output-number encoding. A new high-speed path must be traced through the production IMX861, EXMCU and XCD lens command chain and must bind every physical exposure to its exact ExposureId, receive generation, RAW buffer and successful 3FR close. Unknown pulse-count semantics, missing production callers or a receiver without per-frame ownership fail closed and keep P14_9 blocked.
required_evidence: architecture-correct call recovery classifies every production senc_shu caller and proves whether it belongs to ADS6401, timecode, test code or the main IMX861 capture chain
the exact production IMX861 timing-generator configuration records its trigger type and output-number value without interpreting the output-number encoding beyond proven evidence
the EXMCU and XCD lens path is traced from command admission through leaf actuation, SLVS-EC receive completion and RAW dequeue for every physical frame
stock-log evidence binds each exposure session to its own ExposureId and confirms the corresponding RAW-to-3FR close rather than relying on shutter sound or counter movement
P14_9 remains unavailable unless an executable model and exact binary audit prove independent per-frame ownership with bounded failure recovery
goals.title: Generic SENC repeat controls are not evidence of an XCD leaf-shutter burst path

goals.origin: The earlier lightweight call scanner was built around ARM32 relocation and instruction rules. Running it against the AArch64 camera libraries returned incomplete or empty relationships, which could have been misread as proof that a function was unused. An ELF64 AArch64 scanner using PLT relocations, direct dynamic-symbol targets and EH-frame function boundaries recovered the missing production callers.
goals.required_behavior: Call-graph claims for an AArch64 component must come from an architecture-aware ELF64 analysis that resolves AArch64 PLT relocations and direct symbol targets and assigns call sites to defensible function boundaries. Empty or missing output from an ARM32-only or architecture-mismatched scanner is an analysis failure, never evidence of no caller. Safety-critical results must be cross-checked against independent disassembly at the exact call sites before they may affect a firmware design or release decision.
required_evidence: tool tests cover exact AArch64 PLT call sites, direct dynamic-symbol calls, EH-frame function ownership and missing-symbol fail-closed behavior
the analyzed ELF class, machine architecture, input hash and requested symbols are recorded with every call-reference report
at least one independent disassembler confirms each safety-critical target and call-site address used in the conclusion
an architecture mismatch, unresolved relocation, missing function boundary or empty result is reported as incomplete evidence and cannot be converted into a no-call claim
the final feasibility audit consumes the exact architecture-correct reports and preserves P14_9 as blocked wherever the production ownership chain is not proven
goals.title: AArch64 production call graphs require architecture-correct symbol and function ownership recovery

goals.origin: The retired private request 9 path was initially treated as the beginning of a multi-frame EXMCU burst protocol. Exact binary recovery later proved that its handler only changes the SensorHdlr contCap property and sends one bridge response. The official contCap branch only keeps the sensor out of sleep and standby during teardown; it does not issue another XCD leaf-shutter actuation, start another exposure, create a receive generation, assign an ExposureId, dequeue a RAW buffer or close a 3FR file. Treating the acknowledgement as frame progress can reproduce shutter-state drift, missing files, permanent writing or error 20.
goals.required_behavior: A retained sensor or contCap acknowledgement is only a session-state control and never counts as a captured frame. Every repeated XCD exposure must have a proven physical leaf-shutter command sequence, main-sensor exposure admission, terminal SLVS-EC receive, immutable frame identity, RAW buffer ownership and successful 3FR close. A private command may retain or finalize state, but it may not report burst progress or success unless those per-frame events are bound and verified. Missing actuation, receive, identity or persistence evidence fails closed and leaves P14_9 unavailable.
required_evidence: the official EXMCU exposure dispatcher command set is enumerated and any private command id is explicitly distinguished from an official multi-frame command
compiled call-target inspection proves whether a private handler reaches the exposure transaction entry, XCD leaf commands, main-sensor receive creation and a real response path
the exact contCap branches are shown to affect only retained power or teardown state and are not interpreted as a scheduler or frame generator
an executable protocol audit rejects an acknowledgement-only sequence and accepts only a sequence that binds each leaf actuation, ExposureId, receive generation, RAW buffer and 3FR close
stock P16_3 and P14_3 paths remain free of private retained-state messages, while P14_6 and P14_9 stay noninstallable until their complete per-frame chains pass
goals.title: Retained contCap state is not a leaf-shutter burst engine

goals.origin: Exact EXMCU recovery shows that StopExpo leaves the exposure controller in state 2, while UpdateStillExpo applies new shutter, aperture and gain fields only in state 0 but sends a zero-status response even when the update is ignored. The three RestoreLens variants are also not a burst API: host type 0 is the normal stop-exposure restore, type 1 is the explicit restore callback, and type 2 is called during camx_v2 initialization to clean up inherited state. The EXMCU type-2 branch returns the controller to idle through restore helper 0x08072e08 but does not prepare or actuate another XCD exposure. Mistaking either acknowledgement for an interframe transition can reuse stale exposure parameters or count a non-frame as burst progress.
goals.required_behavior: A native-leaf burst implementation must own an explicit, verified transition from one terminal frame to the next admitted frame. It may update per-frame exposure parameters only when the EXMCU proves that the values were applied to the intended generation, and it may not treat UpdateStillExpo success or any RestoreLens response as preparation, actuation or frame completion. Restore type 2 remains initialization cleanup unless a separately implemented path proves a bounded interframe contract. Every repeated frame still requires readiness, leaf preparation, physical actuation, sensor receive, immutable identity, RAW ownership and 3FR persistence.
required_evidence: exact host call graphs bind RestoreLens type 0 to normal StopExpo, type 1 to the explicit restore callback and type 2 to camx_v2 initialization
exact EXMCU state analysis proves PreStart accepts idle state 0, StopExpo enters state 2, UpdateStillExpo writes fields only in state 0 and its response does not distinguish an ignored update
the RestoreLens type-2 branch is shown to perform cleanup and return to idle without calling the prep, open-close or main-sensor exposure transaction entries
an executable transition model rejects update acknowledgement and restore acknowledgement as frame progress and requires a fresh admitted per-frame chain
tests cover update while idle and busy, all restore types, stale parameters, missing restore, duplicate acknowledgement, abort and recovery while stock P16_3 and P14_3 remain unchanged
goals.title: Stock update and restore variants are not a hidden interframe repeat transition

goals.origin: The retired P14_6 staged-prestart candidate called X2Bridge_PreStartExpo immediately after a successful StopExpo. Exact EXMCU state recovery proves that StopExpo leaves the controller in state 2, while PreStart performs physical preparation only from state 0. In every nonzero state the PreStart handler returns zero without changing the controller to state 1. The candidate interpreted that ambiguous zero as success, set STAGED, skipped the next stock PreStart and skipped per-frame RestoreLens. That can leave the lens and capture controller stopped while the host believes the next frame is prepared, producing an unresponsive shutter, missing RAW or 3FR files, permanent writing, error 20, or broader UI and capture-state drift.
goals.required_behavior: A burst scheduler may mark a next frame prepared only after it proves both command success and the required physical controller transition for the same immutable generation. A zero-status response from PreStart while the EXMCU is prepared, stopped or recovering is an ignored request, not success. After StopExpo state 2, the implementation must complete a verified transition to idle before a fresh PreStart, or introduce and independently prove an explicit atomic interframe transition. It may never skip the stock next-frame PreStart or RestoreLens on an acknowledgement alone. Any ambiguous state, response, generation or physical transition fails closed through bounded official recovery.
required_evidence: exact EXMCU analysis proves StopExpo leaves controller state 2 and PreStart changes state only when entered from state 0
instruction-level inspection of every candidate identifies the exact state at each staged PreStart call and rejects any success predicate based only on a zero return value
an executable model reproduces the ambiguous zero response in state 2 and proves that STAGED, duplicate-prestart suppression and restore suppression remain false
negative tests reject missing state proof, stale or duplicate acknowledgements, skipped restore, skipped fresh PreStart, and generation mismatch
the retired P14_6 staged-prestart artifacts are explicitly noninstallable and no future package may inherit their helper or state model without passing this gate
goals.title: A zero-status PreStart response must not be treated as accepted preparation

goals.origin: Exact librcam recovery corrected an earlier assumption about the stock start path. The call through manager offset +0x25118 immediately before capture setup is _expm_print_expo_hist, not the Hasselblad exposure-transfer proxy. X2Bridge_UpdateStillExpo is instead reached asynchronously from expm_on_ae_update through the proxy slot at +0x25138. The EXMCU accepts and copies that shutter, aperture, gain and auxiliary exposure tuple only while its controller is idle state 0, yet returns the same zero status when the controller is busy or stopped. A private rearm after StopExpo can therefore prepare or actuate with an older tuple unless the intended values and immutable frame generation are applied and acknowledged together.
goals.required_behavior: A private P14_6 or future P14_9 interframe transition may report APPLIED only when it atomically validates the expected controller state, session token, capture generation, next frame id and complete intended exposure tuple, installs that tuple, and enters the verified prepared state for the same generation. Ordinary UpdateStillExpo or PreStart zero responses are never sufficient. A lens-only rearm may overlap the prior frame's receive only after that receive has started and owns an immutable current-frame context; APPLIED preparation never authorizes the next main-sensor exposure until the prior receive is terminal and its RAW buffer ownership is proven. With intentional AE lock, reuse of a prior tuple is allowed only when its hash and source generation are explicitly carried into the next-frame contract. With per-frame AE, the new tuple must be bound before actuation. STALE, BUSY, IGNORED, duplicate, mismatch and timeout outcomes remain distinct and fail closed without suppressing stock cleanup.
required_evidence: exact official librcam analysis maps +0x25118 to _expm_print_expo_hist and +0x25138 to the Hasselblad proxy, preventing another mistaken call-site interpretation

exact EXMCU analysis proves UpdateStillExpo copies the complete exposure tuple only in idle state 0 and returns an indistinguishable zero-status response when ignored in stopped or other non-idle states

an executable protocol model rejects stale generation, wrong session or frame id, incomplete tuple, ordinary zero acknowledgement, duplicate apply, wrong controller state, a receive that has not started and an unowned receive; it may accept one tuple-bound lens rearm before receive terminal but must still reject next-sensor start until terminal receive and RAW ownership

goals.origin: The official camx_v2_stop_expo path calls one synchronous still_transfer operation before RestoreLens. Exact recovery of hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer shows that this single call first enables the SLVS-EC receiver, waits for the link, sends the start-transfer request, sleeps 5 ms and only then blocks in wait_end_reciving. Moving RestoreLens and PreStart before still_transfer would postpone the current RAW transfer instead of hiding work under it; leaving them after still_transfer preserves safety but loses the only measured overlap window. The earlier staged-prestart attempt also ran before a legal stopped-to-idle transition. A correct high-speed path therefore needs an explicitly owned seam after current-frame receive start and before its terminal wait, while keeping next-frame sensor actuation behind the terminal boundary.
goals.required_behavior: For a private native-leaf mode, the current frame's receiver IRQ, link readiness and start-transfer acknowledgement must be established and bound to its immutable session, generation, ExposureId and RAW destination before any overlapping lens work. Only inside that owned receive window may the scheduler complete stock RestoreLens option 0, observe its full successful controller return to idle, bind the intended next-frame exposure tuple and perform one fresh leaf PreStart. The current receive then remains authoritative until terminal success and RAW ownership; only afterward may the next main-sensor exposure advance. A restore, rearm, receive, release, timeout, storage or identity failure cancels the staged frame and executes bounded stock cleanup exactly once. Stock P16_3 and P14_3 must retain their original synchronous ordering.
required_evidence: exact official librcam analysis proves the receiver-enable, link-ready, start-transfer, 5 ms sleep and blocking receive-terminal order inside hb_exmcu_global_shutter_start_transfer

exact EXMCU analysis proves successful RestoreLens option 0 completes its restore helper, exposure-sequence completion, controller transition to idle state 0 and bridge response before a fresh PreStart is considered

an executable phase model rejects lens rearm before receive start, receiver identity mismatch, duplicate restore or prestart, next-sensor start before terminal, missing RAW ownership and every stale callback
candidate instruction-level inspection proves the private rearm executes only between the current generation's accepted start-transfer and terminal wait and that stock modes cannot enter the seam

live qualification binds equal-count start-transfer, RestoreLens, PreStart, FSync, terminal receive, RAW dequeue, JLS completion, 3FR close and buffer return events for every frame, including release and injected failure recovery
goals.title: Sensor receive start, leaf rearm and receive terminal are three distinct interframe phases

goals.origin: The first transfer-window candidate placed the private finalize sentinel at the first instruction of rcam_obj_expm_stop_expo. Its sentinel branch called resource and restore functions before the official prologue had saved x30, then executed ret without restoring the caller return address. The first bl therefore replaced x30 and could loop inside the helper, jump into the wrong instruction or crash the camera even though ordinary static branch-target checks passed.
goals.required_behavior: A helper entered before the official function prologue may call another function only after saving x30 on a 16-byte-aligned stack and must restore both x30 and sp on every private return path. A stock bypass must undo any private stack change before replaying the exact displaced prologue. Helpers entered after a proven official prologue may rely on the saved frame only when the exact function boundary and epilogue are bound. No branch-back, early return or failure path may leave a changed stack pointer or caller return address.
required_evidence: exact disassembly identifies whether every hook runs before or after the official x30-saving prologue
instruction-level inspection proves every pre-prologue bl is dominated by a 16-byte-aligned x30 save and every private ret is dominated by its matching restore
machine-code emulation covers stock bypass, successful private cleanup and failed private cleanup and proves the original x30 and sp values at each exit
negative mutations removing the save, either restore or stack rebalance are rejected
the final binary delta remains confined to declared hooks, helpers and loader mappings
goals.title: Every entry-hook helper that calls another function preserves the AArch64 return contract

goals.origin: In the first transfer-window state engine, a failed receive, restore, prestart or identity check could leave ACTIVE and NEEDS_RESTORE set while STAGED was clear. A later private mode request normalized the mode and fell through to the stock PreStart call without first returning the stopped controller to idle. The EXMCU can answer zero while ignoring that PreStart outside idle, recreating the retired fake-stage failure despite the new receive-window design.
goals.required_behavior: Before any fresh PreStart, the scheduler proves either that no restore debt exists for the active session or that a complete RestoreLens option-0 transaction has just succeeded and returned the controller to idle. An invalid, stale, premature or unadmitted staged state fails the current exposure request after bounded cleanup; it never silently converts that same request into a stock PreStart. Restore failure preserves debt and returns a real nonzero capture error. Successful fault recovery resets transient generation state before a later fresh request may proceed.
required_evidence: an executable state model covers every combination of ACTIVE, STAGED, NEEDS_RESTORE, RECEIVE_STARTED, RECEIVE_TERMINAL, NEXT_ADMITTED and ERROR_LATCHED
instruction-level paths prove fresh PreStart is unreachable from restore debt until successful full restore and is unreachable from an invalid staged consume in the same request
failure-path emulation proves nonzero propagation to the host while restore debt remains latched on cleanup failure
negative mutations that remove the debt check, convert recovery to same-request fallthrough or treat zero PreStart alone as proof are rejected
stock P16_3 and P14_3 preserve their exact official PreStart and RestoreLens paths
goals.title: Restore debt or invalid staged state can never fall through to an ambiguous PreStart

goals.origin: The transfer-window scheduler intentionally prepares the next leaf before it knows whether the user will keep holding the shutter. Its standalone librcam candidate added a magic finalize-sentinel handler, but the official system has no caller that sends that magic. Without a separately composed and verified upper-layer release or abort dispatch, the final speculative preparation can remain live after the burst ends and the manifest can falsely imply exact-once cleanup that is not reachable.
goals.required_behavior: Any mode that speculatively prepares a next leaf must include a real, private-session-only release, abort and teardown dispatch from the production upper capture state machine to the exact librcam cleanup handler. The dispatch is armed only after the private mode identity is accepted, is sent once when no next frame will be admitted, and is acknowledged only after stock RestoreLens has completed. Missing dispatch, stale session, duplicate release, transport failure or process teardown preserves visible failure state and bounded recovery; stock modes receive no synthetic message.
required_evidence: architecture-correct call tracing identifies the production end-of-burst and abort transitions that own the release decision
the composed camera-service, HAL and librcam binaries bind one immutable private session token through arm, release request, restore completion and state clear
instruction-level or machine-code tests prove no official caller can accidentally match the private sentinel and no stock mode sends it
normal release, one-frame release, mode switch, cancellation, timeout, transport failure, deinit and duplicate-release tests prove exact-once cleanup
a standalone librcam handler without its composed dispatcher remains explicitly noninstallable and cannot satisfy this gate
goals.title: Speculative leaf preparation requires a proven private-only release dispatch

goals.origin: Independent review of the transfer-window r2 candidate found that its entry hook returned from expm_on_ae_update whenever the private burst was active and exposure-locked. The official callback does substantially more than call X2Bridge_UpdateStillExpo: under the exposure-manager write lock it copies main and secondary exposure sets, dirty ISP registers, bracketing data, long-exposure data, highlight-recovery data and the complete AE result into manager-owned state before invoking the Hasselblad transfer proxy and unlocking. Returning at the entry can leave UI, metering, metadata, ISP state and synchronization stale even if the intended leaf tuple remains fixed.
goals.required_behavior: Intentional burst exposure locking may suppress only the exact Hasselblad +0x25138 transfer-proxy invocation that would replace the EXMCU still-exposure tuple. The rest of expm_on_ae_update must execute byte-identically, including validation, manager state copies, ISP dirty-state propagation, write-lock acquisition and release, tracing and stack checking. The private skip is allowed only for an active session after one successful physical PreStart; stock modes and unlocked private state must execute the original proxy call. No path may skip the lock release or depend on a stale callback return value.
required_evidence: exact official disassembly identifies the indirect transfer-proxy call at expm_on_ae_update address 0x20f234 and proves its return value is dead before the following lock-unlock sequence
candidate byte inspection proves the function-entry prologue and every instruction except the single declared proxy-call hook remain official
instruction-level emulation proves stock and unlocked paths issue exactly one original proxy call while active locked state skips only that call and rejoins at 0x20f238
control-flow and ABI checks prove every path reaches the official write-lock release, trace exit, stack canary and epilogue with preserved live registers
negative tests reject entry-level early return, skipped unlock, stock suppression, pre-PreStart suppression and any hook spanning manager-state copy operations
goals.title: Exposure tuple locking must not suppress the complete AE update callback

goals.origin: The private upper cadence and the official readiness queues can admit another exposure after the sensor receive is terminal while the X2D shooter's main RAW bout or optional fast-preview RAW route still owns the preceding frame.  The shooter increments +0x678 for the main root Bayer consumer and, when root_bayer_raw_rout exists, +0x698 for the routed fast-preview consumer before physical start.  Those counters are released only by their real callbacks.  Re-entering before both releases can overwrite or mismatch per-frame context and reproduce shutter actuation without a completed file, permanent writing, error 20 or a stuck capture session.
goals.required_behavior: For the private P14_6 path, the first exposure still passes through every official readiness and queue check.  After one private physical request has been issued, a later readiness call returns false while +0x678 is nonzero or while root_bayer_raw_rout exists and +0x698 is nonzero.  It may delegate to the untouched official readiness body only after those actual callback-owned counters are zero.  The gate never decrements a counter, signals an event, invents a RAW result or bypasses official full-link and queue limits.  Stock P16_3, P14_3 and single capture execute the official readiness function byte-for-byte; P14_9 remains blocked.
required_evidence: exact shooter analysis proves _x2dss_shoot increments +0x678 and conditionally +0x698 before cam_shooter_start_expo and identifies the matching synchronization objects

goals.origin: The transfer-window librcam scheduler can prepare the next XCD leaf during the current receive window, but its private finalize sentinel is unreachable without an upper dispatcher.  The official _cont_cap_finalize waits on the main +0x670 and optional +0x690 shooting objects before sending message 0x4f4f.  Dispatching earlier can restore a lens still owned by a frame; omitting dispatch can leave the last speculative preparation live after shutter release.
goals.required_behavior: Only an exact issued P14_6 session may request the private finalize sentinel, and it does so from the production 0x4f4f finalization path reached after both official shoot-done waits.  Successful acknowledgement clears private dispatcher ownership exactly once.  Failure remains visible and retryable in the downstream recovery state; duplicate finalization cannot issue a second successful restore.  P14_9, stock modes, a session with no issued frame, malformed state and stale requests send no sentinel.  The complete official stopped-state body always resumes.
required_evidence: exact official analysis binds _cont_cap_finalize order to _wait_shoot_done(+0x670), _wait_shoot_done(+0x690), message 0x4f4f and its production external-handler case

live qualification proves release after one frame and long bursts returns the XCD lens to official idle with equal admitted, RAW-returned, 3FR-closed and buffer-released counts
goals.title: Private speculative leaf release is dispatched only after official RAW drain

goals.origin: Several earlier native-leaf binaries remain in the workspace. Copying any of them by path or filename into a newer overlay can silently reintroduce already diagnosed crashes, stale metadata, restore debt or missing files.

No legacy librcam hash, full-AE-callback suppression, post-stop ambiguous PreStart or deferred receiver candidate may enter the component set.  A filename, prior PASS report or matching version label is not identity evidence.

goals.origin: The composed local candidate exposed 14-bit 9fps as an ordinary fourth menu value while its backend deliberately blocked physical admission.  A visible selectable item with no executable capture and storage route is a half-built feature: the UI can persist the choice, but the camera cannot produce the promised native-leaf 3FR sequence.

A preset that lacks any link remains disabled or absent from every installable candidate and cannot be silently accepted, persisted, remapped, downgraded, simulated or presented as working.  The four-option product requirement remains recorded, but an unreleased option is not an enabled camera feature.

goals.origin: A complete symbol and source-family sweep of official librcam 1.3.16.2 found similarly named frame-FSync and frame-end callbacks in fast, normal, smooth-switch and AEB metering states, rolling-AEB capture, rolling-single capture and the body mechanical-shutter master. Only the global-single capture family selects the native global exposure mode, registers the paired still FSync and frame-end callbacks, binds the accepted hardware frame id to the common-still result, validates that id at the final IRQ, emits frame-over event 0x23, disables the exposure IRQ and returns the stream. Borrowing another family as a shortcut would change shutter semantics or lose the authoritative still-photo identity.

Metering, rolling-AEB, rolling-single and body mechanical-shutter callbacks may not be reused, redirected or counted as XCD leaf-frame completion. If a held multi-frame state keeps callbacks registered across frames, it must reproduce the nonzero increasing FSync acceptance, actual-versus-predicted final-IRQ check, per-frame event 0x23 and exact cleanup for every frame without disabling or rebinding the shared IRQ path prematurely. Frame-over remains a physical exposure milestone and never substitutes for RAW, JLS or 3FR completion.
required_evidence: an exact-hash function and source-family inventory distinguishes every similarly named FSync and frame-end callback and records the absence of a named stock continuous XCD leaf capture state

goals.origin: The stock 1.3.16.2 trace used compression=false and delivered calibrated RAW directly to camera-service; it contained no JLS-success callback even though three 3FR files closed successfully. RG-189 incorrectly made a JLS completion mandatory for every route, which could reject a valid direct-RAW route or tempt an analyzer to relabel FullRaw delivery as JLS evidence.

A JPEG-LS route separately proves matching JLS completion, 3FR close and exact source-buffer return. Evidence from one format is never renamed or substituted for the other. Both routes retain immutable frame and exposure identity through their real terminal callback.

Exact section-relative comparison showed that the v4/v8 topology changed only two continuous-DSP flags and still_gdc_fast_preview from one buffer to two; the storage-critical calibrated RAW and JLS streams remained single-slot.

Existing official values are reported as baseline, never as candidate changes. Reordered, cloned or renamed groups are identified separately from scalar edits, and conclusions remain bound to the exact candidate hash.

the report lists official and candidate hashes plus every changed, added and removed section

goals.origin: The early 16-bit and selectable-capture topology patches enabled is_continous_capture_mode and doubled only still_gdc_fast_preview. Exact ownership analysis later proved that one still_calibrated_big_raw buffer is retained through camera-service and storage until the 3FR transaction releases it. Those early changes therefore did not create an overlapping RAW-to-file pipeline.

The candidate must provide distinct per-frame ownership across calibrated RAW delivery, packaging, destination write, close and exactly-once release, with bounded backpressure and abort behavior. A buffer-count-only edit without matching lifecycle and memory proof is rejected.

goals.origin: The first pass over the long ION trace counted repeated snapshots of still-active allocations as fresh allocations and equated topology vmem_heap_id 21 with the trace heap field.  That produced totals larger than the physical carveout and a false heap identity.  Exact replay showed the repeated records are idempotent refreshes and that camera-service topology allocations appear under logical ION heap 8, which spans physical carveout banks.
goals.required_behavior: Memory qualification decodes both initial snapshot and timestamped event records, treats an exact duplicate of an active allocation as a refresh, and maps topology streams to allocations using process identity, time, exact size and lifetime rather than numeric heap-id equality.  It proves both aggregate carveout headroom and an eligible contiguous physical gap.  Capacity alone never qualifies overlapping capture, storage concurrency, lifecycle safety or an installable preset.
required_evidence: all source archives, embedded ION traces, process snapshots, carveout maps and the sensor topology are bound to exact hashes and valid record framing
idempotent replay and a negative mutation test prove duplicate active-allocation refreshes cannot inflate peak memory
every free matches an active allocation with the same size, no active ranges overlap, and corrected peak usage remains below total carveout capacity
camera-service process identity plus exact allocation size and timing reproduces four graph creations containing thirty root BOUT buffers, one root ROUT-sized buffer and one calibrated RAW buffer
the report proves aggregate and contiguous capacity separately while explicitly leaving concurrency and lifecycle qualification false

goals.origin: The official FileWriter keeps one shared ShineIoInstance and is safe only because both FileIO admission and its worker pool are limited to one.  Every ShineIoFile::open overwrites the handle's single private-data pointer with that file object, while the completion adapter retrieves that pointer and dispatches the work id to it.  Raising either concurrency limit without separating callback ownership can send one frame's completion into another file, consume the wrong work id and leave the original RAW transaction waiting forever.
goals.required_behavior: Every simultaneously open ShineIoFile has an immutable completion route for its entire outstanding-work lifetime.  It either owns a distinct ShineIoInstance handle or uses a proven dispatcher keyed by a globally unique handle and work identity; no open operation may overwrite another in-flight file's private-data target.  FileIO admission and worker-pool limits increase only with this ownership change, and completion, close, error, cancellation and shutdown each retire exactly the matching work and handle.
required_evidence: exact official disassembly binds both concurrency limits to one, FileWriter to one shared ShineIoInstance, open to private-data overwrite, and the callback adapter to private-data lookup followed by onWriteComplete
a negative interleaving model reproduces cross-file callback routing and a stuck original transaction when two files share one handle
the corrected model proves distinct handles or a collision-free global work namespace preserve file, exposure, work and callback identity under reordered completion
library-level analysis proves the selected isolation design has independent context, queue, callback, private data and lifetime and identifies every remaining process-global disk state
live qualification shows overlapping writes with equal submitted, completed, closed and released counts under normal, timeout, storage-full, cancellation and shutdown paths
goals.title: Overlapping file writes never share one mutable ShineIO callback identity

goals.origin: The official FileIO pending and active QList state is mutated without an internal mutex. addWork calls pumpQueue synchronously, pumpQueue dispatches processItem through the virtual table, and a QFutureWatcher completion calls itemFinished. Raising the active limit makes several worker writes overlap, but it must not make queue admission, active-list mutation or ShineIoInstance rotation concurrent. Otherwise distinct handles can still be lost through a race in the shared FileWriter member or the unprotected lists can be corrupted.
goals.required_behavior: All queue, addWork, pumpQueue, processItem admission and itemFinished state transitions execute on one FileIO QObject owner thread. Only the actual write or rewrite function runs in the worker pool. Every future completion is marshalled back to that owner thread before active-list removal and the next pump. If any caller can enter from another thread, the candidate must add a proven serialization boundary before changing the active limit; atomic QSharedPointer reference counts alone are not a queue lock.
required_evidence: exact official decompilation binds addWork to synchronous pumpQueue, pumpQueue to the virtual processItem call and the worker future to an owner-thread completion watcher
all direct and signal-driven queue callers are inventoried and the QObject connection type and thread affinity are established rather than inferred from process IDs
a dispatch model proves three admissions rotate three distinct handles serially while shuffled worker completions retire only their matching active items
negative tests inject concurrent queue or completion entry and require rejection or serialization before any unprotected QList or shared instance mutation
live qualification records one owner thread for admission and completion plus distinct worker and ShineIO handle identities during overlapping normal, failure, cancellation and shutdown cases
goals.title: Parallel FileIO admission and completion remain serialized on one owner thread

goals.origin: The camera-storage Ghidra project uses image base 0x100000 while the executable PT_LOAD begins at ELF virtual address zero. The concurrency instructions appear at Ghidra addresses 0x214574, 0x214640 and 0x215f88, but their file offsets are 0x114574, 0x114640 and 0x115f88. Treating the analysis address as an ELF virtual address selects unrelated bytes and can silently corrupt the executable.
goals.required_behavior: Every patch point records analysis address, analysis image base, normalized ELF virtual address and program-header-derived file offset as separate fields. The builder derives the file offset from the normalized ELF address, asserts the exact official instruction bytes there, decodes both before and after instructions at the analysis address and refuses ambiguous, unmapped or multiply mapped targets. No identity mapping assumption is allowed merely because one PT_LOAD has equal ELF virtual address and file offset.
required_evidence: the exact Ghidra report records image base 0x100000 and the official ELF program headers record the executable mapping used for normalization
builder tests prove all three camera-storage patch points map to the expected 0x11xxxx file offsets and exact official bytes
negative tests reject using the raw 0x21xxxx analysis address, a wrong image base, an unallocated address and a mutated anchor
independent instruction decoding proves the two immediate edits and the branch target at their original analysis addresses
a complete binary delta proves no byte outside the three declared four-byte spans changed
goals.title: Binary patches never confuse Ghidra image addresses with ELF virtual or file offsets

goals.origin: Exact recovery of the XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 internal 0x12 through 0x15 command family found a real lens-side periodic shutter actuator. Its timer callback calls the same low-level exposure engine used by production, but increments its progress counter unconditionally even when the exposure call returns busy or fails. The completion bridge sends LensExpReply 0x32 only while one ordinary production request latch is armed, so the diagnostic timer has no generation, sequence, ExposureId, RAW-buffer or file identity for each tick.
goals.required_behavior: A high-speed native-leaf session may reuse the lens timer only after every accepted actuation receives an immutable session generation and frame sequence, progress advances from the real actuator-completion path rather than the timer attempt, and exactly one completion is propagated through EXMCU to a pre-armed host ExposureId and RAW buffer. Busy, missed, duplicated, stale, out-of-order and post-stop events must fail closed; an internal timer count, leaf movement or FSync edge alone never qualifies a stored frame.
required_evidence: the exact lens image and its non-zero linked-address bias resolve internal commands 0x12, 0x13, 0x14 and 0x15 plus their timer callback without treating table data as Thumb instructions
instruction-level analysis proves the stock timer callback ignores the exposure-call return value and increments an attempt counter before physical completion
the corrected lens path increments completion only from the real actuator terminal and emits generation, sequence, status and cancellation state for every accepted actuation
EXMCU and host models reject busy, missing, duplicate, stale, out-of-order and post-stop events and bind each accepted completion to one pre-armed ExposureId and RAW buffer
live qualification shows equal requested, accepted, leaf-completed, FSync, RAW-completed, 3FR-closed and buffer-released counts at the selected cadence before the preset becomes selectable
goals.title: Lens timer ticks and attempt counters are never accepted as completed photo frames

goals.origin: Exact EXMCU recovery proved that every ordinary LensExpRequest 0x31 registers one pending command in group 3, and Lens::onNetPacketReceived dispatches physical LensExpReply 0x32 to the handler that completes exactly that group. The group-3 slot rejects a second ordinary request while the first is pending. A scheduler that invents a timer tick, FSync edge, generic packet counter or parallel overwrite as completion can issue an uncorrelated leaf cycle or wake the wrong host frame.
goals.required_behavior: Every repeated native XCD leaf command uses the official request builder and at most one pending group-3 transaction. A new command is admitted only after the matching physical 0x32 terminal, and the scheduler binds its own immutable session generation and frame sequence around that official transaction without replacing or bypassing the pending-command manager. Timeout, busy, duplicate, stale, reordered and post-stop replies fail closed. The 0x32 terminal qualifies only lens-command completion; FSync, sensor receive, RAW ownership and successful file close remain separate required terminals.
required_evidence: exact official disassembly binds operation 5 to LensExpRequest 0x31 low nibble 3 and registration in pending-command group 3
exact official disassembly binds incoming packet id 0x32 to the response handler and that handler to completion of group 3 under the lens mutex
pending-manager tests prove a second group-3 request cannot overwrite the active callback or result and duplicate terminal replies cannot complete a later frame
a generation-aware scheduler model proves absolute-deadline admission, one request in flight, timeout and stop drain without using a timer attempt or FSync as the lens terminal
live qualification binds every admitted command to exactly one 0x32 terminal, matching FSync, RAW completion, destination-specific 3FR close and buffer release before P14_9 becomes selectable
goals.title: Standard LensExpReply 0x32 remains the only accepted leaf-command terminal

goals.origin: Exact XCD 35-100E and EXMCU recovery proved that the asynchronous LensExpReply 0x32 payload contains only two status bytes. The lens keeps one one-byte reply-destination latch and clears it after sending; the EXMCU parser copies only those two bytes and completes whichever group-3 slot is pending. Although overlapping ordinary requests are rejected, the wire reply carries no transaction sequence, so a late duplicate delivered after the next slot is armed could otherwise be rebound to the next frame.
goals.required_behavior: A repeated native-leaf scheduler must prove the underlying transport is ordered, exactly once and drained before rearming, or extend both request and reply with a validated transaction nonce.
