Timeout and cancellation quarantine the old generation until the transport and actuator are explicitly quiescent; they may never immediately reuse group 3. A time delay, expected status value, FSync edge or host-side sequence counter alone cannot turn an unsequenced 0x32 into proof of identity.
required_evidence: exact lens disassembly proves the 0x32 response is two status bytes and the asynchronous completion path uses one reply-destination latch with no transaction sequence
exact EXMCU disassembly proves the 0x32 parser receives only those two bytes and completes the currently pending group-3 slot without a wire transaction identifier
a negative interleaving test proves a late duplicate can complete a newly armed slot in the unprotected model
the selected fix proves ordered exactly-once drain or a collision-free nonce across normal completion, timeout, cancellation, duplicate, reconnect and generation wrap
live fault injection shows no stale 0x32 can advance leaf, FSync, RAW, 3FR or buffer ownership counters for a later frame
goals.title: Unsequenced LensExpReply 0x32 never crosses group-3 generations

goals.origin: The first transport review found sequenced SPI strings in the XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 image but initially could not resolve their references because the startup code copies the main image from flash 0x60016008 into low-address ITCM. Reconstructing that relocation exposed the exact production configuration: the object used by XMountInterface has SpiSupported byte zero, its initializer logs that byte, and SetSPI returns the not-supported error before activating the SPI modules. The same image therefore contains dormant sequenced SPI code while the production configuration selects NetI2C.
goals.required_behavior: Every mount-transport or exact-once claim must reconstruct the lens startup relocation, identify the exact configuration object passed by the production initializer, and trace every allowed interface transition. Strings, linked flash addresses, shell commands or dormant driver code alone never prove that SPI is active. For the exact XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 image, repeated native-leaf qualification must treat NetI2C as the selected transport and must not borrow the SPI sequence counter unless a new exact-hash binary and live trace prove that the production path changed.
required_evidence: the exact lens hash and startup copy loops prove the flash-to-ITCM relocation delta used for all code and string references
the production initializer pointer chain reaches one exact configuration object whose SpiSupported byte is zero and whose log call labels that byte
the interface switch function maps zero to I2C and one to SPI, rejects SPI when SpiSupported is zero, and is the only writer of the current-mode byte after zero initialization
the shell and protocol callbacks are traced through the same guarded switch function so no alternate unguarded SetSPI route is assumed

negative mutation tests reject a changed relocation, configuration pointer, support byte, guard, mode writer or lens hash, and live transport logs are required before any future SPI-based release claim
goals.title: Dormant SPI code is never mistaken for the selected XCD mount transport

goals.origin: Exact recovery of the production XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 NetI2C path proved that LensExpReply 0x32 is a seven-byte unsequenced wire packet and that a failed send requeues the same packet object. The retry counter starts at zero, permits twenty-nine requeues after the initial attempt, and sleeps one millisecond between attempts. Each attempt has a twenty-millisecond timeout for this packet under the supported bitrate range, so the configured retry window can accumulate 629 ms before queue and callback overhead. That spans several 6 fps or 8.845591 fps frame periods and can let an old identical 0x32 consume a newer group-3 slot unless identity or explicit quiescence is added.
goals.required_behavior: A custom repeated native-leaf path must never rearm group 3 while an earlier NetI2C packet can still be queued, transmitting, retrying or arriving. A fixed frame-period delay, the nominal 0x32 arrival time or a host-only sequence is insufficient. The implementation must either carry and validate a collision-free transaction nonce end to end, prove from the exact low-level driver that a failed attempt cannot have delivered a complete packet and establish a bounded drain, or abort and explicitly reset plus verify the selected NetI2C transport and lens actuator are idle before any new generation. The stock P16_3 and P14_3 paths remain unchanged; both custom P14_6 and P14_9 stay blocked until this fault path is closed.
required_evidence: the exact production initializer selects NetI2C, skips dormant SPI, and binds the concrete configuration, object and bitrate limits
instruction-level analysis proves the 0x32 packet length, zero-initialized retry counter, same-object requeue, twenty-nine requeues, one-millisecond retry delay and low-level timeout formula
the configured retry-window calculation is reproduced from exact constants and explicitly excludes unbounded queue, lock and callback overhead
negative interleaving tests show an old unsequenced 0x32 consuming a newly armed group-3 slot at both custom cadence classes, while the selected nonce or reset-and-idle design fails closed
live fault injection covers NACK, timeout, partial transfer, disconnect, cancellation and reconnect and proves no stale reply advances leaf, FSync, RAW, 3FR or buffer-release ownership
goals.title: Selected NetI2C retries never cross native-leaf generations

goals.origin: Exact recovery of the selected XCD 35-100E 1.9.17 NetI2C master path proved that its software wait returns after twenty milliseconds, but the timeout edge jumps directly to the software-lock release without invoking the LPI2C abort path or clearing the master handle state. The next attempt reinitializes the peripheral before the transactional start checks that handle state; if the old completion has not run, the start returns busy, while a completion in the timeout-to-retry gap can make the same unsequenced packet eligible to transmit again. The master configuration also programs pin-low timeout to zero, so the software wait is not a proven hardware delivery deadline.
goals.required_behavior: A NetI2C wait timeout is an ambiguous transport state, never an ordinary retryable send failure. Before releasing ownership, the implementation must prevent any new sender from entering, terminate the active LPI2C transaction, reset its hardware and software handle coherently, wait for both master-busy and bus-busy to clear, clear stale completion state, and report an explicit ambiguous-delivery result. The same unsequenced 0x32 packet may not be requeued from that result. Group 3 remains quarantined until an end-to-end nonce rejects duplicates or an explicit peer-visible reset and idle handshake proves the old generation cannot arrive. Stock P16_3 and P14_3 are not reclassified; custom P14_6 and P14_9 remain blocked until this path is implemented and fault-tested.
required_evidence: instruction-level control-flow proof shows the wait-timeout branch reaches software unlock without any abort, hardware-idle check, handle-state clear or stale-event drain
exact LPI2C setup proves pin-low timeout is disabled and exact transactional start proves a non-idle handle returns busy
negative interleavings cover completion just after timeout, retry before completion, peripheral reinitialization with a busy handle and a stale completion event waking a later caller
the corrected model keeps ownership through abort, reset and dual-idle verification, classifies delivery as ambiguous and rejects same-packet retry unless a validated nonce is present

live fault injection stretches SCL across the software timeout and covers final-byte NACK, lost completion IRQ, disconnect and reconnect while proving no old 0x32 completes a later group-3, RAW or storage transaction
goals.title: NetI2C master timeouts never unlock or retry an active hardware transfer

goals.origin: Exact recovery of the EXMCU message-length table proved that LensExpRequest 0x31 has a fixed five-byte application payload and LensExpReply 0x32 has a fixed two-byte payload. The stock request builder initializes all five bytes, while the XCD 35-100E handler consumes only request payload bytes zero through two and leaves bytes three and four unused. The lens reply builder writes semantic bits zero, three and five in its first byte plus the low status nibble in its second byte, leaving nine bits zero; however, the stock EXMCU handler expands every reply bit into its result object. Globally increasing either fixed length would therefore copy beyond the stock request object or change every caller, while exposing an identity bit to the stock result would alter completion semantics.
goals.required_behavior: P16_3 and P14_3 must retain the exact official five-byte 0x31 request, two-byte 0x32 reply and official reserved-byte values. A custom P14_6 or P14_9 identity overlay may activate only under an explicit patched-lens capability and custom-session marker. It must use only fields proved unused for the relevant operation, echo a marked sequence, validate it before completing group 3, and mask every overlay bit back to the official two-byte semantic result. An unmarked, malformed, stale, duplicate or wrong sequence fails closed without consuming the pending slot. Sequence wrap is allowed only after the transport timeout, retry and drain proofs guarantee no earlier packet with the same sequence can remain live.
required_evidence: exact EXMCU disassembly and table bytes prove fixed payload lengths 0x31 equals five and 0x32 equals two and identify all five initialized request bytes
exact lens disassembly proves operation three consumes request payload bytes zero through two only and the stock reply builder leaves the selected marker and sequence bits zero

an executable codec model proves stock round trips are byte-identical, custom marker and sequence round trips preserve semantic status, and wrong, duplicate, unmarked and wraparound replies cannot consume a newer pending group-3 slot
binary delta and disassembly prove stock paths retain official bytes, custom decoding masks overlay bits before the official result copy, and unsupported stock lenses cannot expose the custom presets
live qualification covers patched and stock lenses, normal sequence advance, wrap, delayed duplicate, timeout, disconnect and reconnect with equal leaf, FSync, RAW, 3FR and buffer-release identities
goals.title: Custom leaf wire identity preserves stock 0x31/0x32 framing and result semantics

goals.origin: The first local XCD fixed-length sequence component stored its custom token in exposure object byte two and its pending flag in byte three after treating those bytes as padding. Exact recovery of the official LensExpRequest 0x31 handler disproved that assumption: every accepted request clears byte two, overlap admission reads byte two, operations six through eight set it, operations one and ten write byte three, and operation three passes byte three into the physical shutter callback. The component could therefore lose its token, change stock admission or alter the native leaf command even though its wire codec tests passed.
goals.required_behavior: No custom sequence, capability, quarantine or scheduler state may occupy exposure object bytes zero through three or any other field merely because initialization first clears it. Every custom state byte must have independently proven allocation, ownership, initialization, reset, concurrency and lifetime, with all stock reads and writes exhaustively excluded. The conflicting XCD sequence component is withdrawn and may not be composed, packaged or installed; its replacement must preserve every official access to object bytes zero through three byte-for-byte.
required_evidence: exact official disassembly proves the request handler reads or writes exposure object bytes zero, one, two and three and identifies the operation-specific meaning of bytes two and three
a whole-image reference and call-flow audit inventories direct pointers, registered callbacks, initialization and every first-word access rather than relying on one decompiler type or zero-filled RAM
negative behavioral tests reproduce token loss, admission drift and operation-three argument corruption when custom state aliases bytes two or three

the replacement binary allocates or proves a disjoint state region, initializes and clears it on every session, timeout, cancellation and reconnect, and an independent final-byte audit rejects any access to stock bytes zero through three
all current sequence, transport, scheduler and historical regression gates are rerun against the exact replacement hashes before any package or camera test
goals.title: Custom lens state never aliases stock exposure object bytes

goals.origin: The first timeout-recovery draft proposed a private return code and made the worker recognize it, but had not proved that the code could never collide with an official error or survive the low-level bitwise merge with the lock-release result. A second draft also exposed a short ordering window by releasing the sender lock before making the old descriptor nonretryable, and initially ignored failures from stale-event clearing and lock release.
goals.required_behavior: A cleaned NetI2C timeout must use the existing descriptor retry state rather than an unproved private status value. While still holding the sender lock, it sets only that descriptor's retry counter to the exact terminal pre-increment value; the unchanged stock worker then increments past its retry ceiling and reports failure without requeue. Event clearing and lock release are checked operations, and either failure invokes the existing lens-MCU reset path. Normal success and ordinary non-timeout failure retry behavior remain byte-identical.
required_evidence: exact call-flow proves the low-level transfer buffer pointer is descriptor plus ten while the retry counter is descriptor plus eight
final-byte disassembly proves retry counter 0x1d is stored at buffer minus two before the sender lock is released
the unchanged stock worker increments 0x1d to 0x1e, compares it above 0x1d and reaches the terminal callback without requeue
fault tests cover stale-event clear failure, lock-release failure, handle non-idle and either hardware busy bit by taking the peer-visible lens reset path
binary comparison proves the normal result path and the complete ordinary worker retry path are unchanged
goals.title: Ambiguous NetI2C descriptors become nonretryable before unlock

goals.origin: The first EXMCU sequence component failed closed before emitting any custom request and depended on a separate unimplemented capability setter. Reusing the first ordinary operation-3 leaf exposure as a challenge avoids an undefined protocol operation, but an unsupported stock lens will legally ignore request bytes three and four and return an unmarked official reply. Rejecting that reply would strand the first group-3 completion and recreate the no-save failure.
goals.required_behavior: A custom P14_6 or P14_9 session starts with exactly one ordinary native-leaf operation-3 frame at the stock-safe cadence while carrying the fixed-length challenge. A correctly marked reply with the matching sequence qualifies the patched lens; an unmarked official reply still completes that first safe frame, records the lens as unsupported, and blocks every later custom high-speed request. A malformed marked, stale, duplicate or wrong-sequence reply is rejected. Capability, failure, pending and validation state reset on every session begin, terminal path, timeout, cancellation and reconnect, and the scheduler may not arm overlap before the probe reaches a terminal result.
required_evidence: behavioral tests prove exactly one probe is emitted before qualification and no second request is admitted while it is pending
a matching marked reply restores official two-byte semantics, completes group 3 once and enables later sequenced requests
an unmarked official reply restores the stock completion path for the probe frame, marks capability failed and blocks all custom continuation without leaving a pending slot
malformed length, wrong marked sequence, stale reply and duplicate completion fail closed without consuming or rebinding another frame
scheduler tests prove the probe frame uses the official safe leaf cadence and no transfer overlap or 6fps or 9fps rearm occurs before successful qualification
final-byte and live tests bind reset behavior to session begin, normal terminal, timeout, cancellation, lens disconnect and reconnect
goals.title: Patched-lens qualification uses one stock-safe probe frame

goals.origin: The fixed-length 0x31/0x32 overlay deliberately removes its marker and sequence before the official group-3 result copy, so both a matching patched-lens probe reply and an unmarked stock-lens reply look like ordinary success to the host. Keeping capability only in EXMCU-local RAM would let the host arm sensor overlap without knowing whether the lens qualified.
goals.required_behavior: After the first stock-safe probe frame reaches group-3 completion, the host sends the existing custom session QUERY and receives a dedicated capability field in the custom response. The field reports exactly unknown, patched-lens-qualified or unsupported; transient validation and probe bits never leak into it. The host remains in PROBING and forbids a second sensor or leaf arm until QUERY returns qualified. Unsupported, unknown, malformed, timed-out, stale or generation-mismatched results stop the custom session without entering fast cadence. Stock sessions and official 0x31/0x32 result semantics remain byte-identical.
required_evidence: EXMCU final-byte proof shows the custom response capability field is derived only from qualified and failed state bits and all other response bytes retain the established request-9 ABI
host final-byte proof shows a post-first-frame QUERY dominates the transition from PROBING to FAST and only the exact qualified value permits that transition
behavioral tests prove no second frame or transfer overlap can arm while capability is unknown, failed, stale, malformed or timed out
negative tests prove masking or omitting the host-visible field cannot silently qualify a stock lens and cannot strand the completed first frame
session end, abort, timeout, cancellation, disconnect and reconnect clear both EXMCU capability state and host qualification state
live traces correlate request-9 generation, probe group-3 completion, QUERY capability, subsequent leaf sequence, FSync, RAW and 3FR close
goals.title: Lens qualification is explicitly visible to the host scheduler

goals.origin: The retired P14_9 host guard reserved its 0x50-byte state at 0x005b8610 when the preceding leaf scheduler used only one word at 0x005b8608. The current transfer-window scheduler later expanded that leaf state to 40 bytes at 0x005b8608 through 0x005b862f. Layering the old guard or session binary onto the current scheduler would therefore overlap 32 bytes and let protocol callbacks corrupt leaf flags, frame identity, restore debt and error state.
goals.required_behavior: Every independently built component that extends a PT_LOAD BSS region must recompute its aligned address from the exact immediately preceding composed binary. No historical fixed address may be reused merely because it was loader-zeroed in an older foundation. The final composition must prove all private state intervals are pairwise disjoint, remain inside the intended RW PT_LOAD without colliding with a later mapping, and are initialized and reset by only their owning component.
required_evidence: the exact current transfer-window binary maps its 40-byte leaf state at 0x005b8608 through 0x005b862f and an audit rejects the retired host address 0x005b8610
the replacement host state is aligned from the current RW memory end and the final ELF program header covers its complete interval without changing file-backed stock data
an interval audit enumerates every private BSS block in the final camera-service, shooter, HAL and librcam composition and proves pairwise disjoint ownership
final-byte emulation alternates leaf-state and host-state writes and proves neither component changes any byte owned by the other
a negative mutation restoring the historical 0x005b8610 address must fail the composition gate before any package or camera test
goals.title: Private state allocations are recomputed after final binary composition

goals.origin: The first current-foundation host qualification draft correctly separated its BSS state but allowed a new P14_9 BEGIN while the transfer-window state might still contain an active frame, receive ownership, a staged prestart, restore debt or a latched error from the preceding session. Starting the stock-safe probe in that condition could overwrite lifecycle ordering even though the two memory blocks no longer overlap.
goals.required_behavior: The P14_9 IDLE-to-PROBING transition requires the entire current transfer-window leaf state word to be zero before BEGIN is sent. Any active, staged, receive-owned, restore-debt or error bit blocks the new prestart without sending BEGIN or arming a sensor or leaf operation. Existing terminal and deinit recovery owns cleanup; only a later fresh request after zero state may begin a probe.
required_evidence: final-byte proof shows the leaf state at 0x005b8608 is acquired and tested before the BEGIN helper is called
tests inject each individual transfer-window flag and representative valid multi-flag states and prove BEGIN, QUERY and fast-arm counts remain zero
after the established finalizer clears the leaf state, one fresh request emits exactly one BEGIN and one stock-safe probe frame
a negative mutation removing the nonzero-state branch is rejected by the permanent gate
no probe-start failure clears or fabricates ownership of a preceding frame
goals.title: A capability probe never starts over unresolved leaf state

goals.origin: The first current P14_9 RAW-dispatch layer armed its private HAL finalization state before invoking the librcam prestart callback.  If the second-frame host capability QUERY rejected an unsupported, unknown, malformed or timed-out result, librcam returned an error before any physical prestart, but the original HAL error branch did not clear the private arm.  Because the stopped callback is not guaranteed after a failed prestart, that stale state could survive into the next capture and issue a private finalize sentinel for a frame that never started.
goals.required_behavior: Immediately after the production prestart callback returns, a zero result preserves the exact armed P14_6 or P14_9 state and resumes the official success path.  Every nonzero result atomically clears the HAL private finalization state before resuming the original error path.  Disarming does not report sensor, RAW or storage success, does not invoke the finalizer, and does not alter shooter or librcam recovery ownership.
required_evidence: final-byte disassembly proves the original post-callback conditional branch is replaced by a helper that preserves w0 and selects the same success and error destinations
instruction-level tests prove a zero callback result preserves both exact private armed values while every representative nonzero result clears them before reaching the official error path
stock, unarmed and malformed private state cannot become armed through the result helper and no finalization sentinel is sent from this path
a negative mutation that removes the failure clear is rejected by the permanent binary gate
end-to-end failure tests cover unsupported lens, capability timeout, malformed QUERY, mode switch and retry and prove the next fresh capture starts with HAL state zero
goals.title: A failed HAL prestart disarms private finalization state

goals.origin: The capability overlay admitted EXMCU preset values two and three when preparing 0x31, but its underlying request-9 handler still accepted, stored and returned only preset three, while the host qualification layer opened a session only for P14_9.  P14_6 therefore had no complete BEGIN, stock-safe probe, QUERY and qualified transition even though downstream code could arm its private scheduler.
goals.required_behavior: P14_6 and P14_9 use the same bounded qualification lifecycle with distinct immutable preset identities two and three.  BEGIN stores the exact selected preset with token and generation; every active QUERY, repeated BEGIN, END and ABORT must match that preset; every response returns the bound preset.  Each mode performs one stock-safe first frame, waits for QUERY capability one before its second private arm, and aborts on unsupported, unknown, malformed, timed-out or cross-preset state.  Stock P16_3, P14_3 and single capture never enter this protocol.
required_evidence: EXMCU final-byte tests accept only preset two or three, store the actual BEGIN preset, reject cross-preset operations against an active session and return the exact bound preset
host final-byte tests begin and query both P14_6 and P14_9, preserve the selected preset across PROBING and FAST, and require exact capability one before either second private arm
the first frame of both custom presets normalizes to the complete official native-leaf path with transfer overlap inactive
mode-switch, stale-token, stale-generation, duplicate, timeout, disconnect and teardown tests cannot move a qualification result between preset two and preset three
a composed protocol matrix proves equal preset, token, generation and operation at host request, EXMCU state, response guard and XCD probe state before backend or UI selection becomes releasable
goals.title: Both custom cadence presets share one end-to-end lens qualification contract

goals.origin: The first dual-preset composition repeated an inherited statement that camera-service still blocked P14_9.  Final-byte inspection of the exact composed camera-service disproved it: the public setter accepts preset three, the private route accepts presets two and three, and the capture-parameter helper emits the distinct P14_9 marker.  The stale text would have sent later work toward patching a branch that no longer existed.
goals.required_behavior: Every open or closed release gate is derived from the exact final component bytes and their current composition, never copied unverified from an upstream manifest.  When a later layer closes an earlier blocker, the final manifest removes that blocker and replaces it only with the next demonstrable boundary.  A claimed missing backend route must identify the rejecting final-byte branch; if all admission branches are present, work proceeds to cadence, frame identity, storage, UI, packaging and live qualification instead of adding a redundant patch.
required_evidence: final camera-service disassembly proves the public preset guard accepts zero through three and caches preset three only while settings are unlocked
the final private state route accepts only presets two and three and maps both to the isolated continuous sequence while stock presets retain their official routes
the final capture-parameter helper emits distinct A6 and A9 markers and emits zero for every stock or invalid preset
a negative mutation of the preset-three route or A9 marker fails the backend-admission audit
the final composition manifest contains no inherited blocker contradicted by its exact binaries, and every remaining blocker names concrete missing final-byte or live evidence
goals.title: Release blockers are re-derived from the final composed bytes

goals.origin: The first dual-preset host qualification layer preserved P14_6 and P14_9 through BEGIN, QUERY and capability validation, but then rewrote both qualified presets to transfer-window mode two. The delegated transfer-window scheduler owns only one receive session and does not admit the next sensor start until the previous receiver-wide terminal; the observed terminal is about 169 ms, while the P14_9 sensor period is about 113.050667 ms. The final protocol labels were distinct but the physical schedulers were not.
goals.required_behavior: P14_6 and P14_9 may share lens qualification and wire framing, but must never alias after qualification to one physical cadence implementation unless that implementation proves both exact timing and ownership contracts. P14_6 may use the bounded single-receive transfer-window scheduler. P14_9 must use a separately identified scheduler with bounded multi-frame receive ownership, or fail closed before a second fast frame; it may not be relabelled as mode two, inherit a 169 ms receiver terminal, or claim the 8.845591 fps source cadence from menu state alone.
required_evidence: final-byte disassembly follows preset two and preset three from the qualified host branch to different physical scheduler destinations or proves preset three fails closed before a second fast sensor start
the P14_9 scheduler retains immutable session generation, exposure or FSync identity, root RAW frame id and concrete buffer ownership for at least three bounded in-flight contexts
an offline timing model and final-byte test prove that no 169 ms receiver-wide terminal dominates the 113.050667 ms P14_9 arm period
negative mutation that rewrites preset three to transfer-window mode two fails the permanent binary gate
live qualification separately measures P14_6 and P14_9 FSync cadence and equal-count RAW, JLS, 3FR-close and buffer-return terminals
goals.title: Distinct cadence presets retain distinct physical scheduler identities

goals.origin: The first dual-preset RAW-dispatch layer applied the conservative P14_6 safety barrier to P14_9. After the first private frame it refuses every later admission while shooter +0x678 or optional +0x698 is nonzero, and it carries only one global frame-issued bit. Those conditions deliberately wait for the preceding RAW consumers to drain and therefore serialize the high-rate path even if the sensor and leaf schedulers are later made asynchronous. Replacing only the host wait cannot produce 9fps and risks rebinding one global state to several physical frames.
goals.required_behavior: P14_9 exposure admission must reserve one free slot from a bounded ownership ring before physical actuation, not require every earlier BOUT or ROUT consumer count to be zero. Each reservation carries an immutable session generation and request sequence, is joined exactly once to the next verified FSync and authoritative root RAW frame id, follows that same frame through JLS and 3FR close, and is freed only by its matching real buffer-return terminal. Ring full, missing or nonmonotonic identity, duplicate callback, stale generation, abort, timeout and mode switch fail closed without overwriting an active slot or fabricating a release. P14_6 may retain its conservative one-frame barrier until its own overlap is proved; stock P16_3, P14_3 and single capture retain official readiness behavior.
required_evidence: an exact final-byte audit identifies the current P14_9 zero-inflight checks at shooter +0x678 and optional +0x698 and proves why the single frame-issued state cannot own more than one admitted exposure

an executable bounded-ring model covers reserve, FSync bind, root-RAW frame-id bind, storage terminal, exact release, ring-full backpressure, generation reset and every duplicate, stale, gap and out-of-order fault
the binary implementation reserves before sensor actuation, never decrements official consumer counters, and binds each slot to the concrete RAW object plus frame id before downstream dispatch
the exact storage callback frees only the slot whose immutable frame id matches its per-frame context and cannot clear or finalize any neighboring in-flight frame

instruction-level concurrency tests sustain at least three distinct in-flight contexts without aliasing, while negative mutations restoring zero-inflight admission or a single global frame marker fail the gate
live qualification proves equal-count native-leaf actuation, FSync, RAW, JLS, 3FR close and buffer return with bounded queue depth and no error 20, permanent writing state, missing file or UI stall
goals.title: High-rate admission uses bounded per-frame ownership instead of a zero-inflight barrier

goals.origin: A follow-up exact decompilation disproved an intermediate assumption that the stock frame-timing array at shooter +0x740 was reserved before actuation and released by the 3FR storage terminal. The array is sized from the 30-entry full-link limit, but a timing entry is first claimed only inside the root RAW ROUT callback after a concrete frame id already exists, and it is cleared by the preprocess release callback. The independent BOUT postprocess object carries that same concrete frame id through storage, decrements +0x6bc at its own release callback, and never clears the timing entry. Treating those two lifecycles as one would leave P14_9 without immutable pre-actuation ownership and could release or overwrite the wrong state.
goals.required_behavior: Every high-rate implementation preserves the two official lifecycles exactly: ROUT timing entries remain RAW-arrival-to-preprocess objects, while BOUT postprocess objects remain per-frame storage ownership through the real storage release. Neither may be relabelled as a pre-actuation reservation. Before each P14_9 physical actuation, a separately proven bounded request identity must already exist and later join in order to verified FSync and the concrete RAW frame id before ownership is handed to the official postprocess chain. The official +0x6bc/+0x6b8 admission limit and queue-full checks remain authoritative and are never shadow-decremented. A rejected physical start must be stopped before cam_shooter_start_expo because its stock failure path terminates the camera service.
required_evidence: exact initialization evidence proves +0x738 and +0x740 are allocated from +0x6b8, while captured stock logs bind that capacity to 30 without claiming throughput
exact ROUT callback evidence proves a free timing entry is selected only after RAW arrival and is populated with the concrete RAW frame id before tag 0x1780 is attached
exact preprocess release evidence proves the timing entry is found by its context frame id and clears active, frame-id and valid fields there

exact BOUT and postprocess release evidence proves tag 0x1781 carries an independent per-frame storage object whose frame id survives until the real storage terminal and whose release decrements only official +0x6bc

exact start-exposure evidence proves official capacity is incremented before cam_shooter_start_expo and every nonzero start result enters a nonreturning process-exit path, so unsafe custom starts fail before that call

instruction-level tests reject mutations that allocate a timing entry before RAW, clear it from the postprocess terminal, bypass official capacity or substitute either official object for the missing pre-actuation request identity
goals.title: RAW timing slots and storage ownership are not conflated

goals.origin: Exact 1.3.16.2 decompilation and a captured successful stock sequence close the frame-identity gap left by the first P14_9 ownership model. The global-single FSync callback rejects nonmonotonic ids, writes the received id into both capture state and the exposure-info object, while the registered per-frame metadata callback passes its concrete callback id to metadata_update_per_frame_info, which queries that exposure-info object by the same id. In the stock log, ids 4708, 4713 and 4718 appear unchanged at FSync, ROOT RAW ROUT, ROOT RAW BOUT, postprocess storage completion and preprocess release. Later FSyncs arrive before the first storage completion, proving the downstream stock chain already permits at least three overlapping per-frame contexts. The gaps of five also disprove any assumption that still-frame ids must increase by exactly one.
goals.required_behavior: Custom P14_9 preserves the official frame-id namespace instead of inventing or translating an FSync-to-RAW id. Before actuation it may carry only a bounded generation plus request sequence. The next verified FSync binds the oldest eligible request exactly once to the official strictly increasing frame id; gaps are valid. Every later ROOT RAW, metadata, JLS, 3FR and release event must use that exact id. Storage completion is allowed to lag later actuations and must never gate the next start by itself. Abort or mode switch cancels only requests that have not actuated; already actuated or frame-id-bound official contexts drain under their original generation and may not bind into a new session.
required_evidence: exact FSync decompilation proves the global-single callback accepts only zero or a value greater than the prior id and writes the received id into capture state and the common-still exposure-info object
exact callback-table and metadata decompilation proves the per-frame metadata callback passes its callback id unchanged and the exposure manager is queried by that same id
captured stock evidence proves ids 4708, 4713 and 4718 match exactly at FSync, ROOT RAW ROUT, ROOT RAW BOUT, postprocess storage completion and preprocess release
captured timestamps prove FSync 4713 and 4718 both occur before storage completion of 4708, establishing at least three overlapping official downstream contexts without claiming 9fps qualification

an executable model accepts strictly increasing ids with gaps and exact cross-stage matches, but rejects duplicate or decreasing FSync, missing request ownership, mismatched RAW or storage id, stale generation and unsafe mode-switch rebinding
negative mutations of the FSync assignment, per-frame metadata forwarding, exposure-info query key, any one live-stage id or overlap ordering fail the permanent audit
goals.title: Official frame id joins FSync, RAW and storage exactly

goals.origin: Executable failure injection against the actual startup guard found sixteen paths across valid, malformed, legacy and missing camera.ini scenarios where stale-temporary cleanup or sync returned an error but the guard continued, renamed files and returned success. Earlier recovery tests exercised malformed input only and did not inject failures during the recovery transaction.
goals.required_behavior: Every cleanup, copy, permission, sync and rename failure returns a nonzero result before the next filesystem mutation or success report. At every interruption the live file is either its complete original contents or the complete validated replacement, and a fresh recovery run remains possible. Successful host tests establish process-level failure handling only: sync success is not a proof of target power-loss durability, and synchronous init ordering is not a proof that camera-service startup is conditional on guard success.
required_evidence: the actual guard runs in temporary host directories with each filesystem command failure injected independently for valid, malformed, legacy and missing profiles
each injected error causes nonzero exit with no later operation in the recorded trace
at every interruption camera.ini retains exact old or replacement contents, and a fresh run finishes recovery without losing the selected valid preset
a negative mutation removing a cleanup or sync error check is detected by the executable harness
target file and directory durability, Android init failure admission and stable camera-service profile loading remain explicit unproven gates until directly verified
goals.title: Settings recovery stops on every failed filesystem command

goals.origin: The project recap incorrectly treated the RG217 observation of three outstanding frame identities as disproving the earlier single calibrated-RAW buffer and single writer findings. The same successful stock log explicitly queues frame 4713 while frame 4708 is still processing. Identity-safe overlap upstream and serialized downstream processing coexist; neither finding cancels the other.
goals.required_behavior: Reuse of official frame identities and ownership must be assessed separately from producer cadence, downstream service rate and finite buffer capacity. Every 6fps or 9fps claim states its measured duration and backpressure behavior. Three outstanding RAW contexts, thirty upstream buffers, a sensor mode label or SSD sequential bandwidth never substitutes for measured calibrated-RAW, file-close and buffer-release throughput. Retaining sensor mode is an optimization hypothesis until measured; it is not established as the only bottleneck by a stock three-frame log.
required_evidence: the same hash-bound stock log demonstrates matching FSync, RAW and terminal identities together with the explicit postprocess queue-wait event
capture intervals, calibrated-RAW delivery intervals and storage-terminal intervals are reported separately with sample size and no steady-state capacity claim
native leaf actuation, sensor receive safety, downstream throughput and backlog remain independent qualification results
a new composition does not delete calibrated RAW, optional JLS or writer ownership gates merely because official frame-id reuse was proved
short bursts and sustained operation are distinguished by test duration, maximum queue depth, backpressure and complete file and release counts
goals.title: Queued RAW identities do not prove parallel downstream throughput

goals.origin: The original settings overlay inserted exec_start before the unconditional start camera-service command and left camera-service in the automatically started core class. Waiting for a recovery process to finish did not make either subsequent start conditional on that process succeeding.
goals.required_behavior: The boot-time recovery launcher requests the original camera-service from init only after the real guard returns zero. The unconditional direct start is removed and automatic class-start admission is disabled. Recovery or control-request failures remain nonzero. Init retains the original camera-service executable, credentials, options and SELinux transition; no shell-domain exec of the camera binary is substituted. Recovery writes and camera startup never overlap through this launcher.
required_evidence: actual launcher execution records no camera-service control request for any nonzero guard result and exactly one ctl.start request after a zero guard result
the final init overlay contains the synchronous launcher in place of the original direct start and marks the original camera-service disabled for class_start
the exact official property contexts and SELinux policy permit the guard shell domain to request ctl.start without adding privileges or changing camera-service domain
failure-injected guard execution composed with the launcher never starts camera-service after a failed cleanup, copy, sync, chmod or rename
target init control dispatch, property-service readiness during early-init, guard execution and camera-service startup ordering require live verification before installation eligibility
goals.title: Camera startup requires successful configuration recovery

goals.origin: The local official-capture backend marked P14_6 and P14_9 NOT_IMPLEMENTED in its manifest but sent every nonzero preset through group 18 and the stock slow-burst state. Selecting 6fps or 9fps could therefore run ordinary 3fps with a misleading menu label. The rebuilt UI/settings-only layer does not itself implement any capture preset.
goals.required_behavior: Each locally implemented capture preset must be checked against the effective drive mode, bit depth, shutter and stream identity immediately before native engine start. In the P14_3 baseline, only preset one with continuous drive, effective 14-bit, native leaf shutter, stream group 18 and global exposure is admitted. Unsupported or inconsistent continuous requests return a nonzero result through the official notification and cleanup path before engine start; they never report success, hang silently, use electronic shutter, or fall back to another labelled rate. Noncontinuous shooting preserves its original path. Backend rejection is not a substitute for disabling unavailable UI options or for live verification.
required_evidence: final-byte execution covers all four presets, invalid presets, effective drive overrides, bit depth, electronic shutter and group/global-exposure mismatches with caller-saved register poisoning
accepted P14_3 reaches the original engine call instruction with unchanged arguments and return address; all rejected continuous requests emit exactly one nonzero notification before any engine call
real official callback instructions propagate the failure without setting exposure-active fields, and the original reference-count cleanup and epilogue remain intact
negative mutations that admit an unsupported preset, bypass a format or shutter check, emit success, corrupt stack/registers or skip cleanup fail the instruction-level gate
the exact output binds the unchanged sensor configuration, native shooter and storage components and does not claim 3fps cadence or complete 3FR storage from an admission test
full Qt signal delivery, unavailable-option UI behavior, exception unwinding, target state recovery, leaf actuation and equal-count saved files remain explicit unverified release gates
goals.title: Unimplemented burst presets cannot silently enter another capture route

goals.origin: The first P14_3 negative-mutation harness accessed op_str on project disassembly dictionaries, whose actual field is operands. Positive cases ran, but the negative cases failed in test setup instead of exercising damaged instructions. The failed suite was not accepted. Updating the permanent registry also changes the composition evidence even when executable bytes remain identical.
goals.required_behavior: Every negative test resolves exactly one instruction using the real disassembler output schema, checks its original bytes and executes the deliberately damaged final binary. A missing or ambiguous mutation, unexpected exception, skipped case or setup failure is a failed gate, never proof of rejection. Fresh verification binds source, test, registry, component and configuration hashes before and after the run; prior candidate files and reports are preserved rather than overwritten or silently attributed to a new composition.
required_evidence: a native negative-test suite exercises unsupported-preset admission, bit-depth, shutter, group and global-exposure checks, success-code corruption, QString ABI, temporary destruction, cleanup bypass and live callee-saved register corruption
the harness uses address, mnemonic, operands and bytes from the actual project disassembler and requires a unique exact-byte mutation site
an explicit schema regression test rejects missing or renamed operands and ambiguous mutation sites before claiming any negative execution result
the complete applicable UI/settings and admission suite runs from the beginning with zero errors, failures or skips, and all before/after hashes remain identical
verification refuses an already occupied report location and never packages or claims live success from a passing host suite
goals.title: Negative-instruction tests execute against the actual helper schema and fresh evidence

goals.origin: Review of the first offline-passing P14_3 admission layer found new BL calls inside private caves without unwind metadata. Even the session-drive getter can allocate through its exit-drive override, so only removing error-text allocation would not close the gap. The replacement reuses official getter results at their original call sites, consumes a strictly local tag before dispatch and calls rejection through the original protected BLR. Assembly also rejected an absolute ADR operand; a checked local label fixes that syntax without guessing encoded bytes.
goals.required_behavior: Private admission code either has proven complete unwind metadata or introduces no call instruction or new frame. Every potentially throwing getter or Qt call retains a registered original call site and its applicable LSDA cleanup entry. Borrowed QString and QVariant arguments have exact ABI, lifetime and relocated addresses, never overlap live owned temporaries, and survive any retained copy. A local stream tag never reaches engine, sensor, settings or wire state. Failure and exception cleanup release the original notification references exactly once without claiming a full target recovery test from host stubs.
required_evidence: final-byte tests execute original drive selection, effective shutter selection, accepted engine dispatch and nonzero rejection across presets, formats, overrides, relocation and shared-reference counts
independent FDE and LSDA parsing identifies original getter call sites and dispatch cleanup, while final private helpers contain no BL or BLR and no additional frame
actual official QString copy instructions retain the immutable borrowed UTF-16 data, and failure arguments preserve live stack objects and canary

the original registered landing-pad instructions release the correct shared references and forward the original exception when an explicit host boundary injects a throw; this is not execution of the C++ personality unwinder
negative instruction mutations bypassing shutter, format, group, global-exposure, failure return site, message layout or reference cleanup must be detected on the final bytes
full Qt signal delivery, all caller recovery, target exception unwinding and actual capture remain separate unverified gates
goals.title: Admission rejection preserves official exception call sites and temporary lifetimes

goals.origin: The actual DropdownSelector uses ListSelectorSettings. Its PropertyData condition filters a row out of DisplayConverter::setModel rather than greying the delegate, while listValues still returns every row value. The delegate has no per-option availability role. Assuming that condition meant disabled, or that a rejecting proxy setter alone fixed QML selection highlighting, would repeat the mismatch between menu appearance and actual behavior.
goals.required_behavior: The four fps values remain immutable and their display order cannot be mistaken for filtered indices. Unimplemented presets are explicitly labelled and cannot generate a configuration write or silently trigger another rate. True disabled rendering must cover both mouse and key acceptance plus local selection/highlight/close behavior; it cannot be claimed from labels, native setter suppression, or backend admission tests alone. The local P14_3 baseline may expose all four labelled options but must report its missing grey-delegate and full Qt interaction gates explicitly.
required_evidence: exact official QML unit identities prove DropdownSelector inherits ListSelectorSettings and identify its setSelected, keyboard, MouseArea, label and color paths
native option-constructor execution checks all four UTF-8 lengths, labels and integer values without modifying keys, conditions or unrelated row fields

final GUI setter execution rejects unavailable values without memory writes, allocation, proxy-cache mutation or DBus transport, while preset one retains the original key, transport result and cleanup
GUI and backend tests bind the same preset one as the admitted baseline, and negative mutations admitting another value or corrupting UTF-8 lengths fail
a full Qt interaction test must separately verify grey rendering, rejected click/key selection, committed highlight and close behavior before claiming the unavailable-option UX complete
goals.title: Unavailable menu options are not confused with hidden rows or backend rejection

goals.origin: The local Qt reference folder was named v6_8_0, but the actual camera QML unit has Qt 6.8.2, data structure version 66 and its own library compile hash. A 6.8.0 host dependency was downloaded before this mismatch was checked; it was not used as runtime proof. The correct 6.8.2 host matches both version and compile hash.
goals.required_behavior: Before executing or editing target QML bytecode, check the unit magic, size, data structure version, exact Qt version and library compile hash against the runtime/compiler. Opcode definitions come from a hash-bound matching reference. Truncated or unknown instructions and invalid branch targets fail closed. Host tests must prove they executed the supplied compiled code, not silently recompiled source or a handwritten behavioral substitute.
required_evidence: target and host cache headers bind exact Qt 6.8.2, version 66 and equal library compile hashes
decoder and assembler tests cover narrow, wide and extended opcodes, forward and backward jumps, bad arity, truncation and invalid targets
host source methods deliberately throw if the modified compiled cache is not loaded
unmodified target bytecode is a failing negative control for the unavailable-option behavior
host model/transport/context substitutions and the absence of a full target GUI run remain explicitly stated
goals.title: QML runtime version and compile identity come from the target unit

goals.origin: ListSelectorSettings itemSelected and color have native AOT entries, while setSelected and the keyboard handler do not. Changing only bytecode leaves native behavior active. The keyboard handler also calls setSelected and closes independently, bypassing an itemSelected-only guard. Nulling a middle AOT function pointer terminates the entire remaining table in the actual Qt loader.
goals.required_behavior: All burst-only acceptance paths reject unavailable row values before index changes, valueSaved, settings writes or close. Row identity is read from the model, not equated to its index. Grey state uses the same availability predicate. Replaced native AOT entries are removed from the active sequence without disabling unrelated compiled functions; the terminator and every moved relocation remain coherent under ASLR. Raw and relocation-resolved CachedQmlUnit pointers must agree. Other menus retain original behavior.
required_evidence: real Qt execution covers mouse entry, direct setter, half-press, accept and joystick keys, external-close behavior, abort, navigation, row reordering and grey color
the final ELF unit is found through its CachedQmlUnit relocation, rather than an obsolete symbol address or intermediate patch
an independent Qt table-walk model verifies exactly the intended AOT removals and unchanged signatures and implementations for all other functions at multiple load biases
every AOT relocation destination is unique, type and addend are preserved, and the moved original terminator is never relocated to a nonzero pointer
negative controls for stale native AOT, early termination and mismatched raw/load-time pointers fail
full target object construction, accepted-write acknowledgement, init recovery, capture, saved-file validity and rollback remain independent release requirements
goals.title: Patched QML selection must actually replace the active AOT and keyboard paths

goals.origin: The unit dump parser read Function +36 as source Location, but Qt 6.8.2 defines nRegisters at +36 and Location at +40. During real-Qt negative testing the first bytecode editor also cleared the line-table count, causing Qt stack-frame lookup to read before the table and report line 458752. That local-only composition was superseded without installation.
goals.required_behavior: Parse source line and column from +40 and preserve the independently decoded register count at +36. Function replacement validates its register budget separately and does not carry stale statement or basic-block PCs into new bytecode. Retain a valid first source-line record at pc zero because Qt stack-frame lookup subtracts one from lower_bound; an empty line table is not safe. Existing reports with the old parser or empty line table are not reused as source-line evidence.
required_evidence: a synthetic mutation varies register count without changing the reported source location and varies Location without changing register count
actual target functions match the pinned Qt function-header layout
new function code is decoded completely and every branch lands on a valid instruction before any composition is accepted
real Qt exception reporting from rewritten functions reports their host wrapper source line instead of reading neighboring header fields
goals.title: QML function source location is not the register count

goals.origin: The September 5 current readout obtained official component identity and storage mounts, then a 2500-line camera-log tail failed to return its completion marker. A later short read timed out and Windows no longer enumerated any camera-vendor USB device. This does not establish why USB disappeared or prove the long read caused it. The first readout also treated an empty settings grep as a completed read without recording the command exit status.
goals.required_behavior: Use small byte-bounded fragments on the diagnostic text tunnel, not large or merely line-limited log dumps. A unique completion marker establishes framing only; preserve the remote query exit status separately, retain incomplete fragments as incomplete, and never infer absent settings or a capture failure from empty or interrupted output. Record exact current USB presence before and after collection, including alternative product ids from the same camera vendor. Full raw-log backups require a separate verified byte-exact transfer and coherent file identity; repeated moving-window pages or decoded fragments are not backups. A disconnect is reported without an invented physical or firmware cause.
required_evidence: every fixed query fits the 232-byte command buffer including distinct status and completion tokens and contains no camera mutation
recent camera-log text is bounded by bytes rather than unbounded line length and is labelled as a fragment
fault injection rejects stale, duplicate, missing, trailing and invalid markers or status while preserving partial evidence
nonzero remote status, empty output and connection timeout cannot become a successful query or a capture diagnosis
current USB enumeration and host timestamps distinguish earlier successful identity from later lost connectivity; local component and source hashes remain bound
actual target collection, full-file integrity and capture-to-file completion remain separate unproved gates until obtained
goals.title: Live text diagnostics are byte-bounded and distinguish framing, command failure and disconnection

goals.origin: The second September 5 live read returned exactly 2048 bytes of log but no actual shell status or terminator while USB remained present. The retained fragment contains camera-test logging the submitted tail command, including the random completion marker. receive_packets matched that marker as an arbitrary substring and stopped before the real status and completion output. The high-level parser also incorrectly counted marker substrings inside logged commands as additional control records.
goals.required_behavior: Receive termination and high-level validation recognize only complete standalone control lines, including a real LF, never marker substrings inside log text or a partial socket chunk. Logged copies of the command, completion token and status format are preserved as payload and cannot count as completed or duplicate control records. Real duplicated or missing control lines still fail closed. Byte bounds remain required even after fixing self-referential markers.
required_evidence: the retained readout_02 fragment is an exact negative control: substring matching finds the token while standalone-line matching finds no terminator
synthetic valid protocol packets cover command echoes, real data, split tokens and seven socket chunk sizes; every data packet is received before the real terminator
unterminated, prefixed, suffixed and quoted tokens do not count, while real LF and CRLF control lines and duplicate real lines are recognized
the high-level reader preserves a logged command containing both status and completion tokens without treating either embedded token as control

a fresh real camera log fragment must include a separate zero exit status and completed terminator before being marked complete; larger decoded fragments remain distinct from byte-exact full-log backups
goals.title: Logged diagnostic commands cannot terminate their own log response

goals.origin: Review of the rebuilt settings-only setter found that it tail-calls the private CameraSettings setter but does not itself refresh CameraObjectImpl's effective-depth cache. The previous P16 proposal added new unprotected calls and patched the common update-depth join, which would also override stock camera-mode 2 and 4 restrictions. The new local route hooks only the actual continuous branch and refreshes via a type-checked tail after the original preset notification.
goals.required_behavior: Changing or restoring the preset must bring the real effective-depth cache and its native notification into agreement before capture admission. The stock mode-2/mode-4 overrides and noncontinuous user settings remain unchanged. Capture rejects a stale or mismatched preset, effective depth, topology group or leaf-shutter state. Any notification tail must preserve sender lifetime, original arguments, canary, caller return and all callee-saved registers, restore its entire original frame, and skip incomplete construction or unrelated object types. No unprotected throwing call or invented successful GUI acknowledgement may substitute for actual target dispatch.
required_evidence: final-byte execution traverses the official preset signal, original activation call site, patched tail and original depth updater across preset, camera-mode, drive, stored depth, current depth and ASLR cases
type mismatch, missing settings and missing FSM do not dereference an unconstructed CameraObjectImpl or invoke its updater
all depth-changing signal and access-control calls remain at original sites, with correct argument and stack layouts and caller restoration
actual settings-to-camera signal delivery, sender ownership during signal dispatch, startup restore and capture-time settings locking are separately proven on target
negative controls using old bytes, lost sender storage, stale-depth admission or wrong-group admission fail without being reported as physical capture tests
goals.title: Preset notification refreshes effective bit depth without overriding other camera modes

goals.origin: The official SingleContinuous graph and group-zero 16-bit topology provide a bounded repeat-session starting point. Routing preset zero to that graph does not implement a new 16-bit HS pipeline or demonstrate 3fps, and the original sensor mode, calibration and 270 descriptor must not be silently changed while establishing a two-frame baseline. The local helper segment also changes program-header mapping and needs independent loader qualification.
goals.required_behavior: Only P16 routes to the stock SingleContinuous sequence and group zero; P14_3 keeps its stock SlowBurst and group eighteen. Unsupported high-rate presets remain rejected. Original constructor options, stop/repeat transitions, sensor topology, calibration, frame ownership and storage components are preserved until separately implemented and verified. The appended helper segment must be nonoverlapping, correctly aligned, executable but nonwritable, ASLR-correct and round-trip reversible, with original note data, relocations and exception call sites retained. An offline routing pass cannot enable the GUI preset, claim achieved fps or authorize an installation.
required_evidence: fresh final-byte execution of the original ready switch proves P16 sequence zero and P14 sequence one, using the original sessionDriveMode getter at its existing call site
new admission executes original engine or original failure dispatch with exact group, depth, shutter and shared-reference cleanup; unsupported presets never alias a supported rate
independent ELF and branch validation checks all appended mappings, modified anchors and ASLR behavior, and exact reversal recovers the parent binary
target loader and complete state-graph execution prove correct start, shutter-hold repeat, release, abort, mode change and late completion behavior
at least two native-leaf P16 exposures produce equal-count valid calibrated 16-bit 3FR files with matching frame identities before GUI availability is enabled
physical cadence and higher-rate scheduling remain separate measured requirements; 270 or 300 configuration values alone cannot satisfy them
goals.title: P16 full-session routing is not evidence of sustained 3fps or valid saved RAW

goals.origin: The first freestanding ownership build used an unsupported Zig linker flag. After removing it, the reproducible binary compiled and decoded successfully but execution tests found that it clobbered x18. Adding clang's fixed-x18 flag alone did not fix the binary: Zig's later negative reserve-x18 target feature overrode the earlier positive flag. Selecting generic+reserve_x18 in the Zig target features corrected the actual output. Failed r1, r2 and r3 local artifacts remain excluded from integration.
goals.required_behavior: Compile using the exact qualified toolchain and supported options, then inspect and execute the actual output. The camera platform register x18, callee-saved registers, stack alignment, caller return and reserved state must be preserved regardless of generic freestanding compiler defaults. A successful compiler exit, a fixed-register command-line flag or a byte-reproducible but wrong binary is not ABI proof. Unknown calls, unresolved symbols, privileged instructions or unexpected target features block integration.
required_evidence: pinned compiler hash and version, full effective target configuration, immutable source and registry hashes, and two byte-identical complete builds
independent final disassembly contains no x18/w18 use, external calls, syscalls or unresolved symbols
actual compiled AArch64 instructions preserve the camera ABI on every tested operation and at multiple load biases
the preserved r2 binary remains a negative control which fails specifically on x18 preservation
unsupported linker flags, overriding target-feature order and corrupt output cannot be reclassified as successful builds or omitted from the recorded review
goals.title: Native ownership code preserves platform ABI, not just generic AArch64 ABI

goals.origin: The older Python ring assumed consecutive FSync ids and a learned RAW offset; later stock evidence disproved both. Its storage-only simplification also cannot stand in for distinct physical buffer release and file-close ownership. The native module therefore uses exact gapped official ids, independent file and buffer terminals, and a nonblocking ownership lock. Review additionally identified impossible persisted COMPLETE slots and initialized CLOSED state as corrupt states, not free capacity.
goals.required_behavior: Reserve bounded request ownership before actuation and bind it once to the exact monotonically increasing official frame id. Do not translate ids or require gaps of one. An actually released RAW buffer may be reused while its older file is still being written, but the older request ticket cannot be freed until both matching file close and matching buffer release arrive. Only unactuated reservations may be cancelled. Contention returns BUSY without consuming an event or altering ownership; integration must retain and retry that immutable event. Unknown or mismatched callbacks quarantine further admission while already owned valid frames drain. New sessions require both exact request drain and separately proven transport quiescence; no timeout fabricates completion.
required_evidence: compiled-machine-code tests run three overlapping gapped frame ids and prove only an exact middle terminal frees one reusable slot
all legal JLS, file-close and buffer-release orderings preserve occupancy until both final terminals, including physical buffer reuse before an older file closes
ring-full, locked, armed-in-flight, stale generation, invalid pointer alignment, input alias, count corruption and duplicate or mismatched callbacks fail without overwriting active slots
stop drains already actuated requests under the old generation and rejects new-generation admission until every exact terminal is present
hundreds of compiled-code cycles remain bounded, preserve the platform ABI and work at multiple load biases without growing seen-id collections

real pre-actuation, FSync, RAW, JLS, file-close, buffer-release and event-retention hooks remain mandatory integration evidence; a standalone module cannot enable 6/9fps or count as physical camera validation
goals.title: Native request ownership joins real terminals and retains events under contention

goals.origin: Independent review of the new r5 native ring against RG-191 found the old mandatory-JLS assumption had returned: CLOSE required HAS_JLS even for the stock compression=false path. Its generic tests passed because they synthesized JLS for every frame. The native implementation now binds compression format before actuation and distinguishes real FullRaw delivery from real JLS completion. The official writer also emits itemProcessed for errors and aborts, so that signal or an object destructor cannot be used as successful file-close evidence.
goals.required_behavior: Record the immutable direct-RAW or JPEG-LS format in each reserved request. Direct-RAW completion requires actual calibrated FullRaw handoff and never waits for or fabricates JLS; JPEG-LS completion cannot pass from FullRaw. Both require destination-specific successful 3FR close and exact original-buffer release. Error, abort, reference decrement, postprocess destruction and timing-entry cleanup are distinct outcomes, not successful close or proof that a physical buffer is free. Historical contracts must be executed against new native modules rather than only checking the registry hash or running self-consistent synthetic examples.
required_evidence: compiled-code tests replay the exact successful stock frame identities and uncompressed path with no JLS event
compiled-code tests cover both compression choices, all legal payload/close/release orderings, out-of-order frame completion and immutable per-request format
negative controls reject cross-format, absent, duplicate and stale payload events and preserve ownership
the retained r5 ELF fails the direct-RAW case and cannot be integrated merely because its earlier available-scope suite passed

target callback mapping independently qualifies concrete source-buffer lifetime, final reference release, destination identity, writer success code, abort status and actual close result before any adapter is connected
goals.title: Native ownership implements the historical format-aware storage contract

goals.origin: The rebuilt GUI retained two private helpers with no FDE coverage: one called QString allocation/destruction for four labels, and the other destroyed an audio-table item then copied a developer-table item and called the native map initializer. This repeated the unprotected-call risk already recorded for backend helpers. The first label replacement anchor also assumed base-helper lengths, overlooking the availability layer's longer unavailable labels; the exact-parent check stopped that local build before output. New local overlays borrow immutable UTF-16 labels and construct a separate native DropDown at the original table-construction call site instead of mutating a live item's ownership after startup.
goals.required_behavior: Every newly reachable private GUI helper must be demonstrably call-free and frame-free or have fully qualified exception unwinding and cleanup. Borrowed QString values use the actual Qt layout and UTF-16 length, retain their immutable mapped lifetime and never leak an old owned allocation. A replacement constructor receives every argument required by its own ABI, not just those of the old constructor. Construct and move the independent burst menu through original native code, restore original map initialization, and preserve all adjacent availability, selection, property and unrelated-menu behavior. Compose against exact prior-layer bytes; never drop unavailable suffixes or overwrite neighboring helpers to make an anchor pass.
required_evidence: execute the actual final original PropertyData constructor and four-copy loop followed by actual QString destruction, including ASLR and preserved keys, values and unavailable labels

goals.origin: The standalone r7 ownership module accepted any nonzero file token supplied at CLOSE, without a prior writer-job binding. Those cleanup functions and the no-error byte alone are not successful destination-specific writes. Independent review of the first local result adapter also found it emitted CLOSE although the original void ShineIoFile close/sync wrappers do not propagate all low-level failures into Result. The adapter now emits a separate WRITE_RESULT and cannot itself free a ticket.

A CLOSE must match the already-bound token; another frame, destination, old job or fabricated token must not free a ticket. Abort status dominates the original 0xff no-error byte, and action, concrete job/cache identity, file type and path must match the owned binding. Never interpret reservation release, fileFlushed, a reply/destructor, a rename attempt or a byte-count log as proof of durable valid 3FR. Original error/abort cleanup must still execute. goals.origin: Whole native execution shows that WaitForBuffersWithAbort suppresses a second query while captureReadyCall is pending, and the completion callable must clear its shared pointer before an exit event. Early exit and duplicate completion with no pending call hit explicit fatal guards. A deliberately invalid replay after another query starts instead consumes the current state's call: the original closure captures STATE, not an immutable notification or generation. This is a negative integration scenario, not evidence that Qt normally duplicates signals or that it caused a historical camera failure. The actual engine uses a thread-pool task and refuses to lock its mutex on the main thread; uninitialized or absent sessions return -1001 and the worker takes a process-exit path, not ordinary capacity=false. Read-only tooling also encountered Windows GBK output failure and an absent .symtab in stripped shooter ELF; neither is camera evidence.

Any new replay, retry, generation or callback adapter must bind completion to its exact original query and owner lifetime, not rely solely on the existing mutable state pointer. Preserve the preceding command's actual exit status before the separator-printing command can replace it, and keep payload, status and completion marker distinct without inventing or deleting payload bytes. A nonzero command result must remain visible even when transport framing completes; the last command's status cannot certify every preceding command in a compound query. Restrict the command set to reviewed bounded read-only operations, retain original failed and successful acquisition artifacts separately, and treat Permission denied, unknown policy and incomplete responses as limitations rather than proof of absence or authorization to mutate the camera.

goals.origin: The separately authorized run-x40kmx2z/HOST_OBSERVER.jsonl retained a validated CNXN command 0x4e584e43, advertised version 0x01000001, maxdata 4096 and payload length 144 before OPEN. AOSP Android 9 commit 0fac9018f2388f25f5a5778663a14712e75a9903 send_connect advertises its maximum version while update_version selects the minimum of the peer and local versions. Retain mandatory packet checksum, framing, AUTH rejection, exact device and shell identity checks, maxdata floor, fixed identity-only command and one-attempt/no-automatic-retry controls. Reject lower, higher and otherwise unknown peer versions, including 0x01000002, and preserve exact rejection diagnostics with accurate accepted-peer and host-version fields. Keep existing live observations and executed sources immutable; local compatibility tests and regenerated sources do not authorize another trial or prove live identity.

goals.origin: The run-p5c96kf0 final staged-script hash read and subsequent worker-lock read failed the host parser on a function 1 candidate after command completion text. The 3944-byte hash response retains a partial final 1024-byte record because the old receiver stopped at the text marker. Pinned camera-test d018fee011426aefef1ded0bd2554ec6f4d31ea0b2529b63f9d5baddc44c42e0 SUTest::ok at ELF 0x56198 preserves the request operation/function and returns 236 zero body bytes. SUTest::error uses body uint32 1 plus zeros. Pinned msg2dbus eb65334f497c12f63e73528973b734e3e79078de885f43f2a0be67ba93080765 SendMessage at 0x51e70 resizes each network record to 1024 bytes; the logical AppsMessage is 260 bytes. Require one unique nonce/RC completion and one successful native terminal result, not the text marker alone.
